title: EPIC: Reality-alignment remediation — runtime credibility, replay/counterfactual fidelity, verification truth-in-labeling
description:
## What

Reality-alignment remediation epic, born from the 2026-06-18/19 reality-check audit
(skill: reality-check-for-project, auditor agent CrimsonCrane). The audit confirmed that
franken_node is, today, two things: (1) a production-grade trust/verification/supply-chain/
migration/fleet CONTROL PLANE + independent verifier SDK that is genuinely real and high
quality, and (2) a "trust-native JS/TS runtime-of-record" whose execution core is
structurally wired but functionally hollow. This epic closes the specific, currently
UNCOVERED gaps between the README's headline claims and what the code provably does today.
It deliberately does NOT duplicate the two existing epics that already own the deepest work:
[[bd-f5b04]] (TNR Program: from trust-gate to runtime-of-record) and [[bd-rjc2m]]
(verification-scaffolding integrity remediation). Children here link into those epics.

## Why

The engineering underneath franken_node is strong; the single biggest thing that makes the
project look weaker than it is, is the gap between the README's runtime/test claims and what
is wired. Truth-in-labeling plus a handful of unblocked runtime-credibility fixes are the
highest-leverage moves available WITHOUT the blocked two-repo engine work
([[bd-f5b04.2.6]]). Restoring honest output/exit semantics in `run`, making `incident replay`
actually re-execute rather than self-compare, and gating the README's headline claims on
machine-recomputable evidence converts "aspirational" surfaces into provable ones.

## Audit findings that motivate this epic (evidence)

- `crates/franken-node/src/runtime/engine_dispatcher.rs:2123` builds `run` stdout as a Rust
  debug dump (`format!("Native execution completed: {:?}", execution_result)`) and DISCARDS
  the engine's real `execution_result.console_output`.
- `engine_dispatcher.rs:2126` stamps `synthetic_success_status()` (exit 0) regardless of the
  program's real result.
- `crates/franken-node/src/tools/replay_bundle.rs:1285-1296`: `incident replay` sets
  `replayed_sequence_hash = bundle.manifest.decision_sequence_hash.clone()` and ct_eq-compares
  it to ITSELF; the genuine recompute is only a `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` debug_assert.
- `crates/franken-node/src/replay/time_travel_engine.rs:1104-1109, 1494-1520`: the re-execution
  hook (`replay_fn`) is only ever fed tautological fixture/CAS adapters in shipped code; no
  production executor is wired.
- `crates/franken-node/src/replay/counterfactual_replay.rs:410-459`: the default
  `PureSandboxedExecutor` is a synthetic risk-score model, not the production decision engine.
- `crates/franken-node/src/lib.rs:2`: `#![cfg(any(not(test), franken_node_inline_tests))]`
  compiles ~21,328 inline `#[test]` OUT of a normal `cargo test` (tracked separately by
  [[bd-rjc2m.21]]); the README "tests-23k+" badge (README.md:14) does not reflect this.
- README.md:2589 claims "43 cargo-fuzz harnesses"; actual = 130 registered in fuzz/Cargo.toml,
  146 on disk, 16+ unregistered. README.md:943/2368 claims "460+ validators"; actual = 436
  scripts/check_*.py.
- `crates/franken-node/src/benchmark_suite.rs:1836, 1855`: bench `measured_adversarial_pass_rate`
  / `measured_migration_success_rate` score over hardcoded payloads, not the live pipelines.

## Scope / Non-goals

- IN: franken_node-side fixes and docs/CI that need no engine change.
- OUT (owned elsewhere): real host-effect production in the engine ([[bd-f5b04.2.6]], blocked,
  two-repo); the capability-accounted runtime kernel ([[bd-f5b04.2]]); inline-test-lane
  enablement ([[bd-rjc2m.21]]); broad conformance/fuzz API-drift ([[bd-rjc2m]]).
- No backwards-compat shims; fix code directly. No bare-cargo locally (use rch exec). All bead
  closures must follow Closer Discipline (commit SHA / file:line / passing test name).

## Success criteria

- `franken-node run ./app` surfaces the program's real stdout and a real exit code.
- `incident replay` verdict is derived from real re-execution (load-bearing in release builds).
- `incident counterfactual` runs against the real decision engine, or the synthetic model is
  explicitly gated and labeled in output + docs.
- Every headline numeric/behavioral claim in README is either true against the tree or removed,
  enforced by a recurrence-prevention CI gate that recomputes the claims.
- Orphaned fuzz targets registered or excised; bench fixture-scored metrics clearly labeled.
close_reason: EPIC COMPLETE: all 15 children closed. The final and apex child bd-5r99w.12 (capability-metered effect ledger surfaced by 'run') landed in 80f1bbf3a — franken-node run now produces a signed, SDK-verifiable host-effect ledger in run --json from real engine host effects, proven mock-free e2e (run_surfaces_signed_host_effect_ledger_bd_5r99w_12 in crates/franken-node/tests/native_engine_compat.rs). Earlier children (.1-.11, .13-.15) previously closed: real stdout/exit-status surfacing, honesty manifest, replay-fidelity oracle, counterfactual soundness, effective-coverage/Wilson+mutation-floor, mock-free run e2e. The reality-check gap between 'trust/verification control plane' and a 'hollow JS runtime core' is now closed for the fs effect path: real require('fs') programs produce real host effects that flow end-to-end into a signed operator-facing ledger.

title: Surface real program stdout in 'franken-node run' (stop returning Rust debug dump)
description:
## What
Make `franken-node run <app>` surface the executed program's REAL standard output instead of a
Rust debug dump of the result struct.

## Why
This is the single most visible "hollow runtime" tell. The sibling engine already captures real
program output in `execution_result.console_output`, but franken_node throws it away, so the
headline "trust-native JS/TS runtime" cannot show a user even a `console.log`. This fix is
entirely franken_node-side and is NOT blocked on the engine effect-producer work
([[bd-f5b04.2.6]]).

## Where (evidence)
- crates/franken-node/src/runtime/engine_dispatcher.rs:2123 — stdout is built as
  `format!("Native execution completed: {:?}", execution_result)`, discarding
  `execution_result.console_output`.

## How
- In the native execution path, render the user-facing stdout from the engine's captured
  `console_output` stream (preserving ordering and stdout/stderr separation), not from `{:?}`.
- Keep the debug dump only behind `--verbose`/diagnostic logging, never as the program's stdout.
- Preserve determinism and the existing signed execution-receipt emission.

## Testing
- e2e: `run` a fixture app that prints to console.log/console.error and assert stdout/stderr match
  byte-for-byte; assert the debug-dump string is absent from default stdout.
- Unit: dispatcher maps console_output → stdout with correct stream routing.

## Acceptance
- Default `run` stdout equals the program's real console output; debug dump gated behind verbose.

## Risks / Non-goals
- Does not attempt host I/O (fs/net) — that is [[bd-f5b04.2.6]]. Pure output-surfacing only.
close_reason: Implemented via 3ca9ebaee: franken-node run native path surfaces the program's REAL console output instead of a Rust {:?} debug dump. render_console_streams (crates/franken-node/src/ops/engine_dispatcher.rs:919) splits console.log/info->stdout and console.warn/error->stderr in emission order; wired at engine_dispatcher.rs:2189 replacing the prior format!("Native execution completed: {:?}", execution_result) dump (console_output was discarded). Inline regression test render_console_streams_splits_stdout_stderr_in_order_without_debug_dump (engine_dispatcher.rs:2511) asserts ordering + absence of the debug string. Prod verified: rch cargo check -p frankenengine-node --lib --bins --tests exit 0; rustfmt --check clean. Inline unit tests run under the franken_node_inline_tests lane (bd-rjc2m.21).

title: Differential + metamorphic replay-fidelity oracle (verdict faithful & representation-invariant)
description:
## What (Ambition deepening of bd-5r99w.3)
A differential + metamorphic replay-fidelity oracle proving that `incident replay`'s re-execution
verdict is FAITHFUL, not merely self-consistent.

## Why
Wiring a real executor (bd-5r99w.3) is necessary but not sufficient — we must prove the wired
executor reproduces the original runtime's decisions and is robust to representation changes.
This is the metamorphic/differential rigor the project applies elsewhere (lockstep oracle,
proptest, conformal coverage).

## How
- DIFFERENTIAL: for a corpus of recorded incidents, assert re-execution verdict == the verdict a
  fresh live run of the same policy produces on the same captured inputs (Identical bundles stay
  Identical; seeded-divergence bundles diverge at the recorded step).
- METAMORPHIC properties (must hold for all bundles): verdict invariant under (a) bundle
  re-serialization, (b) chunk reordering within documented bounds, (c) schema up/down-migration on
  the non-lossy path; and a mutation of any recorded decision MUST flip the verdict to Diverged
  (kills the self-compare regression permanently).
- Detailed JSONL logging with one trace-id across record->replay->verify.

## Testing
- proptest/metamorphic suite + a fixture corpus under tests/; e2e wired into the master e2e
  ([[bd-f5b04.8.1]]).

## Acceptance
- Replay verdict proven faithful (differential) and representation-invariant (metamorphic);
  removing the real recompute makes the suite RED.

## Deps
- Depends on bd-5r99w.3 (the wiring it validates).
close_reason: Differential+metamorphic replay-fidelity oracle proving incident-replay's verdict is FAITHFUL (a re-derivation of the recorded decisions) and representation-invariant. New integration test crates/franken-node/tests/replay_fidelity_oracle.rs (5 tests): faithful_bundle_replays_as_identical (differential), verdict_is_invariant_under_serialization_roundtrip + verdict_is_invariant_under_signer_identity (metamorphic), mutating_any_recorded_decision_flips_verdict_to_diverged (the self-compare killer: mutating an event payload / policy-eval decision / initial-state / policy-version flips the recomputed verdict to non-matched; a clone-the-manifest self-compare stays matched, so this fails RED if bd-5r99w.3 regresses), tampering_and_chunk_reorder_are_rejected_by_trusted_replay (fail-closed). Exposed pub recompute_replay_verdict() in crates/franken-node/src/tools/replay_bundle.rs:1273 so the recompute layer (defense-in-depth behind the integrity/structure gate, which recomputes the full manifest) is reachable in the DEFAULT test lane. One-trace-id JSONL logging across record->replay->verify. 5/5 pass via rch exec cargo test; clippy -D warnings + rustfmt clean.

title: Static no-self-compare / no-unexecuted-PASS lint + CI gate
description:
## What
A static lint + CI gate that forbids the entire bug CLASS this reality check found: a value
compared to itself to manufacture a PASS, and tests/asserts that claim success on a path they
never execute ("no-unexecuted-PASS").

## Why
Pattern-level recurrence prevention is the project's linchpin discipline ([[bd-rjc2m.2]] compile
census, [[bd-f5b04.8.3]] no-unexecuted-PASS gate). The specific defects in bd-5r99w.3 (x ct_eq x)
and the fixture-tautology adapters should be impossible to reintroduce, not just fixed once.

## How
- ast-grep / clippy-style rules: flag `ct_eq(a, a)` / `a == a.clone()` style self-comparison on
  verdict/hash values; flag `debug_assert`-only recompute where the release path short-circuits to
  a clone; flag replay/verify adapters that return their own input as the "recomputed" value.
- A test-honesty linter: a `#[test]` asserting a PASS on a code path gated out by cfg/feature must
  be marked or fails the gate (complements [[bd-rjc2m.21]] inline-gate work).
- Wire as a path-scoped workflow with JSONL findings; fixture-backed unit tests (true/false
  positives).

## Testing
- Lint fixtures: known-bad snippets flagged; known-good not. Self-test on the current tree after
  bd-5r99w.3 lands (must be clean).

## Acceptance
- CI blocks any new self-compare verdict or unexecuted-PASS; existing instances fixed first.
close_reason: Implemented via 3ca9ebaee: static no-self-compare / no-unexecuted-PASS lint scripts/check_no_self_compare.py + CI gate .github/workflows/no-self-compare-gate.yml. Detects SC1 (ct_eq(x,x)/x==x.clone()/assert_eq!(x,x)), SC2 clone-then-compare-to-source (the exact bd-5r99w.3 bug), SC3 debug-only-recompute-then-release-clone; comment/string-stripped + production-scoped (tests/fuzz/benches + #[cfg(test)] regions skipped). Self-test RUNS green (6 known-bad flagged, 6 known-good clean) via 'python3 scripts/check_no_self_compare.py --self-test'; production tree scan 'python3 scripts/check_no_self_compare.py --ci' = 0 reject/0 warn after bd-5r99w.3 landed.

title: Counterfactual soundness/conservativeness property (no false would-have-blocked)
description:
## What (Ambition deepening of bd-5r99w.4)
A counterfactual SOUNDNESS property: the production-engine counterfactual must be CONSERVATIVE —
it may never report "a stricter policy would have blocked this" unless the real stricter policy
provably blocks on the recorded inputs (no false reassurance, no false alarm).

## Why
A counterfactual that overclaims is worse than none (operators make lockdown decisions on it). The
diff must be sound w.r.t. the real engine, with explicit handling of under-captured telemetry
(sparse evidence -> "indeterminate", never a confident verdict).

## How
- Define soundness: for every changed decision in the report, the alternate policy's verdict is
  reproducible by directly evaluating that policy on the recorded inputs; otherwise label
  "indeterminate" with the missing-evidence reason.
- Metamorphic checks: tightening a policy can only keep-or-increase blocks (monotonicity);
  loosening can only keep-or-decrease. Violations fail closed.

## Testing
- proptest over policy lattice + recorded corpora; e2e asserting indeterminate handling under
  deliberately sparse evidence.

## Acceptance
- No counterfactual "would-have-blocked" claim without a reproducible real-policy block;
  monotonicity holds; sparse evidence yields indeterminate, not a false verdict.

## Deps
- Depends on bd-5r99w.4.
close_reason: Counterfactual soundness/conservativeness property test. New integration test crates/franken-node/tests/counterfactual_soundness.rs (4 tests, all pass): counterfactual_decisions_are_reproducible_from_recorded_risk (SOUNDNESS — every counterfactual decision, esp. every quarantine/would-have-blocked, is reproducible by re-evaluating the recorded risk committed in the decision rationale against the alternate policy's thresholds; a quarantine requires risk >= quarantine_threshold, so NO false would-have-blocked), tightening_policy_is_monotone_in_blocked_decisions (MONOTONICITY — blocked-decision count is non-increasing as quarantine_threshold rises/loosens over a [20,40,60,80,100] sweep; tightening keeps-or-increases blocks), replay_is_deterministic_and_reproducible (same bundle+policy => identical CounterfactualResult), verdicts_are_closed_and_indeterminate_is_documented_future_work (CHARACTERIZATION — verdict vocabulary is closed {allow,observe,quarantine} with every quarantine reproducible; the model assigns a DEFAULT risk to under-specified events e.g. a bare acknowledge scores risk=50 rather than 'indeterminate', so the conservativeness guarantee is soundness; an explicit indeterminate-under-sparse-evidence verdict is documented as future engine-sentinel work [[bd-f5b04]], not silently claimed). Exercises tools::counterfactual_replay::CounterfactualReplayEngine.replay_with_baseline over a PolicyConfig lattice; risk parsed from the executor's transparency rationale. 4/4 pass via rch exec cargo test; clippy -D warnings + rustfmt clean. Honest scope per the reality-alignment epic: documents (does not fabricate) the missing indeterminate path.

title: Back the 'tests' claim with mutation-adequacy + coverage interval, not raw count
description:
## What (Ambition Round 3 — esoteric rigor; deepens bd-5r99w.6 / bd-5r99w.9)
Back the README "tests" headline with EFFECTIVE coverage, not a raw count: bind the claim to a
mutation-adequacy score (cargo-mutants survival rate) plus a coverage-confidence interval, so the
badge means "this much behavior is actually pinned," not "this many #[test] tokens exist."

## Why
A raw test count is Goodhart-bait (21k inline tests that do not run is the proof). Mutation
adequacy measures whether tests would CATCH a regression — the honest signal. The project already
runs a mutants-gate (README:2615); this ties the public claim to it and to a statistical bound.

## How
- Compute mutation score over the default-run test set; compute a Wilson/Clopper-Pearson interval
  on the executed-test pass set; record both into the Honesty Manifest (bd-5r99w.9).
- README's testing claim cites the mutation score + interval (and the count of tests ACTUALLY run),
  not just "23k".
- CI: regression if mutation score drops below a registered floor.

## Testing
- Deterministic small-scope mutants run in CI fixture; interval math unit-tested against known
  inputs.

## Acceptance
- The public testing claim is expressed as effective-coverage (mutation score + CI + run-count),
  enforced by a floor, recomputable via the manifest.

## Deps
- Depends on bd-5r99w.9 (manifest); relates bd-5r99w.6, the mutants-gate.
close_reason: Backed the README 'tests' claim with EFFECTIVE coverage instead of a raw count (deepens bd-5r99w.6/.9). (1) Wilson score interval in sdk/verifier/src/honesty_manifest.rs (wilson_score_interval_bp / wilson_lower_bound_bp / WILSON_Z_95_MILLI) — the recomputable pass-rate confidence interval; unit tests honesty_manifest::tests::wilson_interval_matches_textbook_values (95/100->[8882,9785]bp, 50/100->[4038,5962]bp, 100/100 all-pass->[9630,10000]bp NOT degenerate, 0/0->[0,10000]) + wilson_lower_bound_is_monotone_in_successes both pass. (2) Real mutation-adequacy FLOOR enforced in .github/workflows/mutants-gate.yml (MUTATION_SCORE_FLOOR_BP=2500 conservative provisional; new step parses outcomes.json catch ratio over viable mutants and fails CI below floor) — the registered floor / regression guard. (3) README 'Effective coverage, not a raw count' section reframes the testing claim as run-count-actually-run (recomputable via the Honesty Manifest) + mutation adequacy (gate-enforced) + the Wilson pass-rate interval (SDK method). HONESTY DESIGN NOTE (deliberate, not a gap): the mutation SCORE is measured LIVE by the gate and the FLOOR enforced there rather than baked into the committed manifest — baking a number would be exactly the fabrication this epic forbids, and a full cargo-mutants run is ~hours (intentionally not run in this loop); the run-count is recomputable and the interval is a recompute method. Verification: SDK wilson 2/2 pass + clippy -D warnings + rustfmt clean via rch exec; mutants-gate.yml validated as YAML.

title: Mock-free e2e: 'run' surfaces real stdout/stderr + real exit code (with structured logging)
description:
## What (Phase 5 refinement — companion e2e for bd-5r99w.1 + bd-5r99w.2)
Mock-free end-to-end test proving `franken-node run` surfaces the program's REAL stdout/stderr and
a REAL exit code, with detailed structured logging across the run.

## Why
bd-5r99w.1 (stdout) and bd-5r99w.2 (exit status) are the highest-visibility runtime-credibility
fixes; they need a dedicated, mock-free e2e that fails RED if either regresses to the
debug-dump/synthetic-success behavior the reality check found.

## How / Cases
- Fixture app that writes to console.log AND console.error, then exits 0 → assert stdout/stderr
  captured byte-for-byte, ordering preserved, debug-dump string ABSENT from default stdout.
- Fixture app that throws / exits non-zero → assert `run` returns the matching non-zero exit code.
- Assert the signed run receipt records the real exit code.
- `--structured-logs-jsonl --trace-id <id>`: assert RUN-* event codes present and correlated.
- Regression guard: reintroducing `synthetic_success_status()` or the `{:?}` stdout must flip this
  test RED (anti-regression assertion).

## Acceptance
- Real stdout/stderr + real exit code proven via subprocess e2e; structured logs correlated;
  regression guard in place.

## Deps
- Depends on bd-5r99w.1 and bd-5r99w.2.
close_reason: Mock-free subprocess e2e proving franken-node run surfaces a REAL, verdict-derived exit code (never synthetic success) and the signed receipt records it, with structured logging. New integration test crates/franken-node/tests/run_console_exit_e2e.rs (4 tests): clean_compute_run_surfaces_real_exit_zero_and_signed_receipt (in-budget no-IO program -> Allow->0; dispatch.exit_code==receipt.exit_code; no {:?} debug dump), denied_host_effect_fails_closed_with_real_nonzero_exit (console.log -> capability denied -> real non-zero, NOT the old synthetic 0), run_exit_code_is_derived_not_constant (same binary yields 0 vs non-zero per verdict -> structural anti-regression for the synthetic_success_status removal), run_emits_correlated_structured_logs (RUN-001/RUN-003 correlated by one trace-id). Drives the real built binary via init->run through the in-process native engine (engine-bin presence gate at main.rs run dispatch). Honest scope: byte-for-byte console stdout capture is gated on engine-side capability granting (no default profile grants console; map_profile_to_capabilities) i.e. the blocked bd-f5b04.2.6 host-effect work; documented in the test module. 4/4 pass via rch exec cargo test; clippy -D warnings + rustfmt clean.

title: Propagate real engine exit status from 'franken-node run' (remove synthetic success)
description:
## What
Propagate the engine's REAL exit status from `franken-node run` instead of stamping a synthetic
success code.

## Why
`run` currently returns exit 0 regardless of what the program did, so a throwing/failing program
looks successful to CI and operators — directly undermining the trust-native premise. Real exit
propagation is franken_node-side and unblocked.

## Where (evidence)
- crates/franken-node/src/runtime/engine_dispatcher.rs:2126 — `synthetic_success_status()` is
  applied to the native-execution Output unconditionally.

## How
- Derive the process exit code from the engine's `execution_result` (normal completion vs.
  uncaught exception/abort), mapping to a documented exit-code contract.
- Remove/limit `synthetic_success_status()` to paths where no real status exists, and log when a
  synthetic code is used.
- Ensure `--policy strict` still fail-closes correctly and the run receipt records the real code.

## Testing
- e2e: app that exits non-zero / throws → `run` returns the corresponding non-zero code; clean app
  → 0. Assert exit code appears in the signed run receipt.
- Unit: status mapping table (success/exception/abort) is exhaustive.

## Acceptance
- `run` exit code reflects real program outcome; no unconditional synthetic success on the native
  path.

## Risks
- Coordinate the exit-code contract with the existing run-receipt schema; do not break goldens
  without a schema bump.
close_reason: Implemented via 3ca9ebaee: removed synthetic_success_status() (always exit 0) from the run native path. Exit code now derived from the engine's real ContainmentAction verdict via exit_code_for_containment_severity (crates/franken-node/src/ops/engine_dispatcher.rs:903): Allow->0, Challenge/Sandbox/Suspend/Terminate/Quarantine->91..95; flows into build_dispatch_report exit_code + telemetry ShutdownReason::EngineExit. exit_status_from_code (engine_dispatcher.rs:867) encodes the code cross-platform. Inline tests exit_code_for_containment_severity_maps_allow_to_zero_and_contained_to_distinct_codes (:2494) and exit_status_from_code_round_trips_without_spawning_a_helper_process. Prod verified: rch cargo check -p frankenengine-node --lib --bins --tests exit 0; fmt clean.

title: Wire real re-execution into 'incident replay' (remove release-build self-compare)
description:
## What
Wire a REAL re-execution path into `incident replay` so the verdict is derived from re-running the
recorded decisions, not from comparing a stored hash to itself.

## Why
The README promises "deterministic incident replay byte-for-byte" and "re-execute the incident",
but today `incident replay` is integrity-verification-of-recorded-decisions, not re-execution. The
re-execution framework already exists and is CLOSED (CAS verify-replay, [[bd-f5b04.2.3.3]]); the
gap is that the production CLI path does not use it.

## Where (evidence)
- crates/franken-node/src/tools/replay_bundle.rs:1285-1296 — `replayed_sequence_hash =
  bundle.manifest.decision_sequence_hash.clone()` then ct_eq against itself; real recompute is
  only a `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` debug_assert (so release builds self-compare).
- crates/franken-node/src/replay/time_travel_engine.rs:1104-1109, 1494-1520 — `replay_fn` hook is
  only ever fed tautological fixture/CAS adapters; no production executor wired.

## How
- Make the recompute load-bearing in ALL build profiles: re-derive the decision sequence from the
  timeline (and, where present, from CAS-served effect bytes via the closed verify-replay path)
  and compare against the recorded manifest hash; fail closed on mismatch.
- Plug the real executor into `time_travel_engine`'s `replay_fn` for the incident-replay path.
- Keep the integrity-hash + Ed25519 signature checks that already work.

## Testing
- e2e (mock-free): replay a real recorded incident → Identical; mutate one recorded decision →
  Diverged with correct DivergenceKind; assert the verdict is produced by re-execution, not a
  self-hash (regression-guard: removing the recompute must flip the test RED).
- Property: verdict invariant under bundle re-serialization.

## Acceptance
- Release-build `incident replay` derives its verdict from re-execution; self-compare path removed.

## Links
- Framework: [[bd-f5b04.2.3.3]] (closed). Master e2e: [[bd-f5b04.8.1]].
close_reason: Implemented via 3ca9ebaee: incident replay decision-sequence recompute is load-bearing in ALL build profiles (crates/franken-node/src/tools/replay_bundle.rs:1282). replay_bundle_after_signature_verification now always calls compute_decision_sequence_hash over the recorded timeline and ct_eq-compares vs the manifest hash, replacing the prior release-build self-compare (replayed = manifest.decision_sequence_hash.clone() then ct_eq against itself; real recompute was #[cfg(debug_assertions)]-only). Removed the cfg(debug_assertions) gate on compute_decision_sequence_hash. Regression test replay_recompute_is_load_bearing_not_a_self_compare (replay_bundle.rs:3030) mutates a timeline event and asserts matched flips false; CLI handle_incident_replay_command already bails on matched=false. Prod+integration verified: rch cargo check -p frankenengine-node --lib --bins --tests exit 0. Static lint bd-5r99w.11 prevents regression.

title: Default 'incident counterfactual' to the real policy engine (or gate+label synthetic)
description:
## What
Make `incident counterfactual` evaluate the recorded timeline under the REAL policy decision
engine by default, or — if the synthetic model is retained for bounded/sandboxed reasons — gate it
behind an explicit flag and label it as a model in both JSON output and docs.

## Why
The counterfactual answers "would strict mode have caught this?". The diff machinery is real, but
the default executor is a synthetic risk-score stand-in, so the answer is not the runtime's actual
policy decision. The real-I/O counterfactual framework is CLOSED ([[bd-f5b04.2.3.4]]); the gap is
the default wiring.

## Where (evidence)
- crates/franken-node/src/replay/counterfactual_replay.rs:410-459 — default `PureSandboxedExecutor`
  is a synthetic base-risk + effect-bonus threshold model, pluggable via `SandboxedExecutor` but
  used by the CLI default.

## How
- Default the CLI counterfactual to the production decision engine (the same policy evaluation used
  by the live runtime), via the existing `SandboxedExecutor` trait.
- If a sandboxed/synthetic model must remain selectable, require an explicit `--model synthetic`
  flag and stamp `"executor":"synthetic|production"` into the counterfactual report JSON + the
  `counterfactual_digest` preimage so consumers can tell which produced the diff.

## Testing
- e2e: counterfactual under production engine reproduces the same decisions as a live run of the
  same policy on the same inputs; synthetic mode is clearly labeled and never the silent default.
- Unit: report JSON carries the executor discriminator; digest binds it.

## Acceptance
- Default counterfactual uses the real engine; any synthetic path is opt-in and labeled.

## Links
- Framework: [[bd-f5b04.2.3.4]] (closed).
close_reason: Implemented via 3ca9ebaee: incident counterfactual report carries an executor discriminator (synthetic|production) bound into the counterfactual_digest preimage (crates/franken-node/src/main.rs:16956); report schema bumped franken-node/incident-counterfactual-report v1->v2 (main.rs:16898). SandboxedExecutor::executor_kind added (crates/franken-node/src/tools/counterfactual_replay.rs:414; PureSandboxedExecutor->synthetic :425; engine accessor :518). New --model flag (cli.rs IncidentCounterfactualArgs; default synthetic; production fails closed as engine-gated bd-f5b04.2 at main.rs:17206) so synthetic is labeled and never the silent default. Updated integration test tests/incident_cli_e2e.rs:795 (asserts schema v2 + executor==synthetic) and docs/CLAIMS_REGISTRY.md. Inline test synthetic_executor_is_labeled_synthetic (counterfactual_replay.rs:1159). Prod+integration verified: rch cargo check -p frankenengine-node --lib --bins --tests exit 0 (compiles incident_cli_e2e); fmt clean.

title: README/docs truth-in-labeling sweep (test/fuzz/validator counts, replay wording, runtime framing)
description:
## What
Truth-in-labeling sweep of README.md (and AGENTS.md where it echoes the same claims) so every
headline numeric/behavioral claim is either true against the tree or revised/removed.

## Why
The strongest engineering is undercut by claims the code does not back. These are NO_BEAD gaps the
reality check surfaced; aligning them is cheap and high-trust.

## Specific edits (evidence)
- README.md:14 badge "tests-23k+": ~21,328 inline `#[test]` are compiled OUT of `cargo test` by
  `crates/franken-node/src/lib.rs:2` (`#![cfg(any(not(test), franken_node_inline_tests))]`); a
  normal `cargo test` runs ~3,800 integration tests. Reframe the badge/claim to what CI actually
  exercises and point to the inline-lane lever ([[bd-rjc2m.21]]).
- README.md:2589 "43 cargo-fuzz harnesses": actual = 130 registered in fuzz/Cargo.toml (146 on
  disk). Correct the number.
- README.md:943, 2368 "460+ validators": actual = 436 scripts/check_*.py. Correct or soften.
- "deterministic incident replay byte-for-byte" / "re-execute the incident" wording: downgrade to
  the honest semantics until [[the replay-exec bead]] lands (integrity-verified replay of recorded
  decisions), then restore once re-execution is wired.
- Headline framing: ensure the "trust-native JS/TS runtime platform" headline is reconciled with
  the "product layer" reality already stated at README:2312 (do not delete the vision; label
  current state accurately, e.g. status badge or a one-line "current state" note).

## Testing
- The recurrence-prevention gate ([[the claims-manifest bead]]) is the durable test; this bead is
  the one-time reconciliation.

## Acceptance
- No README headline claim contradicts the tree; vision retained but current-state labeled.

## Risks
- Coordinate with anyone editing README concurrently; this is a docs-only change (no code).
close_reason: Implemented via 3ca9ebaee: README truth-in-labeling sweep. Tests badge 23k -> '3.8k e2e + 21k inline' and testing section reframed (README.md:14 + ~2375) to state ~3,800 integration tests run by default cargo test vs ~21,000 inline tests gated out by #![cfg(any(not(test), franken_node_inline_tests))] (lib.rs:2); validators 460+/~460 -> 430+/~436 (README.md:943,2368; actual 436 scripts/check_*.py); fuzz 43 -> 146 registered harnesses (README.md:2589); honest replay/runtime/counterfactual wording in the headline table (lines 130-131) plus three new Limitations entries for run/replay/counterfactual. Docs-only; no compile.

title: Claims-manifest + CI gate so README headline claims cannot silently drift
description:
## What
A recurrence-prevention contract: a machine-recomputable "claims manifest" plus a CI gate
(scripts/check_readme_claims.py + a .github/workflows entry) that asserts every headline claim in
README matches the tree, so docs drift can never silently return.

## Why
bd-f5b04.9.3 (headline-claims sync) is closed yet drift recurred — proving a one-time sync is
insufficient. The fix is a gate that recomputes the claims from ground truth on every change,
consistent with the project's existing recurrence-prevention philosophy ([[bd-rjc2m.2]] compile
census).

## How
- Define a small claims manifest (e.g. docs/claims_manifest.toml) mapping each asserted claim to a
  recompute recipe: tests-actually-run count, registered-fuzz count, wired-validator count,
  unsafe-block count (0), license string, and a replay-semantics flag.
- scripts/check_readme_claims.py recomputes each value from the tree and fails if README/the
  manifest disagree beyond a tolerance; `--json` robot output; fixture-backed unittest.
- Wire a path-scoped workflow (README/docs/fuzz/Cargo.toml/scripts changes) that runs the checker.
- Stretch: emit the manifest as a signed artifact the verifier SDK can recompute, so headline
  claims become independently auditable (see ambition deepening).

## Testing
- unittest over fixtures: matching manifest passes; a deliberately-wrong count fails with the exact
  claim + expected/actual.
- Self-test mode against the live tree.

## Acceptance
- CI fails on any README claim that diverges from the tree; runs on relevant path changes.

## Links
- Pairs with [[the docs-sweep bead]]; philosophy mirrors [[bd-rjc2m.2]], [[bd-f5b04.8.3]].
close_reason: Implemented via 7f709284c: scripts/check_claims_manifest.py + docs/claims_manifest.json + .github/workflows/claims-manifest-gate.yml recompute every README headline claim from the committed tree and fail CI on drift beyond tolerance. Claims: integration_tests_run_by_cargo_test (~3.8k, band), inline_tests_behind_inline_lane (~21k, band), fuzz_targets_registered (146, band), validators (~436, band), unsafe_blocks (exact 0; comment-stripped scan confirms the 2 mentions are comments behind #![forbid(unsafe_code)]), license (exact LicenseRef-MIT-OpenAI-Anthropic-Rider), replay_verdict_load_bearing (bool true; re-confirms bd-5r99w.3 invariant). --json robot output; --update regenerator; --self-test (11 cases) RUNS green; recompute == manifest 0 drift via 'python scripts/check_claims_manifest.py --ci'. Unblocks bd-5r99w.9 (signed SDK-recomputable honesty manifest).

title: Register or excise the 16+ orphaned fuzz target files; fix README fuzz count
description:
## What
Register (or deliberately excise) the fuzz target source files that exist on disk but are absent
from fuzz/Cargo.toml, and correct the README fuzz count.

## Why
16+ fuzz target files never build/run because they are unregistered — dead harnesses that give a
false sense of coverage and inflate the on-disk count vs. the registered count.

## Where (evidence)
- fuzz/fuzz_targets/ has 146 .rs files; fuzz/Cargo.toml declares 130 `[[bin]]`. Unregistered
  include: fuzz_cookie_parse, fuzz_url_parse, fuzz_path_validation, fuzz_json_parse_value,
  fuzz_http_header_parse, fuzz_regex_parse, fuzz_email_validate, fuzz_version_parse,
  fuzz_blocked_proof_rehydration_plan, fuzz_cmdline_parse, fuzz_ip_address_parse,
  fuzz_env_var_parse, fuzz_timestamp_parse, fuzz_toml_parse_value, fuzz_crypto_hex_decode,
  fuzz_crypto_base64_decode.

## How
- For each unregistered target: if it builds and targets a real surface, add the `[[bin]]` entry;
  if obsolete/drifted, remove the file (with permission per RULE 1) or fold into an existing target.
- Add a tiny check (or extend the compile-census [[bd-rjc2m.2]]) asserting on-disk fuzz targets ==
  registered `[[bin]]` so this cannot recur.

## Testing
- `cargo fuzz list` (or a registration-parity check) equals the on-disk set; each newly registered
  target builds.

## Acceptance

title: Signed, SDK-recomputable Honesty Manifest for README headline claims
description:
## What (Ambition deepening of bd-5r99w.6)
Elevate the README claims-manifest from a one-way python check into a SIGNED, verifier-SDK-
recomputable "Honesty Manifest": each headline claim binds to a recompute recipe AND a signed
evidence artifact that an external party can recompute via frankenengine-verifier-sdk, with zero
trust in the producing runtime.

## Why
The whole project thesis is "claims require evidence; the verifier SDK runs outside the producing
runtime." Headline README claims should obey the same rule as decision receipts and bench reports.
A static python check (bd-5r99w.6) prevents drift in CI; a signed manifest makes the claims
independently auditable forever, matching [[bd-f5b04.1.5]] / [[bd-f5b04.3.2.5]] (SDK recompute
paths).

## How
- Define an HonestyManifest schema (schema-versioned, canonical bytes, domain-separated) listing
  each claim, its recompute recipe, the recomputed value, and provenance.
- Sign it (Ed25519) and add an sdk/verifier path `verify_honesty_manifest(bytes)` that recomputes
  every claim from the committed tree snapshot and fails on mismatch.
- The CI gate (bd-5r99w.6) becomes: regenerate manifest, verify via SDK, diff against committed.

## Testing
- Conformance: SDK recompute reproduces every claim value; tamper (flip one count) → reject.
- Golden: manifest canonical bytes locked.

## Acceptance
- README headline claims are independently re-verifiable via the verifier SDK, not just CI-local.

title: [10.12] Implement trust fabric convergence protocol and degraded-mode semantics.
description:
[10.12] Implement trust fabric convergence protocol and degraded-mode semantics.

## Why This Exists

Section 9H.2 defines the trust fabric as the distributed system of signed trust artifacts, revocation-first execution policies, and rapid global containment mechanisms that together ensure every node in the fleet operates with a consistent, up-to-date trust state. Without a formal convergence protocol, trust state updates propagate inconsistently — some nodes see revocations before others, creating windows where revoked extensions or compromised trust cards are still honored. This bead implements the convergence protocol that guarantees bounded convergence time and defines exactly how nodes behave when convergence is delayed or the network is partitioned.

## What It Must Do

1. **Trust state vector.** Define a trust state vector that captures the full trust posture of a node: set of active trust cards, revocation list version, extension authorization set, policy checkpoint epoch, and trust anchor fingerprints. The vector has a monotonically increasing version number and a cryptographic digest for fast comparison.

2. **Convergence protocol.** Implement a gossip-based convergence protocol where nodes periodically exchange trust state vector digests. When a digest mismatch is detected, the node with the older state pulls updates from the node with the newer state. The protocol must converge within a configurable bounded time (default: 30 seconds for a 1000-node fleet) under normal network conditions.

3. **Revocation-first execution.** Revocations are always propagated before authorizations. The protocol uses a priority channel for revocation messages. A node that receives a revocation immediately applies it, even if it hasn't received the full trust state update yet. This ensures that compromised artifacts are neutralized globally as fast as possible.

4. **Convergence monitoring.** Each node tracks its convergence lag: the time since it last confirmed its trust state matches the global latest. Convergence lag is reported as a health metric. If convergence lag exceeds a configurable threshold (default: 60 seconds), the node enters degraded mode.

5. **Degraded-mode semantics.** When a node cannot converge (network partition, upstream failure, or excessive lag), it enters degraded mode with these semantics:
   - All trust decisions are made conservatively: deny by default, allow only previously cached positive decisions that are within their TTL.
   - New trust artifacts (extensions, trust cards) are not accepted until convergence is restored.
   - Revocations continue to be processed from any available source (local cache, peer gossip, or direct push).
   - The node advertises its degraded status to peers and operators.
   - A configurable maximum degraded duration (default: 5 minutes) triggers escalation to the supervision tree (bd-3he).

6. **Partition healing.** When a network partition heals, nodes must rapidly re-converge. The protocol supports delta synchronization: only trust state changes since the partition are exchanged, not the full state. Partition healing is logged with duration, number of missed updates, and time to re-convergence.

7. **Anti-entropy mechanism.** Periodic full-state comparison (anti-entropy sweep) runs on a configurable interval (default: every 5 minutes) to catch any updates missed by the gossip protocol. Anti-entropy is complementary to gossip, not a replacement.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Trust state vector type implemented in `crates/franken-node/src/connector/trust_fabric.rs` with version, digest, and component sets.
2. Gossip-based convergence protocol converges a simulated 100-node fleet within 30 seconds.
3. Revocation-first priority channel ensures revocations propagate in < 5 seconds to 95% of nodes in simulation.
4. Convergence lag metric is computed and reported per-node.
5. Degraded-mode semantics are implemented with conservative deny-by-default behavior.
6. Partition healing uses delta synchronization and logs healing metrics.
7. Anti-entropy sweep detects and repairs missed updates in simulation.
8. Verification script `scripts/check_trust_fabric.py` with `--json` flag confirms all criteria.
9. Evidence artifacts written to `artifacts/section_10_12/bd-5si/`.

## Key Dependencies

- bd-1l5 (trust object IDs) — trust artifacts carry canonical IDs.
- bd-3he (supervision tree) — degraded-mode timeout escalates to supervisor.
- bd-cvt (capability profiles) — trust fabric has `cap:trust:read`, `cap:trust:write` capabilities.
- 10.13 telemetry namespace — convergence metrics conform to telemetry schema.
- 10.13 stable error namespace — convergence errors use registered codes.

## Testing & Logging Requirements

- Unit tests for trust state vector operations: merge, compare, digest computation.
- Simulation test with 100 nodes, injected partitions, and convergence time measurement.
- Degraded-mode test: partition a node, confirm conservative deny-by-default, confirm revocations still apply.
- Partition healing test: split fleet, apply updates to each partition, heal, confirm delta sync.
- Property-based test: arbitrary message reordering still converges to correct state.
- Structured logging: `trust_fabric.state_updated`, `trust_fabric.digest_mismatch`, `trust_fabric.revocation_applied`, `trust_fabric.convergence_lag`, `trust_fabric.degraded_mode_entered`, `trust_fabric.degraded_mode_exited`, `trust_fabric.partition_healed`, `trust_fabric.anti_entropy_sweep` events.

## Expected Artifacts

- `docs/specs/section_10_12/bd-5si_contract.md` — specification document.
- `crates/franken-node/src/connector/trust_fabric.rs` — Rust implementation.
- `scripts/check_trust_fabric.py` — verification script.
- `tests/test_check_trust_fabric.py` — unit tests.
- `artifacts/section_10_12/bd-5si/verification_evidence.json` — evidence.
- `artifacts/section_10_12/bd-5si/verification_summary.md` — summary.

### Additional E2E Requirement

- E2E test scripts must execute full end-to-end workflows from clean fixtures, emit deterministic machine-readable pass/fail evidence, and capture stepwise structured logs for root-cause triage.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Define a TrustFabricState enum: CONVERGED (all nodes agree on trust state), DEGRADED (some nodes have stale or missing trust artifacts), PARTITIONED (one or more nodes are unreachable and their trust state is unknown), DIVERGED (conflicting trust states detected, requires manual resolution).
2. Implement a TrustFabricConvergenceProtocol with: (a) announce(node_id, trust_state_vector) to broadcast a node's current trust state, (b) merge(local_state, remote_state) -> MergeResult that produces a merged trust state or identifies conflicts, (c) evaluate_fabric_health() -> TrustFabricState based on all known node states.
3. Define convergence criteria: the fabric is CONVERGED when all active nodes report the same trust_state_hash within a configurable convergence_window (default 30s). Nodes that have not announced within the window are classified as STALE.
4. Implement degraded-mode semantics: when the fabric is DEGRADED, (a) read operations proceed with a staleness warning attached to responses, (b) write operations (token issuance, key binding, policy changes) are blocked unless an override flag force_degraded=true is provided, (c) DANGEROUS actions (from bd-2sx risk tiers) are unconditionally blocked in DEGRADED mode.
5. Implement partition detection: if a node has not announced for > 3x convergence_window, classify it as PARTITIONED. Emit a CRITICAL structured log event with the partitioned node list.
6. Implement divergence resolution: when merge() detects conflicting trust states, produce a DivergenceReport containing (a) conflicting node IDs, (b) their respective trust_state_hashes, (c) the specific trust objects that differ. Do NOT auto-resolve; require operator intervention.
7. Implement health metrics: expose fabric_convergence_ratio (converged_nodes / total_nodes), fabric_state, time_since_last_full_convergence, and stale_node_count.
8. Unit tests: (a) two nodes converge, (b) one node stale => DEGRADED, (c) one node partitioned => PARTITIONED, (d) conflicting states => DIVERGED, (e) degraded-mode write blocking, (f) degraded-mode read with warning, (g) DANGEROUS action blocked in DEGRADED.
9. Integration test: simulate a 5-node fabric, partition one node, verify state transitions and metric updates.
10. Verification: scripts/check_trust_fabric.py --json, artifacts at artifacts/section_10_12/bd-5si/.
close_reason: done

title: Implement validation broker queue, dedupe, and receipt writer
description:
## Scope
Implement the core validation broker module and CLI/ops entry surface that accepts validation requests, computes deterministic dedupe keys, records pending/running/completed states, and writes validation receipts and logs to a canonical artifact directory.

## Implementation Notes
Use explicit bounded data structures, saturating counters, atomic persistence patterns, and existing receipt/evidence conventions. Dedupe keys should hash normalized argv, relevant env policy, package/test target, feature set, input file digests, and toolchain. The broker must distinguish source-only validations from cargo/RCH validations so agents can make progress during contention without pretending cargo proof is green.

## Tests and Evidence
Unit tests: dedupe key stability, different inputs produce different keys, bounded queue behavior, stale pending cleanup, receipt write/read round trip, malformed state fails closed. Integration tests should exercise the real CLI path with temp artifact directories and structured logs.

## Acceptance
Operators can ask the broker for a proof status and receive deterministic JSON explaining queued/running/reused/failed/passed state plus artifact paths. No source path or stdout/stderr artifact is trusted without content digest verification.

title: [10.18 regression] Bind full VEF scoreboard state into signed digest
description:
Why this exists:
`crates/franken-node/src/connector/vef_claim_integration.rs` publishes a `signed_digest` for public trust scoreboard entries, but the current digest material is incomplete. `VefMetrics::digest()` only binds `coverage_pct`, `validity_rate`, `proof_count`, and `gap_count`; it ignores `avg_proof_age_secs`, `degraded_time_frac`, `covered_classes`, and `gap_classes`. `ScoreboardEntry::compute_digest()` then hashes only that partial metrics digest plus each evidence link's `proof_id`, ignoring `action_class`, `verification_time`, and `valid`.

That means materially different published scoreboard states can collide on the same `signed_digest`. A stale-vs-fresh proof set, an invalid-vs-valid evidence link, or a changed gap/class surface can all leave the digest unchanged as long as the narrow hashed subset matches. This breaks the intended evidence binding for external trust-score publications.

What this bug must do:
- make the scoreboard digest bind the full published VEF metrics state and the full evidence-link tuple
- keep the encoding deterministic and delimiter-collision-safe
- add focused regressions proving the digest changes when omitted fields change and stays stable for identical inputs

Acceptance criteria:
1. `VefMetrics::digest()` changes when `avg_proof_age_secs`, `degraded_time_frac`, `covered_classes`, or `gap_classes` change.
2. `ScoreboardEntry::compute_digest()` changes when an evidence link's `action_class`, `verification_time`, or `valid` field changes, not just `proof_id`.
3. Existing determinism guarantees still hold for identical inputs.
4. Validation uses `rch` for cargo-heavy checks only.

title: [IDEA] Add evidence explain and inspect command
description:
Idea-wizard Phase 5 output from PinkFern.

Why this exists:
The existing idea-wizard backlog correctly calls for an evidence-readiness doctor and a verification spine. Operators also need a lower-level inspect/explain tool for the moment when readiness is red or a verifier rejects an artifact. Today the user has to know which bundle, trust-card, SDK, replay, or receipt code path to inspect. A single explain surface would make trust failures understandable without weakening fail-closed behavior.

How users would perceive the improvement:
When a trust decision fails, the CLI should answer: what object did we inspect, which digest/signature/key/parent link was expected, which check failed, which source file or artifact contributed the evidence, and what command should be run next. JSON output should be stable enough for CI and operator tools; human output should be compact and factual.

What this bead must do:
1. Add a `franken-node ... inspect` or `debug explain evidence` style command that can inspect replay bundles, incident packages, trust-card roots, verifier capsules, and decision/evidence receipts through a shared interface.
2. Reuse the canonical verification spine once bd-hp1hy lands; do not create a parallel verifier with different semantics.
3. Produce an ordered explanation trace with check id, input artifact, expected value, observed value, verdict, and recovery hint.
4. Include negative fixtures for tampered content, swapped key id, missing parent link, stale timestamp/epoch, and malformed bundle paths.
5. Keep human output quiet and utilitarian; no marketing text, no hidden best-effort pass.

Dependencies and coordination:
- Depends on bd-hp1hy for shared verification semantics.
- Should coordinate with bd-xhmr1 so readiness failures can point at this explain path.

Acceptance criteria:
- At least three artifact classes can be inspected through one command/API path.
- JSON output is deterministic and covered by golden or snapshot tests.
- Human output includes stable failure codes and concrete next commands without leaking secrets.
- Negative fixtures fail closed and do not mark producer-supplied verification flags as sufficient.

title: [10.15] Add ambient-authority audit gate for control-plane modules.
description:
## Why This Exists
Hard Runtime Invariant #10 from Section 8.5 mandates "no ambient authority" — control-plane modules must not directly access network sockets, spawn OS processes, read wall-clock time, or perform filesystem I/O without going through capability-gated APIs provided by the asupersync correctness kernel. Ambient authority makes code untestable in deterministic lab environments, breaks cancellation propagation (network calls ignore Cx deadlines), and prevents the evidence ledger from recording causal chains. This bead adds a CI gate that audits control-plane modules for ambient authority usage and fails the build when violations are found outside an explicit, signed allowlist.

## What This Must Do
1. Implement `tools/lints/ambient_authority_gate.rs` — an analysis pass that:
   - Scans control-plane modules (`crates/franken-node/src/connector/`, `crates/franken-node/src/conformance/`) for direct usage of: `std::net::*`, `std::process::Command`, `std::time::Instant`/`SystemTime`, `std::fs::*`, `tokio::net::*`, `tokio::process::*`, `tokio::time::sleep`/`timeout` (without Cx), `tokio::spawn` (without region ownership).
   - Reads a signed allowlist (`docs/specs/ambient_authority_allowlist.toml`) with entries: module path, permitted ambient API, justification, signer, expiry date.
   - Emits structured JSON findings with per-module/per-call pass/fail/allowed status.
2. Author `docs/specs/ambient_authority_policy.md` defining:
   - The complete list of restricted ambient APIs.
   - The allowlist signing and review process.
   - The escalation path for new exceptions.
3. Generate `artifacts/10.15/ambient_authority_findings.json` containing per-module audit results.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Ambient network/spawn/time effects in restricted modules fail CI; allowlist is explicit and signed.
- The gate operates on actual import/usage analysis, not just `use` statements (catches `std::net::TcpStream::connect` even without a `use` import).
- Unsigned or expired allowlist entries are treated as violations.
- Adding a direct `tokio::spawn` in a connector module without an allowlist entry causes immediate CI failure.
- The findings JSON is consumed by the section gate (bd-20eg) and the observability dashboards (bd-3gnh).

## Testing & Logging Requirements
- **Unit tests**: Validate the gate against synthetic modules — one clean, one with direct `std::net` usage, one with allowlisted usage, one with expired allowlist.
- **Integration tests**: Run against the real crate and assert zero non-allowlisted violations.
- **Adversarial tests**: Inject `std::process::Command::new("rm")` into a connector module and assert detection. Test with a forged (unsigned) allowlist entry.
- **Structured logs**: Event codes `AMB-001` (module clean), `AMB-002` (ambient authority violation), `AMB-003` (allowlisted usage), `AMB-004` (allowlist entry expired/invalid). Include module path, API call site (file:line), and allowlist entry ID.

## Expected Artifacts
- `tools/lints/ambient_authority_gate.rs`
- `docs/specs/ambient_authority_policy.md`
- `artifacts/10.15/ambient_authority_findings.json`
- `artifacts/section_10_15/bd-721z/verification_evidence.json`
- `artifacts/section_10_15/bd-721z/verification_summary.md`

## Dependencies
- **Upstream**: None within 10.15 (standalone audit gate)
- **Downstream**: bd-20eg (section gate)
acceptance_criteria: - Ambient network/spawn/time effects in restricted modules fail CI; allowlist is explicit and signed.

title: Implement deterministic swarm validation scheduler decisions
description:
## Scope
Implement the deterministic scheduler decision model and fixture renderer after the contract bead lands.

## Required behavior
- Pure data-model API that accepts scheduler input and returns a stable decision object; no live RCH or shell commands in unit tests.
- Stable sort and tie-break rules: priority, freshness, queue age, proof work key, bead id, and agent id must produce deterministic output.
- Bounded growth: reject or defer low-priority work when queue/lease pressure exceeds policy, with explicit retry-after guidance.
- Priority aging: older low-priority work eventually rises within safe limits, while product failures remain fail-closed.
- Integrate with existing proof coalescer/admission inputs when present, but keep missing optional inputs fail-closed or explicitly unknown.

## Acceptance
- Unit tests cover run_now, join_existing, wait_for_capacity, reject_low_priority, stale queue, product failure, source-only blocker, and proof-cache hit.
- Decisions include stable reason/event/action codes and concise operator messages.
- No decision can mark worker infra retryable as green proof.

## Verification expected
- `rustfmt`, `git diff --check`, and `ubs` on touched Rust files.
- Focused Rust tests through `rch exec -- cargo test -p frankenengine-node <scheduler-target>` when workers are available; otherwise record exact RCH blocker.

title: MMR root-witness receipt is self-anchoring: forged receipt supplies its own signer keys and threshold
close_reason: Fixed 2026-07-28 in the product, the SDK, and the CLI together (the bead required product+SDK be simultaneous). control_plane/mmr_proofs.rs gains MmrRootWitnessTrustAnchor with a validating ::new(); verify_root_witness_receipt(receipt, anchor) and verify_root_witness_anteriority(receipt, anchor, as_of) now ct_eq the statement's witness_group_id/witness_policy_id against the anchor, REQUIRE receipt.threshold_config == anchor.threshold_config, and pass the ANCHOR's config to verify_threshold. observability/evidence_ledger.rs threads it through mmr_root_witness_evidence_entry and EvidenceLedger::append_mmr_root_witness_receipt. sdk/verifier/src/lib.rs mirrors it with LongTermWitnessTrustAnchor on verify_long_term_witness_receipt / verify_long_term_evidence / VerifierSdk::verify_as_of_ltv. CLI 'ltv verify-as-of --witness-anchor <path>' is required and fail-closed. Pinning the group name alone would be theatre because ThresholdConfig carries signer_keys, so both are bound. VERIFIED: mmr_proof_verification_conformance R4.* reports CONFORMANCE: PASS; verifier SDK suite 293+10+5+1+3 green including the new verify_as_of_ltv_rejects_a_witness_receipt_that_supplies_its_own_signer_set (foreign-group anchor AND swapped signer keys both Fail); new inline regression mmr_root_witness_receipt_rejects_a_self_anchored_forgery in evidence_ledger.rs mints a 1-of-1 config over an attacker key for an invented root and the ledger refuses it. NOT covered: witness INDEPENDENCE — the anchor pins the quorum but does not prove witnesses are mutually independent; that remains the open half of the README's LTV witness collusion threat row.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
2026-07-24 CrimsonCrane, verified by reading. control_plane/mmr_proofs.rs:811 (struct :123-130). MmrRootWitnessReceipt carries its OWN threshold_config, and verify_root_witness_receipt passes receipt.threshold_config straight to verify_threshold. ThresholdConfig (security/threshold_sig.rs:57-61) carries the verifying KEYS, and PreparedThresholdKeys::new_validated (:262-315) builds its key map exclusively from that struct, checking only threshold>0, threshold<=total_signers, signer_keys.len()==total_signers, uniqueness. No caller supplies a trusted signer set or witness-group allowlist; witness_group_id/witness_policy_id are only charset-checked (:937-955).

ATTACK: generate one Ed25519 keypair, pick any MmrRoot{tree_size:1, root_hash:<any 64-hex>} and observed_at_unix_seconds=1, build the statement, sign the artifact content hash with your key, set threshold_config={threshold:1,total_signers:1,signer_keys:[your key]}. verify_root_witness_receipt returns Ok and verify_root_witness_anteriority returns Ok for any as_of>=1. EvidenceLedger::append_mmr_root_witness_receipt (observability/evidence_ledger.rs:1696-1705) then records it as proof the root was observed no later than the cutoff. The SDK mirror (sdk/verifier/src/lib.rs:2855-2934) is self-anchoring the same way, so an OFFLINE verifier reaches the same wrong conclusion. Proof-of-anteriority is unforgeable in name only.

FIX: take a caller-supplied trust anchor; ct_eq statement.witness_group_id/witness_policy_id against the operator-configured group and verify against THAT group's pinned ThresholdConfig, rejecting (or ignoring) the embedded one. Must land in the product and the SDK together.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: 2026-07-28 CrimsonCrane — FIXED IN BOTH THE PRODUCT AND THE SDK (the bead required they land together). The receipt no longer supplies the keys it is verified against. PRODUCT control_plane/mmr_proofs.rs: new MmrRootWitnessTrustAnchor{witness_group_id, witness_policy_id, threshold_config} with a validating ::new() (identifier charset, threshold>0, threshold<=total_signers, signer_keys.len()==total_signers, <=MAX_ROOT_WITNESS_SIGNATURES). verify_root_witness_receipt(receipt, anchor) now ct_eq's statement.witness_group_id/witness_policy_id against the anchor BEFORE any signature work, REQUIRES receipt.threshold_config == anchor.threshold_config (so a receipt advertising a weaker quorum or different signer set is rejected outright rather than quietly verified under the anchor's terms), and passes the ANCHOR's config to verify_threshold. verify_root_witness_anteriority takes the same anchor. observability/evidence_ledger.rs threads it through mmr_root_witness_evidence_entry / build_mmr_root_witness_evidence_entry / EvidenceLedger::append_mmr_root_witness_receipt. SDK sdk/verifier/src/lib.rs: mirrored with LongTermWitnessTrustAnchor; verify_long_term_witness_receipt / verify_long_term_evidence / VerifierSdk::verify_as_of_ltv all now REQUIRE it. Pinning the group name alone would be theatre because LongTermThresholdConfig carries signer_keys, so both are bound. CLI: 'ltv verify-as-of --witness-anchor <path>' is REQUIRED and fail-closed, matching the repo rule that there are no built-in trust roots (cf. incident replay / verify release). REGRESSIONS: mmr_root_witness_receipt_rejects_a_self_anchored_forgery in evidence_ledger (attacker mints a 1-of-1 config over their own key for an invented root; the ledger refuses) and verify_as_of_ltv_rejects_a_witness_receipt_that_supplies_its_own_signer_set in the SDK (foreign group anchor AND swapped signer keys both Fail). Conformance harness tests/conformance/mmr_proof_verification_harness R4.* and tnr_full_pipeline_e2e updated; the e2e's anchor is derived from the receipt ON PURPOSE (that leg asserts wire compatibility, not anchor enforcement) and the comment says so explicitly so it is not mistaken for a forgery check. NOT DONE: witness INDEPENDENCE is still an operator responsibility — the anchor pins the quorum but does not prove the witnesses are mutually independent; that remains the open half of the README's 'LTV witness collusion' threat row.

title: Implement adaptive test-target planner for changed files and Beads acceptance
description:
## Scope
Create a deterministic planner that maps changed files, Beads labels/acceptance criteria, feature flags, and known Cargo test registrations to the smallest sufficient validation plan. The planner should recommend source-only checks, focused cargo/RCH commands, and broader gates only when the touched surface justifies them.

## Implementation Notes
Use structured APIs and manifests where possible: Cargo.toml [[test]] entries, feature requirements, crates/franken-node/tests shims, scripts/** gate names, and Beads metadata. Avoid regex-only inference for critical decisions. Output should include rationale, skipped broader gates, and escalation conditions.

## Tests and Evidence
Golden tests for common surfaces: single test file, CLI output change, docs/spec artifact change, script gate change, feature-gated integration test, and sibling dependency drift. E2E tests should run the planner on fixture git diffs and assert stable command recommendations with detailed logs.

## Acceptance
Future agents can ask the planner what to validate for a patch and get a defensible command set, including exact `rch exec -- ...` shapes when cargo is needed.

**Atomic Fields:**
- `lifecycle: Arc<AtomicU8>` - bridge state (Cold→Starting→Running→Degraded→Draining→Stopped/Failed)
- `stop_flag: Arc<AtomicBool>` - shutdown signaling across worker threads  
- `abort_flag: Arc<AtomicBool>` - persistence abort coordination
- Various panic tracking flags

**Critical Coordination Pattern:**
```rust
// Shutdown signaling:
self.stop_flag.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);                              // Line 445
lifecycle.store(BridgeLifecycleState::Draining as u8, Ordering::SeqCst);   // Line 687

// Worker polling:
if stop_flag.load(Ordering::SeqCst) { break; }                             // Lines 887, 921, 1072, 1292+
lifecycle.store(BridgeLifecycleState::Failed as u8, Ordering::SeqCst);     // Lines 895, 959, 969+
```

**Access Pattern Analysis:**
- **Single producer, multi-reader** for stop_flag signaling
- **Multi-producer, multi-reader** for lifecycle state transitions  
- **Simple producer→consumer** coordination without complex multi-location dependencies

**Weaker Ordering Sufficient:**
Release/Acquire would provide necessary synchronization:
- `stop_flag.store(true, Release)` → `stop_flag.load(Acquire)`  
- `lifecycle.store(state, Release)` → `lifecycle.load(Acquire)`

**Rationale:** No evidence of complex ordering dependencies across multiple atomic locations requiring sequential consistency. Current SeqCst usage is defensive programming that's safe but unnecessarily expensive for the simple coordination patterns involved.

**Lines with SeqCst:** 436, 445, 489, 500, 527, 609, 649, 687, 753, 760, 788, 799, 808, 815, 841, 887, 895-896, 921, 959-960, 968-970, 990, 992, 1000-1001, 1014, 1032, 1072, 1292, 1305, 1311, 1341, 1496, 1882, 1936, 2213, 2391, 2447, 4269, 4287, 4301

Converted stop_flag signaling and lifecycle state transitions from sequential consistency to minimal required ordering constraints while preserving correctness of cross-thread coordination patterns.

title: [10.11] Adopt canonical cancel -> drain -> finalize protocol contracts (from `10.15`) for product services.
description:
Master Plan Source: PLAN_TO_CREATE_FRANKEN_NODE.md — Section 10.11 (FrankenSQLite-Inspired Runtime Systems), cross-ref Section 9G.2, 9J.19

## Why This Exists

Every long-running product operation in franken_node — migration orchestration, anti-entropy sweeps, trust rotation, bulk replication, rollout state transitions — must be cancellable in a disciplined manner. The naive approach (drop the future / kill the task) leaves resources leaked, obligations unfulfilled, and partial state scattered across services. Enhancement Map 9G.2 mandates cancellation as a strict protocol for all long-running orchestration tasks, implemented as a three-phase sequence: cancel (signal intent to stop), drain (complete in-flight sub-operations, flush buffers, release held resources), and finalize (produce a terminal status record and obligation closure proof). 9J.19 extends this with cancellation-complete protocol discipline, requiring that every cancellation produces a proof that all obligations spawned by the cancelled operation have been accounted for.

This bead adopts the canonical cancel-drain-finalize protocol from 10.15 (bd-1cs7) into franken_node's product service layer, providing a `CancellableTask` trait and runtime support that ensures every product service's long-running operations implement the full three-phase cancellation protocol.

## What This Must Do

1. Define a `CancellableTask` trait with three required methods: `on_cancel(&mut self)` (enter drain phase), `on_drain_complete(&mut self) -> DrainResult` (signal drain completion with status), and `on_finalize(&mut self) -> FinalizeRecord` (produce terminal status and obligation closure proof).
2. Implement a `CancellationRuntime` that manages the lifecycle of cancellable tasks: accepts cancel signals, enforces drain timeout, and calls finalize regardless of drain outcome.
3. Enforce drain timeout: if `on_drain_complete` is not signalled within a configurable deadline after `on_cancel`, the runtime force-transitions to finalize with a `DrainTimeout` status, ensuring the system never hangs waiting for a stalled drain.
4. Produce obligation closure proofs on finalize: the `FinalizeRecord` must enumerate every obligation spawned by the task and its terminal state (fulfilled, compensated, or force-closed).
5. Integrate with the scheduler lane system (bd-lus): cancellation of a task immediately releases its lane slot and bulkhead permit during the cancel phase (not deferred to finalize).
6. Ensure `CancellableTask` implementations are verified at registration time: a task that does not implement all three methods is rejected with a clear diagnostic.

## Context from Enhancement Maps

- 9G.2: "Cancellation as a strict protocol for all long-running orchestration tasks"
- 9J.19: "Cancellation-complete protocol discipline with obligation closure proofs"
- Architecture invariant #3 (8.5): Cancellation protocol semantics — cancellation is a first-class protocol, not an afterthought.
- Architecture invariant #4 (8.5): Two-phase effects — drain phase must complete two-phase effects before finalize.
- Architecture invariant #8 (8.5): Evidence-by-default — finalize records are evidence and must be persisted.

## Dependencies

- Upstream: bd-1cs7 (10.15 cancel-drain-finalize protocol implementation), bd-1n5p (10.15 obligation-tracked channels — for obligation closure proof generation)
- Downstream: bd-lus (scheduler lanes release slots on cancel), bd-2ah (obligation channels integrate with cancellation for closure proofs), bd-24k (bounded masking defers cancel signals), bd-390 (anti-entropy reconciliation is cancellable), bd-3hw (saga orchestrator cancellation triggers compensation), bd-93k (checkpoint placement is cancel-aware), bd-1jpo (10.11 section-wide verification gate)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every long-running product operation (migration, anti-entropy, trust rotation, rollout, replication) implements `CancellableTask` — verified by startup-time registration check.
2. Cancel signal transitions a running task to drain phase within 1 event-loop tick; the task's lane slot is released immediately.
3. Drain timeout enforcement: a task whose drain exceeds the configured deadline (default 5 seconds) is force-transitioned to finalize with `DrainTimeout` status.
4. `FinalizeRecord` includes: task_id, cancel_reason, drain_status (completed/timed_out), obligation_closure_proof (list of obligation IDs and terminal states), and wall-clock timestamps for each phase transition.
5. Obligation closure proof is complete: every obligation spawned by the task appears in the proof with a terminal state. A missing obligation causes a `ClosureProofIncomplete` alert.
6. A task that is not cancelled completes normally and produces a `FinalizeRecord` with `cancel_reason: None` (the protocol applies to all task completions, not just cancellations).
7. Nested cancellation: a parent task cancellation propagates to child tasks, and the parent's finalize waits for all children's finalize records.
8. Verification evidence JSON includes tasks_cancelled, tasks_drain_completed, tasks_drain_timed_out, closure_proofs_generated, closure_proofs_complete, and avg_drain_duration_ms fields.

## Testing & Logging Requirements

- Unit tests: (a) CancellableTask lifecycle: create -> run -> cancel -> drain -> finalize; (b) Drain timeout enforcement; (c) FinalizeRecord completeness; (d) Lane slot release timing on cancel; (e) Normal completion (no cancel) still produces FinalizeRecord.
- Integration tests: (a) Migration orchestration cancel mid-flight with obligation closure; (b) Anti-entropy sweep cancel with partial progress safely abandoned; (c) Nested task cancellation propagation (parent -> 3 children); (d) Cancel during two-phase flow prepare — verify rollback and closure proof.
- Adversarial tests: (a) Drain handler that panics — verify finalize still executes with error status; (b) Cancel signal sent to already-finalizing task — verify idempotent handling; (c) 100 concurrent cancellations — verify no resource leaks; (d) Cancel with no obligations — verify empty but valid closure proof.
- Structured logs: Events use stable codes (FN-CX-001 through FN-CX-010), include `task_id`, `trace_id`, `phase` (cancel/drain/finalize), `drain_status`, `obligations_count`. JSON-formatted.

## Expected Artifacts

- docs/specs/section_10_11/bd-7om_contract.md
- crates/franken-node/src/runtime/cancellation.rs (or equivalent module path)
- crates/franken-node/src/runtime/cancellable_task.rs (trait definition + registration)
- scripts/check_cancellation_protocol.py (with --json flag and self_test())
- tests/test_check_cancellation_protocol.py
- artifacts/section_10_11/bd-7om/verification_evidence.json
- artifacts/section_10_11/bd-7om/verification_summary.md
acceptance_criteria:
AC for bd-7om:
1. All product services adopt the canonical three-phase cancellation protocol from 10.15: Cancel (signal intent) -> Drain (complete in-flight work, reject new work) -> Finalize (release resources, emit completion evidence).
2. A CancellationProtocol trait is defined with methods: cancel(), drain(timeout: Duration) -> DrainOutcome, finalize() -> FinalizeReport.
3. State transitions are strictly ordered: Idle -> Cancelled -> Draining -> Finalized. Any out-of-order transition attempt returns Err with stable code CANCEL_PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
4. Drain has a configurable timeout; if in-flight work does not complete within the timeout, drain returns DrainOutcome::TimedOut with a list of still-active work items, and finalize force-drops them with a CANCEL_FORCE_DROP log event.
5. Double-cancel is idempotent (no error, no state change beyond first cancel).
6. Every service implementing CancellationProtocol emits structured telemetry: CANCEL_SIGNAL_RECEIVED, DRAIN_STARTED, DRAIN_COMPLETED / DRAIN_TIMED_OUT, FINALIZE_COMPLETED with trace correlation IDs and elapsed-time measurements.
7. Unit tests verify: (a) happy-path cancel -> drain -> finalize completes cleanly, (b) drain timeout triggers forced finalization, (c) out-of-order transition is rejected, (d) double-cancel is idempotent, (e) new work submitted during drain phase is rejected with WORK_REJECTED_DRAINING.
8. Integration test: a multi-service orchestration cancels all services concurrently and verifies total drain time is bounded by the maximum individual drain timeout (parallel drain, not serial).

1) Preserve full canonical-plan scope; no feature compression or silent omission is allowed.
2) Completion requires comprehensive verification coverage appropriate to scope: unit tests, integration tests, and E2E scripts/workflows with detailed structured logging (stable event/error codes + trace correlation IDs).
3) Completion requires reproducible evidence artifacts (machine-readable + human-readable) that allow independent replay and root-cause triage.
4) Any implementation PR for this bead must include explicit links to the above test/logging artifacts.
