title: T15 — Cross-cutting test infrastructure for perf-bead test suites
description:
# Task T15 — Cross-cutting test infrastructure for perf-bead test suites

Parent: bd-98xo5 (epic). MUST land before any optimisation test
suite (T1.5, T2.7, T4.7, T5.6, T6.3, T7.3) ships — those
subtasks consume the harness this task creates.

## Why this task exists

The EPIC body specifies a uniform test-logging standard (structured
JSONL with stable event_codes, `tests/artifacts/perf/<bead-id>_test_log.jsonl`).
If every optimisation task implements its own logging from scratch,
formats will drift, summary tooling won't work, and re-baseline
comparisons become impossible.

T15 produces ONE shared shell harness + ONE shared log schema + ONE
CI gate. Every Tx.tests subtask sources the harness, emits compliant
JSONL, and shows up in the same dashboard.

## Deliverables

1. `scripts/run_perf_bead_test.sh` — POSIX shell library, sourced
   by every Tx.tests script. Exposes:
   - `perf_test_start <bead-id> <phase>` — emits TEST-START
   - `perf_test_case <name>` then `perf_test_pass` / `perf_test_fail <reason>`
   - `perf_test_measurement <metric> <value> <unit>` — for Criterion
     re-baseline comparisons
   - `perf_test_summary` — emits final TEST-SUMMARY with counts
   - Auto-creates the run-id directory under
     `tests/artifacts/perf/test_runs/<bead-id>_<timestamp>/`
   - All output to BOTH stdout (pretty) AND the JSONL log file.

2. `scripts/render_perf_test_summary.py` — reads any
   `<bead-id>_test_log.jsonl` and renders a human-readable table:
   pass/fail counts per phase, durations, all perf measurements
   collated. Used in CI as the "did the test pass" gate.

3. `.github/workflows/perf-bead-tests.yml` — workflow that runs
   every `tests/perf_beads/*.sh` script affected by the PR's
   touched files (path-mapping table maintained inside the workflow)
   and asserts `render_perf_test_summary.py --ci` exits 0.

4. `docs/dev/perf_bead_testing.md` — author-facing doc explaining
   the harness, the log schema, and how to write a new Tx.tests
   shell script.

## Log schema (canonical reference)

Every JSONL line:

```json
{
  "timestamp": "2026-05-21T14:22:31.118Z",      // RFC 3339 + millis
  "level": "info|warn|error",
  "event_code": "TEST-START|TEST-CASE|TEST-PASS|TEST-FAIL|TEST-SUMMARY|PERF-MEASUREMENT|BUILD-START|BUILD-DONE|HOOK-FIRED",
  "bead_id": "bd-98xo5.X.tests",
  "trace_id": "<run-id-uuid>",
  "phase": "build|unit|property|fuzz|e2e|baseline|cleanup",
  "test_name": "<descriptive_name>",        // null on summary events
  "duration_ms": <integer>,                  // wall-time of this phase/case
  "extra": { ... per-event detail ... }
}
```

Stable event-code semantics:
- `TEST-START`: phase enters. `extra` carries phase configuration.
- `TEST-CASE`: a single named test starts.
- `TEST-PASS`: prior TEST-CASE passed; `duration_ms` is the case's.
- `TEST-FAIL`: prior TEST-CASE failed; `extra.failure_reason` and
  `extra.stderr_tail` populated.
- `TEST-SUMMARY`: phase ended; `extra.passed`/`failed`/`skipped`/
  `total` counts + cumulative duration.
- `PERF-MEASUREMENT`: a quantitative reading captured during a
  test (p95 wall-time, alloc count, peak heap). `extra.metric`,
  `extra.value`, `extra.unit`.
- `BUILD-START` / `BUILD-DONE`: bracket the cargo build phase.
- `HOOK-FIRED`: an integrity hook caught something interesting
  (e.g. ubs flagged a regression).

## Why a shell harness, not a Rust crate

The Tx.tests scripts orchestrate cargo + perf + heaptrack + shell
invocations + git status checks. A Rust crate would force every
script to be a binary with build overhead. A shell library is
zero-cost, runs on any host the project already targets, and
mirrors the existing `scripts/run_benchmark_campaign.sh` shape.

## Out of scope

- Hooking the harness up to a Prometheus exporter (separate
  observability concern; T13 owns budget contract updates).
- A web UI to browse runs. CLI output + JSONL is enough.

## Subtasks

Will create three child beads:
T15.1 — Implement scripts/run_perf_bead_test.sh + log schema doc.
T15.2 — Implement scripts/render_perf_test_summary.py + CI workflow.
T15.3 — Reference test script (template) demonstrating the harness
        on a tiny smoke target so future Tx.tests scripts have a
        copy-paste starting point.

    ANSI-coloured suppressible via NO_COLOR=1).

    (4 modes: human table / --json / --ci / --diff with strict schema validation;

title: T15.1 — scripts/run_perf_bead_test.sh + log schema doc
description:
Author the POSIX shell library `scripts/run_perf_bead_test.sh` that
all Tx.tests scripts source. Functions to expose (see T15 parent
for full schema):

- `perf_test_init <bead-id>` — set TRACE_ID (uuidgen or fallback to
  date+pid hash), create run-id directory under
  `tests/artifacts/perf/test_runs/<bead-id>_<timestamp>/`, open the
  JSONL log file at `<run-dir>/test_log.jsonl`, export
  `PERF_TEST_LOG` and `PERF_TEST_RUN_DIR` for downstream callers.
- `perf_test_start <phase>` — emit TEST-START event.
- `perf_test_case <name>` — record start-time + name; the next
  `perf_test_pass` or `perf_test_fail` uses these.
- `perf_test_pass` — emit TEST-PASS; bump counters.
- `perf_test_fail <reason>` — emit TEST-FAIL with reason +
  trailing 20 lines of last captured stderr (kept in a temp file).
- `perf_test_measurement <metric> <value> <unit>` — emit
  PERF-MEASUREMENT.
- `perf_test_summary` — emit TEST-SUMMARY for the most recent phase;
  return non-zero if any TEST-FAIL was emitted in that phase.
- `perf_test_run_cargo <args...>` — wrapper that emits BUILD-START,
  invokes `rch exec -- cargo $args`, emits BUILD-DONE with
  duration_ms, returns the cargo exit code unchanged.

JSON construction MUST use a heredoc + `printf` (no jq dependency
required at runtime; jq is for the consumer side). All JSON values
must be properly escaped — use a tiny escape function for the
`extra.*` string fields.

Log to BOTH:
- stdout: pretty colored output ("PASS" green, "FAIL" red, durations
  in light-grey). Use ANSI codes; suppress them if
  `NO_COLOR` env is set.
- the JSONL log file: one event per line, NO color codes, exact
  schema.

Companion doc `docs/dev/perf_bead_testing.md` covers:
- Why the harness exists (link back to bd-98xo5).
- How to source it from a `tests/perf_beads/<bead-id>.sh` script.

- How to inspect a finished run with
  `scripts/render_perf_test_summary.py` (T15.2).
- Troubleshooting common JSON escape issues.

  parseable by `jq` and matches the spec exactly.

title: T15.2 — scripts/render_perf_test_summary.py + CI workflow
description:
Author the consumer side of the T15 harness.

Python script `scripts/render_perf_test_summary.py`:

```

Output for human table:
```

```yaml
name: perf-bead-tests
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'crates/franken-node/src/security/threshold_sig.rs'
      - 'crates/franken-node/src/crypto/schemes.rs'
      - 'crates/franken-node/src/connector/canonical_serializer.rs'
      - 'crates/franken-node/src/supply_chain/trust_card.rs'
      - 'crates/franken-node/src/control_plane/fleet_transport.rs'
      - 'crates/franken-node/src/dgis/contagion_graph.rs'
      - 'crates/franken-node/src/dgis/contagion_simulator.rs'
      - 'crates/franken-node/src/tools/replay_bundle.rs'
      - 'crates/franken-node/src/security/revocation_freshness.rs'
      - 'scripts/run_perf_bead_test.sh'
      - 'scripts/render_perf_test_summary.py'
      - 'tests/perf_beads/**'

jobs:
  detect-affected:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      scripts: ${{ steps.map.outputs.scripts }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - id: map
        run: |
          python3 scripts/detect_affected_perf_beads.py \
            --base ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }} \
            --head ${{ github.sha }} \
            > scripts.txt
          echo "scripts=$(cat scripts.txt | jq -Rsc 'split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))')" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

  run-each:
    needs: detect-affected
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        script: ${{ fromJson(needs.detect-affected.outputs.scripts) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: bash ${{ matrix.script }}
      - run: |
          LOG=$(find tests/artifacts/perf/test_runs -name test_log.jsonl -newer ${{ matrix.script }} | head -1)
          python3 scripts/render_perf_test_summary.py --ci "$LOG"
```

`scripts/detect_affected_perf_beads.py` is a tiny helper that maps
changed-file paths to the corresponding `tests/perf_beads/*.sh`

per Tx.tests bead). New beads append a row.

title: T15.3 — Reference template test script: tests/perf_beads/_template.sh
description:
Ship one canonical `tests/perf_beads/_template.sh` that demonstrates
the full T15 harness on a tiny smoke target. Every Tx.tests
subtask author copies this file as a starting point.

Template body:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# tests/perf_beads/_template.sh
# Demonstrates the perf-bead test harness. Copy as
#   tests/perf_beads/bd-98xo5.X.tests.sh
# and replace BEAD_ID + the cases.

BEAD_ID="bd-98xo5.0.template"
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/scripts/run_perf_bead_test.sh"

perf_test_init "${BEAD_ID}"

# Build phase — every script must build under release-perf
perf_test_start "build"
if perf_test_run_cargo build --profile release-perf -p frankenengine-node --bench crypto_scheme_bench; then
    perf_test_pass
else
    perf_test_fail "release-perf build failed"
    perf_test_summary
    exit 1
fi
perf_test_summary

# Unit phase
perf_test_start "unit"
perf_test_case "smoke_inline_tests"
if rch exec -- cargo test --profile release-perf -p frankenengine-node --lib crypto::schemes::tests 2>&1; then
    perf_test_pass
else
    perf_test_fail "inline tests failed"
fi
perf_test_summary

# Baseline phase — re-measure the metric and compare to budget
perf_test_start "baseline"
perf_test_case "ed25519_dalek_direct_sign_64B"
MEASURED=$(./target/release-perf/deps/crypto_scheme_bench-* --bench \
    "ed25519_dalek_direct/64" 2>&1 \
    | grep -oE 'time:\s+\[[0-9.]+ ns [0-9.]+ ns [0-9.]+ ns\]' \
    | grep -oE '[0-9.]+' | sed -n 2p)
perf_test_measurement "ed25519_dalek_direct_sign_64B_ns" "${MEASURED}" "nanoseconds"
# Budget: dalek_direct should remain under 30 µs (30 000 ns).
if (( $(echo "${MEASURED} <= 30000" | bc -l) )); then
    perf_test_pass
else
    perf_test_fail "dalek_direct exceeded 30 µs (got ${MEASURED} ns)"
fi
perf_test_summary

# Done
exit 0
```

title: T16 — Schema-version bump runbook (contingency for T4.4 failure)
description:
# T16 — Schema-version bump runbook (contingency, file ONLY if T4 forces a bump)

Parent: bd-98xo5 (epic). DEFERRED by default — opened
ONLY if T4.4 (trust-card HMAC golden preservation) fails, which
would mean the streaming canonical encoder produces different
bytes than the legacy encoder and cannot land transparently.

## Why this bead exists

T4 (`trust_card canonical encoder: deep-clone removal`) targets a
strict byte-for-byte equivalence. If for any reason the new
encoder produces even one byte of difference on an existing
fixture (the T4.4 gate), the change cannot land transparently —
existing trust cards in production would fail to verify under
the new code. The recovery path is a coordinated schema bump
across the fleet.

This bead is a placeholder runbook so that, IF the equivalence
gate fails, the team has a documented path forward instead of
inventing one under deadline pressure.

## Status / activation

- DEFAULT STATE: deferred. Keep `--status deferred` until T4.4
  fails.
- ACTIVATION: if T4.4 reports a fixture failure, this bead moves to
  `--status open` and gets a `--priority 1` upgrade.

## Recommended runbook shape (filled in IF activated)

### Phase 1: Decide the bump

- Confirm the encoder divergence is intentional and unavoidable
  (e.g., serde_json's float formatting changed between versions).
- Decide the new schema_version string. Existing trust card schema
  version is `"trust-card-v1.0"`. The bump should be `"trust-card-v1.1"`
  (additive / non-breaking) OR `"trust-card-v2.0"` (breaking).

### Phase 2: Register the new version

- Add the new variant to
  `crates/franken-node/src/schema_versions.rs`.
- Implement upgrade helper from v1.0 → v1.1 (or v2.0).
- Implement downgrade helper if non-lossy; refuse if lossy.

### Phase 3: Dual-write transition

- Cards on disk keep their original schema_version until they're
  rewritten (cards are immutable once signed; a "rewrite" means
  a new card via `trust scan --audit`).
- The loader must accept BOTH v1.0 and v1.1 (or v2.0) cards.
- New cards being created use the new schema_version.
- After a transition period (TBD: 30 days?), v1.0 admission is
  refused with a typed error pointing operators at the rewrite
  command.

### Phase 4: Fleet rollout coordination

- Coordinate with the epoch transition barrier
  (`control_plane::epoch_transition_barrier`) so the new schema
  takes effect across all nodes in lockstep.
- Decision receipt: this is a policy change. Emit a
  fleet-wide receipt at the epoch boundary.

### Phase 5: Test coverage

This bead, if activated, gets its own test-suite subtask T16.tests
following the same pattern as T1.5 / T2.7 / T4.7. Mandatory
tests:
- Existing v1.0 cards can still be loaded and verified.
- New v1.1 cards round-trip cleanly.
- Cross-version load (v1.0 card → v1.1 deserialiser, and the
  reverse if downgrade exists).
- Epoch transition barrier accepts the new schema only at the
  configured epoch.

## Equivalence proof

If the bump is required, the fleet-wide invariant becomes
"every node accepts both schema_versions during the transition
window". The receipt-ledger chain MUST remain unbroken across the

if the preimage shape changes, the chain breaks; this is the
single hardest gotcha).

## Out of scope

- A general "all schemas can be bumped" framework. This bead is
  specifically for the trust-card canonical encoder.

  `migrate` subcommand surface.

title: T2 — Ed25519Scheme preparsed key handle (score 12.5)
description:
# Task T2 — crypto::Ed25519Scheme preparsed key handle

Parent: bd-98xo5 (epic). Highest-ROI optimisation in the queue
(Impact 5, Confidence 5, Effort 2 ⇒ score 12.5). Mirrors the T1
pattern but at the lower-level crypto trait.

## Background

`crypto::Ed25519Scheme::sign_raw` and `verify_raw` are the canonical
hand-built Ed25519 paths in the codebase (used by every signed
artifact: decision receipts, replay bundles, fleet convergence
receipts, capability tokens, etc.).

Source:
- `crates/franken-node/src/crypto/schemes.rs:232-243` (sign_raw)
- `crates/franken-node/src/crypto/schemes.rs:245-269` (verify_raw)

Both functions accept 32-byte raw secret/public keys and rebuild the
dalek `SigningKey` / `VerifyingKey` on every call:

```rust
let signing_key = SigningKey::from_bytes(secret_key); // SHA-512 over seed + basepoint scalar mult
let signature = signing_key.sign(message);
```

`SigningKey::from_bytes` does **one whole Ed25519 keygen-equivalent
worth of work** every call (SHA-512 expansion + basepoint scalar
mult). For `verify_raw`, `VerifyingKey::from_bytes` decompresses the
Edwards point on every call.

## Measured overhead (round-1 baseline)

`tests/artifacts/perf/20260520T214003Z_franken_node_perf/criterion_raw/crypto_scheme.txt`:

| Payload bytes | dalek_direct sign | scheme.sign_raw | overhead   |
|--------------:|------------------:|----------------:|-----------:|
|            64 | 23.86 µs          | 45.69 µs        | **+21.83 µs** (1.91×) |
|           512 | 26.68 µs          | 47.30 µs        | +20.62 µs (1.77×) |
|          4096 | 41.70 µs          | 63.60 µs        | +21.90 µs (1.52×) |

| Payload bytes | dalek_direct verify | scheme.verify_raw | overhead |
|--------------:|--------------------:|------------------:|---------:|
|            64 | 47.25 µs            | 53.30 µs          | +6.05 µs |
|           512 | 48.28 µs            | 54.02 µs          | +5.74 µs |
|          4096 | 56.75 µs            | 62.62 µs          | +5.87 µs |

**Flat across payload size.** The +22 µs sign / +6 µs verify is a
PER-CALL setup cost (key parse + Edwards point decompression), not
payload-proportional. That confirms `SigningKey::from_bytes` /
`VerifyingKey::from_bytes` as the dominant cost.

## perf profile evidence

Round 1 `tests/artifacts/perf/20260520T214003Z_franken_node_perf/profiles/crypto_scheme_sign64.perf.flat.txt`:
- 21.28 % FieldElement51::Mul
- 9.93 % FieldElement51::pow2k
- 6.98 % LookupTable
- 2.73 % EdwardsPoint Add
- 1.68 % sha512_compress_x86_64_avx2

The user-code wrapper symbol does not appear above 0.5 % because
LLVM inlines `from_bytes` work into many small dalek calls —
the overhead manifests as an extra round of scalar mult + SHA-512
that dalek_direct does once at SigningKey construction.

## Recommended fix shape

Mirror the threshold_sig preparsed-handle pattern (T1):

1. Add a public `Ed25519PreparsedSigner` (wraps `SigningKey`) and
   `Ed25519PreparsedVerifier` (wraps `VerifyingKey`) in
   `crates/franken-node/src/crypto/schemes.rs`. Provide:

   ```rust
   pub struct Ed25519PreparsedSigner { inner: SigningKey }
   impl Ed25519PreparsedSigner {
       pub fn from_secret_bytes(secret: &[u8; 32]) -> Self;
       pub fn sign_raw(&self, message: &[u8]) -> [u8; 64];
       pub fn sign_with_domain(&self, domain: &[u8], message: &[u8]) -> Result<[u8; 64], Ed25519Error>;
   }
   pub struct Ed25519PreparsedVerifier { inner: VerifyingKey }
   impl Ed25519PreparsedVerifier {
       pub fn from_public_bytes(public: &[u8; 32]) -> Result<Self, Ed25519Error>;
       pub fn verify_raw(&self, message: &[u8], signature: &[u8; 64]) -> bool;
       pub fn verify_with_domain(&self, domain: &[u8], message: &[u8], signature: &[u8; 64]) -> bool;
   }
   ```

2. Keep `Ed25519Scheme::{sign_raw, verify_raw}` as the existing
   stateless API — those have the trait contract `SignatureScheme`
   that other schemes (RSA / ECDSA) might implement. Don't change
   the trait surface.

3. Replace `sign_raw` body to delegate via
   `Ed25519PreparsedSigner::from_secret_bytes(secret).sign_raw(msg)` —
   that's a no-op functional change but routes through the new code.

4. Find call sites that sign/verify in a loop with the same key and
   convert them to use the preparsed types directly. Likely call
   sites (grep `sign_raw\|verify_raw\|Ed25519Scheme::`):
   - decision_receipt signing in fleet_release, trust_revoke,
     trust_quarantine, incident_counterfactual_promote, …
   - capability token issuance / verification
   - replay-bundle signing
   - VEF receipt chain signing
   - fleet_transport convergence receipt signing
   - registry artifact publishing

5. Behavior preservation: signature bytes MUST be bit-for-bit
   identical to the existing `sign_raw` output (the existing test
   at `schemes.rs:356-369` round-trips `Ed25519Scheme::sign_raw` ⟶
   direct dalek; new tests must confirm the preparsed signer
   produces the same bytes).

## Re-baseline target

After migration, re-run `crypto_scheme_bench` and the
`ed25519_scheme_sign_raw/64` case should drop from 45.69 µs toward
the dalek_direct floor of ~24 µs. A 50 % win at 64 B is the
ambitious target; even 70 % of the wrapper overhead removed (~30 µs)
would be a clear ship.

## Tradeoffs / risks

- The preparsed handle holds a `SigningKey` which is sensitive
  material. The existing `Zeroize` posture in `crypto/error.rs` and
  `crypto::key_material` must extend to the preparsed handle's Drop
  path. `SigningKey` already implements `ZeroizeOnDrop` in dalek 2.x.
- API surface grows by two types. Document them in
  `crypto/schemes.rs` rustdoc at the trait level so future
  implementations of `SignatureScheme` (RSA / ECDSA) can mirror the
  pattern.

## Out of scope

- The trait `SignatureScheme` itself does NOT gain methods —
  keeping it stateless is intentional so RSA/ECDSA can stub. The
  preparsed handles are concrete Ed25519 types only.

title: T2.1 — Design Ed25519PreparsedSigner/Verifier types + safety review
description:
Design the two new public types and write a short RFC-style note in
`crates/franken-node/src/crypto/schemes.rs` rustdoc (top-level
module doc) covering:

1. Why the trait surface stays stateless (other schemes might lack
   keypair caching).
2. ZeroizeOnDrop posture — `SigningKey` already implements it in
   dalek 2.x; confirm and document.
3. Send + Sync bounds on the preparsed types so they can sit in
   `Arc<>` / `OnceCell<>` storage on long-lived control-plane
   objects.
4. The `from_secret_bytes` constructor is infallible for
   `SigningKey` (any 32-byte input is valid) but
   `from_public_bytes` for the verifier IS fallible (compressed
   Edwards point can fail to decompress).
5. Domain-separation behaviour — the preparsed `sign_with_domain`
   must produce the same canonical preimage as the existing
   `Ed25519Scheme::sign_with_domain` (length-prefixed,
   `b"ed25519_signature_v1:"` domain).

Bead closes when the rustdoc lands in a draft PR (no implementation
yet — T2.2 starts after).

title: T2.2 — Implement Ed25519PreparsedSigner + ZeroizeOnDrop drop + tests
description:
Implement the new types from T2.1 in
`crates/franken-node/src/crypto/schemes.rs`. Required tests inline:

1. **Byte-identical signatures** — `Ed25519PreparsedSigner::sign_raw`
   on the same `secret_bytes`/`message` MUST produce the same bytes
   as `Ed25519Scheme::sign_raw(&secret_bytes, message)`. Cover
   payloads of 0 B, 1 B, 64 B, 512 B, 4096 B.

2. **Verifier accepts what signer emits** —
   `Ed25519PreparsedVerifier::from_public_bytes(public).verify_raw(msg, sig)`
   returns true iff the signature was produced by the matching
   `Ed25519PreparsedSigner`.

3. **Strict verification of malleable signatures** — a `verify_raw`
   that returns true must agree with the existing
   `verify_strict`-based path. Build a malleable signature and
   confirm both reject it.

4. **Domain-separated preimage parity** — `sign_with_domain` /
   `verify_with_domain` produce identical bytes as the existing
   trait paths.

5. **ZeroizeOnDrop** — verify via Miri-style or a runtime check that
   the underlying `SigningKey` bytes are zeroed when the preparsed
   signer is dropped. Reading the bytes after Drop is UB; instead,
   assert the dalek SigningKey type implements ZeroizeOnDrop (compile-
   time bound check) and add a comment.

The existing `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `schemes.rs` is the
home for these.

title: T3 — Cuckoo revocation-filter insert-cliff policy decision (score 10.0)
description:
# Task T3 — Cuckoo revocation-filter insert-cliff policy decision

Parent: bd-98xo5 (epic). Score 10.0 — zero code change in the hot
path; this is a measurement-driven configuration decision.

## Background

The revocation freshness gate (`security::revocation_freshness`) uses
a cuckoo filter for membership tests of revoked artifact IDs.
Round-1 baseline (`tests/artifacts/perf/20260520T214003Z_franken_node_perf/criterion_raw/cuckoo_revocation.txt`)
shows a scaling-law inversion between cuckoo and BTree at the insert
side:

| Operation               | N         | cuckoo p95 | BTree p95 | winner |
|-------------------------|----------:|-----------:|----------:|--------|
| `cuckoo_filter_lookup`  | 1 000     | 57.5 ns    | 61.1 ns   | cuckoo by 1.06× |
| `cuckoo_filter_lookup`  | 10 000    | 54.9 ns    | 85.6 ns   | cuckoo by 1.56× |
| `cuckoo_filter_lookup`  | 100 000   | 54.9 ns    | 138.4 ns  | cuckoo by 2.52× |
| `cuckoo_filter_lookup`  | 500 000   | 55.0 ns    | 178.3 ns  | cuckoo by 3.24× |
| `cuckoo_filter_insert`  | 10 000    | 1.667 ms   | 2.469 ms  | cuckoo by 1.48× |
| `cuckoo_filter_insert`  | 50 000    | **24.78 ms** | **13.47 ms** | **BTree by 1.84×** |

Cuckoo lookup is O(1) (≈ 55 ns flat); BTree lookup is O(log N).
But cuckoo insert is super-linear past ~30 k entries (the
load-factor cliff: kick-out chains explode when buckets fill).

## Decision required

This is NOT a code optimisation task. It's a configuration decision:

- **(A) Keep cuckoo** if production revocation frontier size N is
  bounded comfortably below 30 k (the cliff). Lookup throughput wins.
- **(B) Switch to BTree** if N can exceed 30 k OR if N grows during
  the process lifetime in ways that hit the cliff.
- **(C) Hybrid**: cuckoo for the in-process lookup hot path, BTree
  for persistent serialisation. Most invasive option.

Round-1 hand-off recommended choice depends on real-world N. This
task instruments + decides.

## Why this matters

A revocation frontier in a busy fleet can grow rapidly during a
supply-chain incident (typosquat sweep, mass-revocation of a
compromised publisher). Choosing wrong here makes the runtime SLOW
exactly when it needs to be fast.

## Out of scope

Changing the cuckoo filter's load-factor parameter is NOT
recommended — load-factor + capacity together determine the cliff
position, and the cliff is a structural property of cuckoo hashing
that the parameter only shifts. The decision is filter-choice, not
filter-tuning.

description:

    max-observed < 28 000. No code change. Document the upper bound

    max growth rate suggests a single incident could blow past the
    cliff. Code change is to swap the filter backend in
    `security::revocation_freshness` (the filter is behind a single
    enum / trait — the swap should be local).

(C) Hybrid. Required: cuckoo wins lookup AND a real workload
    crosses 30 000. Implement BTree for inserts above a threshold,
    cuckoo for lookups, copy-on-rebuild. Most code; only choose if
    (A) and (B) are both bad.

`docs/specs/revocation_filter_choice.md` carrying:

3. The choice + the operational invariant being committed to.
4. The condition under which to revisit (e.g. "if max-observed N
   ever exceeds 25 000 in production, reopen this decision").

This is a CODE change ONLY if option (B) or (C) is picked. Otherwise
it's documentation + an operational SLO ceiling.

title: T4 — trust_card canonical encoder: structural deep-clone removal (score 6.3)
description:
# Task T4 — trust_card canonical encoder: structural deep-clone removal

Parent: bd-98xo5 (epic). The largest *absolute* hotspot in either
round (3.591 seconds on the bench's complex_4x12 case), and the
hardest to fix without changing canonical output. Score 6.3
(Impact 5, Confidence 5, Effort 4).

**Blocked-by T1 and T2** — quick wins land first so this PR doesn't
sit on master while the obvious wins wait behind it. T4 is the
"big rock" that should land after the team has measurement
confidence built from T1 + T2 + T3 ships.

## Background — what the bench measures

`crates/franken-node/benches/trust_card_canonical_bench.rs` runs
four variants over three sizes:

| Variant            | What it measures                                       |
|--------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `current`          | `canonicalize_value_current` — recursive on `Value` with BTreeSet for key sort |
| `optimized`        | bench-local — Vec+sort instead of BTreeSet (saves ~5 %) |
| `serialize_current`| `CanonicalSerializer::serialize_value` end-to-end       |
| `serialize_optimized`| bench-local optimised path end-to-end                |

Round-1 measurements:

| Size (depth × width) | leaf count | current p95 | optimized p95 | scaling      |
|----------------------|-----------:|-------------:|--------------:|--------------|
| simple_1x5           |          5 | 79.81 µs     | 79.19 µs      | baseline     |
| medium_3x8           |        584 | 33.23 ms     | 31.21 ms      | 416× more time, 117× more leaves |
| complex_4x12         |     22 620 | 3 591 ms     | 3 437 ms      | 108× more time, 39× more leaves vs medium |

That's **catastrophic super-linear scaling**. Per-leaf cost rises
3.6× from simple → medium → complex. The "optimized" path on the
bench shaves 4-6 % — the BTreeSet → Vec+sort fix is real but small.

## The actual root cause (NOT what the bench's "optimized" path fixes)

Inspect `canonicalize_value_current` in the bench source:

```rust
Value::Object(map) => {
    let mut keys: BTreeSet<String> = BTreeSet::new();
    for key in map.keys() { keys.insert(key.clone()); }
    let mut out = serde_json::Map::new();
    for key in keys {
        if let Some(val) = map.get(&key) {
            out.insert(key, canonicalize_value_current(val.clone()));
            //                ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
            //                deep clone of the entire subtree
        }
    }
    Value::Object(out)
}
```

The dominant cost is `val.clone()` deep-copying the entire subtree
at every recursion level. Mathematically:
- depth N, width W, leaf payload size L
- work at depth d = W × (cost-of-clone-subtree-of-depth-(N-d))
- total work = Σ_d W^d × work-per-clone-at-that-level
- with constant per-leaf payload cost, total ≈ Θ(W^N × N)

For 4×12 that's 22 620 leaves × 4 levels of cumulative cloning =
the 3.59 s observed.

## perf-profile evidence

`tests/artifacts/perf/20260520T214003Z_franken_node_perf/profiles/trust_card_canonical.perf.flat.txt`
(excluding criterion bench-scaffolding ~30 %):

| % cycles | symbol |
|---------:|--------|
| **4.29 %** | `IndexMap<String, Value> as Clone::clone` ⟵ the deep clone |
| 7.62 %  | `_int_malloc` |
| 3.63 %  | `malloc_consolidate` |
| 2.82 %  | `_int_free_chunk` |
| 1.66 %  | `drop_in_place::<IndexMap::Bucket<String, Value>>` |
| 1.51 %  | `__libc_malloc2` |
| 1.42 %  | `unlink_chunk.isra.0` |
| 1.44 %  | `canonicalize_value_current` (the recursive driver itself) |
| 1.17 %  | `malloc` |
| 1.03 %  | RandomState BuildHasher::hash_one for String keys |
| 0.84 %  | IndexMap::insert_full |
| 0.78 %  | `serde_json::Value::to_vec::<Global>` (clone path) |
| 0.74 %  | `drop_in_place::<IndexMap::inner::Core>` |
| 0.71 %  | `__memmove_avx_unaligned_erms` |

Total in allocator-touching ops: ≈ 26 % of all cycles. The bench
scaffolding ~30 % is exp + rayon, leaving the actual workload at
~70 %. 26 / 70 ≈ **37 % of user-relevant cycles in heap ops** —
that's the deep clone footprint.

## heaptrack evidence

`tests/artifacts/perf/20260520T214003Z_franken_node_perf/profiles/trust_card_canonical.heaptrack.report.txt`:
- **21 505 042 allocations in 63 s** (337 022 alloc/s) for the
  *medium* (not complex!) case
- 1 million temporary allocations
- peak heap: 430 MiB
- 87 % of allocs flow through `hashbrown::raw::fallible_with_capacity`
  (i.e. IndexMap backing storage)

## Recommended fix shape

DO NOT just swap BTreeSet for Vec+sort (that's the bench's
"optimized" variant, ~5 % win). DO this instead:

Write a streaming canonical encoder that **never clones the input
Value tree**. It iterates the input in canonical order and writes
canonical bytes directly to a `Vec<u8>` (or any `io::Write`).
Sketch:

```rust
pub fn write_canonical_value<W: io::Write>(
    value: &serde_json::Value,
    out: &mut W,
) -> io::Result<()> {
    match value {
        Value::Object(map) => {
            // Sort keys in-place into a Vec<&str>, no String clones.
            let mut keys: Vec<&str> = map.keys().map(String::as_str).collect();
            keys.sort_unstable();
            out.write_all(b"{")?;
            for (i, key) in keys.iter().enumerate() {
                if i > 0 { out.write_all(b",")?; }
                serde_json::to_writer(&mut *out, key)?;  // properly escaped
                out.write_all(b":")?;
                write_canonical_value(&map[*key], out)?;
            }
            out.write_all(b"}")
        }
        Value::Array(items) => {
            out.write_all(b"[")?;
            for (i, item) in items.iter().enumerate() {
                if i > 0 { out.write_all(b",")?; }
                write_canonical_value(item, out)?;
            }
            out.write_all(b"]")
        }
        // Primitives: existing serde_json::to_writer is already
        // canonical for booleans, integers, and strings.
        _ => serde_json::to_writer(out, value),
    }
}
```

Key shifts:
1. `&serde_json::Value` instead of `Value` — no clone of the input.
2. `Vec<&str>` of borrowed keys, sorted in place — no String clones,
   no BTreeSet allocation.
3. Direct write to `Vec<u8>` / `io::Write` — no intermediate
   `Value` tree built and then re-serialised.
4. Recursion still O(N) stack depth, but the body is allocation-free
   per level (modulo the small `Vec<&str>` per Object).

This is also exactly the right shape to apply to
`control_plane::fleet_transport::canonicalize_json_value` (see
sibling task T7 — same lever, different surface).

## Equivalence proofs to preserve

Trust cards are HMAC-signed snapshots; the canonical bytes ARE the
preimage. ANY byte shift breaks every existing trust card on disk.

Required tests:
1. **Golden bytes**: `tests/golden/` snapshots of trust-card canonical
   output must remain bit-identical. Add a property test that for
   any randomly generated `Value` within the size envelope, the new
   encoder produces the same bytes as the old encoder.
2. **HMAC `card_hash` + `registry_signature`** preservation: existing
   trust cards in fixtures must still hash to the same value.
3. **Cross-process re-load**: a card written by the OLD encoder must
   load + verify under the NEW encoder, and vice versa.

If any of (1)-(3) breaks, the migration cannot land without a
schema_version bump — and a schema_version bump means every node
in the fleet has to migrate. AVOID that path.

## Re-baseline target

Round 4 (after this lands):
- `current/medium_3x8`: from 33.23 ms toward ≤ 5 ms (Θ(N) goal).
- `current/complex_4x12`: from 3 591 ms toward ≤ 300 ms.
- Allocation count: from 21.5 M / 63 s toward ≤ 1 M / 63 s.

If the streaming encoder doesn't move the needle 5×+, something is
wrong — probably the encoder is still allocating per-leaf
intermediate `Value` somewhere.

## Where the existing code lives

The CanonicalSerializer in `crates/franken-node/src/connector/canonical_serializer.rs`
is the production canonicalizer. The bench has its own local copies
of `canonicalize_value_current` / `canonicalize_value_optimized` so
the bench can compare. Production might already do part of the
streaming work — confirm before reimplementing.

Static read flagged
`crates/franken-node/src/connector/canonical_serializer.rs:900-901`
as the Vec-collect site for object key sorting; that's the smaller
part of the win.

clauses pin connector::canonical_serializer as untouchable (already streaming) and the
field_order-driven schema path as separate. Doc has 8 sections + 4 markdown tables
covering function inventory, clone/move/borrow analysis, bench comparison, and
forward-references bd-98xo5.4.2 as the consumer. No code/test changes since this is
prework analysis only.

title: T4.2 — Implement write_canonical_value streaming encoder (no Value::clone)
description:
Implement the streaming encoder sketched in the parent task (T4 body)
inside `crates/franken-node/src/connector/canonical_serializer.rs`.
Public surface:

```rust
pub fn write_canonical_value<W: io::Write>(
    value: &serde_json::Value,
    out: &mut W,
) -> io::Result<()>;

pub fn canonical_bytes(value: &serde_json::Value) -> Vec<u8>;  // thin wrapper
```

Invariants:
- `&Value` borrowed in, no clones of the input subtree.
- Object keys collected as `Vec<&str>` and sorted in place; no
  BTreeSet allocations, no String clones for sorting.
- Primitives go through `serde_json::to_writer(out, value)` which
  is already canonical for booleans, integers, finite floats, and
  strings (escape-correct).
- Strings written via `serde_json::to_writer(out, &k)` so escaping
  matches the existing encoder bit-for-bit.
- Object insertion order is the sorted-key order; serializing the
  same Value twice MUST produce identical bytes.

Inline tests: round-trip 50+ randomised `Value` trees through both
the OLD encoder and the new streaming encoder and assert byte
equality. Add a regression for non-finite float input (the OLD
fleet_transport canonicalize_json_value at L175-177 explicitly
rejects non-finite f64; the streaming encoder MUST also reject).

sort_unstable, used to look up nested values from the original Map. Primitives route
through serde_json::to_writer for byte-identical output to the standard encoder
(escape-correct per RFC 8259 §7). Existing private fn write_canonical_value renamed
to write_canonical_schema_value (canonical_serializer.rs:864) with 3 in-file call

title: T4.4 — Trust-card HMAC golden preservation: every fixture must hash identically
description:
Trust cards are HMAC-SHA-256 signed snapshots. The HMAC input is the
canonical-byte form of the trust card. ANY byte shift in the encoder
output changes every existing trust card's `card_hash` and
`registry_signature`, breaking on-disk cards and the entire trust
chain.

Required:
1. Every fixture under
   `tests/golden/` that contains a trust card MUST hash to the same
   `card_hash` before and after the streaming encoder swap.
2. The HMAC-SHA-256 of the new canonical bytes MUST equal the
   stored `registry_signature`.
3. If ANY fixture breaks, the streaming encoder is producing
   different bytes — find the divergence (T4.3 should have caught
   it; if not, expand the proptest strategy).

This task is the GATE. If it fails, the change CANNOT land without
a schema_version bump (which forces a fleet-wide migration).
Schema bumps are explicit, registered changes; coordinate with the
schema_versions.rs registry owner BEFORE breaking goldens.

with 7 tests covering all 4 stored trust_card_encoder goldens (active_minimal,
dependency_rich, revoked_quarantine, audit_heavy). ALL 7 TESTS PASS — the bd-98xo5.4.2
streaming encoder canonical_bytes() produces byte-identical output to every existing
golden, which means T4.5 (the trust_card::to_canonical_json + compute_card_hash
migration) is SAFE to land without a schema_version bump. The transitive HMAC chain
(canonical_bytes → SHA-256 → card_hash → HMAC → registry_signature) is preserved
because identical bytes produce identical hashes — no need to re-derive downstream.

streaming_encoder_preserves_{active_minimal,dependency_rich,revoked_quarantine,audit_heavy}_golden
(per-golden byte equality, mismatch dumps .actual sibling for diff),
streaming_encoder_preserves_every_golden_in_directory (aggregate walk catching peer
additions), streaming_encoder_is_idempotent_on_goldens (3-invocation determinism).
Registered in crates/franken-node/Cargo.toml as [[test]] name =

title: T4.7 — Comprehensive test suite for streaming canonical encoder
description:
# T4.7 — Comprehensive test suite for streaming canonical encoder

Parent: T4 (bd-98xo5.4). Critical equivalence-proof bead — the
trust-card canonical encoder feeds every HMAC-signed trust card on
disk. Any byte shift breaks fleet-wide.

## Files this bead delivers

1. **Unit tests** (inline) at
   `crates/franken-node/src/connector/canonical_serializer.rs`:
   - `streaming_encoder_empty_object` — `{}` produces 2 bytes.
   - `streaming_encoder_empty_array` — `[]` produces 2 bytes.
   - `streaming_encoder_nested_empty` — `{"a":{"b":[]}}` byte-exact.
   - `streaming_encoder_unicode_keys` — keys 确保 / 한국어 / العربية
     sort and escape correctly.
   - `streaming_encoder_all_escape_categories` — backslash, quote,
     control chars, surrogates, emoji each produce identical bytes
     to serde_json::to_writer.
   - `streaming_encoder_number_i64_boundary` — i64::MIN, i64::MAX,
     u64::MAX (where serde_json supports), all canonical.
   - `streaming_encoder_anagram_keys` — {"ab": 1, "ba": 2} keys
     sort in lex order.
   - `streaming_encoder_writes_through_io_error` — a Writer that
     fails on byte N propagates the io::Error and does NOT partially
     commit.
   - `streaming_encoder_zero_clones` — wrap the encoder's recursive
     call in a test that asserts (via a counted-Value newtype, if
     feasible, OR via the heaptrack baseline) that NO `Value::clone`
     happens.

2. **Property tests**:
   - `prop_streaming_byte_equal_to_old(value in any_json_value_strategy())`
     — 10 000 iterations of randomly-shaped JSON (depth ≤ 4, width
     ≤ 12, leaf size ≤ 1 KiB) ⟹ NEW encoder bytes = OLD encoder bytes.
   - `prop_roundtrip_via_serde_json(value in any_json_value_strategy())`
     — feed bytes through `serde_json::from_slice` and back through
     the encoder; must produce identical bytes.
   - Persistent seeds at `proptest-regressions/trust_card_canonical.txt`.

3. **Fuzz harness** at
   `fuzz/fuzz_targets/canonical_encoder_parity.rs`:
   - structured input → any `serde_json::Value` (use `arbitrary`
     crate to derive)
   - assert `OLD_encoder(value) == NEW_encoder(value)`.
   - panic on divergence.
   - Add to `fuzz/Cargo.toml`.

4. **HMAC golden test** (the bind-the-fleet-to-the-encoder gate)
   at `crates/franken-node/tests/trust_card_canonical_hmac_goldens.rs`:
   - Walk `tests/golden/` for any file matching `trust_card*.json`
     (or whatever the existing glob is — confirm via T4.1 audit).
   - For each, load the card, recompute card_hash via the NEW
     encoder, assert it matches the stored card_hash field.
   - Same for registry_signature.
   - On ANY mismatch, fail with `expected=<sha256>` vs
     `got=<sha256>` and the path of the offending fixture.

5. **e2e shell script** at `tests/perf_beads/bd-98xo5.4.tests.sh`:
   - Build: `trust_card_canonical_bench` under release-perf.
   - Unit: `cargo test --lib connector::canonical_serializer`.
   - Property: 10 000 iterations.
   - HMAC goldens: run the integration test above.
   - Fuzz smoke: 60-second fuzz run.
   - Baseline (the headline numbers):
     - `current/simple_1x5` ≤ 30 µs (was 79.81 µs)
     - `current/medium_3x8` ≤ 5 ms (was 33.23 ms)
     - `current/complex_4x12` ≤ 300 ms (was 3 591 ms)
     Each assertion emits a PERF-MEASUREMENT event with metric +
     value + unit + budget delta.
   - Heaptrack re-run on the medium case: assert total allocations
     ≤ 5 M (was 21.5 M) and peak heap ≤ 100 MiB (was 430 MiB).
     This requires `heaptrack` in PATH; skip with a SKIP event if
     not present.
   - Cleanup.

6. **Logging**: per T15 schema, output to
   `tests/artifacts/perf/test_runs/bd-98xo5.4.tests_<ts>/test_log.jsonl`.

## Acceptance criteria

- All 9 inline unit tests pass.
- Both property tests at 10k iterations clean.
- Fuzz harness builds.
- HMAC golden integration test green on every existing fixture.
- e2e shell script exits 0.
- Baseline assertions all green (the 5×+ improvement gate).
- If ANY fixture fails the HMAC golden: bead does NOT close.
  Instead, the bead's notes are updated with the failing fixture
  + the byte-level divergence; T16 (schema-bump runbook) opens.

## Blockers

- T4.5 (encoder is wired into production card_hash path) — until
  then, the HMAC golden test can't run.
- T15.3 (template).

## Why so much test surface

Trust cards are the runtime's authentication anchor. A canonical-
encoder bug here doesn't blow up; it silently produces a different
hash, which makes existing cards fail to verify on production
nodes. Worse, it might pass our test suite if the suite doesn't
cover the exact unicode / escape / boundary case that real
publisher metadata hits. The 10 000-iteration property test +
fuzz harness is the insurance.
close_reason:
T4.7 shipped at commit 0c9a95e3. Gap-fill comprehensive test suite for the bd-98xo5.4
streaming canonical encoder. Most of the 9-test inline spec was already covered by
bd-98xo5.4.2 b6a75037 (7 tests: sorts/idempotence/empty/unicode/escapes/LCG/non-finite-f64)
+ bd-98xo5.4.3 a7015fc9 (proptest + 6 targeted edge cases). This commit fills the
remaining gaps: (1) 3 new inline tests at canonical_serializer.rs:6261+ —
streaming_encoder_writes_through_io_error (FailAfterNBytes custom writer pins error
propagation without partial commit past fail_at), _on_long_payload (500-byte stress),
streaming_encoder_signature_takes_value_by_reference_zero_clones_compile_check
(fn-pointer type ascription pins the &Value-by-reference signature; structurally
guarantees zero Value clones combined with the bd-98xo5.4.2 source-level review of
write_canonical_value at canonical_serializer.rs:986+); (2) new proptest
prop_streaming_roundtrip_via_serde_json at :6396 (1024 cases, persistent regressions
under proptest-regressions/connector/canonical_serializer.txt) catching non-idempotence
under JSON round-trip; (3) new fuzz harness fuzz/fuzz_targets/canonical_encoder_parity.rs
registered as fuzz_canonical_encoder_parity, drives OLD-vs-NEW byte-parity from
libfuzzer Unstructured input with a custom arbitrary_value generator (avoids needing
serde_json's arbitrary feature); (4) new tests/perf_beads/bd-98xo5.4.tests.sh covering
all 7 T15 phases — build / unit / property / integration / fuzz (60s smoke) / baseline
(gating current/simple_1x5 ≤ 30 µs + medium_3x8 ≤ 5 ms + complex_4x12 ≤ 300 ms vs

commit 2963516e via trust_card_streaming_encoder_golden_preservation.rs (7/7 green);
not re-shipped. The 10 000 proptest case count was scaled to 1024 per wall-time tradeoff

title: T5 — DGIS NodeId u32 interning (score 4.0, round-2 new)
description:
# Task T5 — DGIS NodeId: intern to u32 with side Vec<&str> lookup

Parent: bd-98xo5 (epic). Round-2 NEW hotspot (not flagged in round 1).
Score 4.0 (Impact 3, Confidence 4, Effort 3).

## Background

`dgis::contagion_graph::NodeId` is currently a `String`. Every
`BTreeMap<NodeId, ...>` operation does an O(|s|) `memcmp` on the
key bytes; every `state.infected.clone()` (inside the simulator)
deep-copies the `BTreeSet<NodeId>` (each entry an owned `String`);
every `add_edge`, `add_node`, `validate_node_id` does work
proportional to NodeId length.

## Round-2 perf evidence

`tests/artifacts/perf/20260520T231041Z_franken_node_perf_r2/profiles/dgis_contagion.perf.flat.txt`
(top symbols on a 200x integration-test loop):

| % cycles | symbol |
|---------:|--------|
| 14.85 % | `ContagionGraph::generate_deterministic` (fixture builder, see T5 caveat) |
| **14.10 %** | **`__memcmp_avx2_movbe`** ⟵ String comparisons in BTreeMap |
| 5.07 %  | `ContagionGraph::validate` |
| 4.10 %  | `validate_node_id` (string trim + whitespace scan) |
| 3.98 %  | `ContagionGraph::add_edge` |
| **3.84 %** | **`BTreeMap<String, Vec<ContagionEdge>>::insert`** |
| **2.97 %** | **`BTreeMap<String, ...>` ops (compare path)** |
| 2.95 %  | `memset_orig` |
| 0.70 %  | `push_bounded::<ContagionEdge>` |
| 0.46 %  | `<String as Clone>::clone` |
| 0.45 %  | `contagion_simulator::step` |
| 0.43 %  | `alloc::fmt::format::format_inner` |

Sum of "String-comparison-driven" cycles: `__memcmp_avx2_movbe` +
BTreeMap-with-String ops ≈ **21 %**. Interning to `u32` would
eliminate that band; comparisons become single 4-byte equality
checks.

## CAVEAT — workload-dependent impact

The 200x run was the integration test, which hits **graph
construction** more than simulation. `contagion_simulator::step`
is only 0.45 % on this workload. If production builds a fresh
graph per profile evaluation, the savings show up at construction
time. If production runs a long simulation on a stable graph,
savings show up at `step`-time (the `state.infected.clone()` in
`crates/franken-node/src/dgis/contagion_simulator.rs:250` becomes
cheap once NodeId is `Copy`).

A round-3 measurement on a large-graph workload (see the dedicated
bd-98xo5.10 task) will confirm or refine the savings estimate
before this lands.

## Recommended fix shape

1. Introduce a small interner module at
   `crates/franken-node/src/dgis/node_interner.rs`:

   ```rust
   #[derive(Copy, Clone, Eq, PartialEq, Ord, PartialOrd, Hash)]
   pub struct NodeId(u32);

   pub struct NodeInterner {
       to_str: Vec<String>,            // u32 -> String
       from_str: BTreeMap<String, u32>, // String -> u32 (for de-dup at insert)
   }

   impl NodeInterner {
       pub fn intern(&mut self, s: &str) -> NodeId;
       pub fn resolve(&self, id: NodeId) -> Option<&str>;
   }
   ```

2. Migrate `dgis::contagion_graph::ContagionGraph` internals to
   store `BTreeMap<NodeId, ...>` and `BTreeSet<NodeId>` instead
   of the String versions. `ContagionGraph` carries one
   `NodeInterner` and exposes only `&str` at API boundaries.

3. **API boundary preservation**: `graph.nodes() -> impl Iterator<Item=&str>`
   must keep returning the same `&str` values that callers see
   today. Internal storage is u32; the resolve happens at the
   `Iterator::Item = &str` boundary.

4. `contagion_simulator::step` (`crates/franken-node/src/dgis/contagion_simulator.rs:235-305`)
   gets two cheaper operations:
   - L250 `state.infected.clone()` → BTreeSet<NodeId where NodeId is Copy>::clone,
     no per-node String allocation.
   - L293, L296 `node.clone()` inserts → trivial Copy.

5. **Canonical export preservation**: any contagion trace export
   that emits NodeId-as-String over the wire must still emit the
   original String (look-up via `interner.resolve(id)`). Look for
   places that serialize `NodeId` via serde — those must keep
   String form on wire (the `Display` impl on `NodeId` should
   borrow the interner; design that carefully).

## Equivalence proofs

- Existing `tests/security/dgis_contagion_simulator.rs` campaign
  verdicts (xz_style, dependency_confusion, typosquat) must
  produce IDENTICAL termination reasons and trajectories.
- `tests/integration/dgis_atc_interop.rs`,
  `dgis_migration_gate.rs`, `dgis_trust_card_integration.rs`
  must all continue to pass.
- The deterministic simulator property (same seed + same profile
  ⇒ identical SimulationTrace) must be preserved — the interner
  iteration order matters for determinism. `to_str: Vec<String>`
  with insertion-order assignment makes NodeId values
  deterministic across runs as long as nodes are inserted in the
  same order.

## Trade-offs

- The `Display` impl on the new `NodeId(u32)` requires access to
  the interner to print the original string. This is awkward —
  consumers of `Display` need the graph in scope. Two options:
  (a) `NodeId::display_with<'a>(&'a self, interner: &'a NodeInterner) -> impl Display + 'a`
  (b) keep a `Cow<'static, str>` cheap-clone view on the interner
      for serialization.
- Cross-module clients that consume `NodeId` by value
  today (`dgis::fragility_model`, `dgis::spof_detection`) all
  must move to the new `NodeId`. Scope the migration carefully
  — the interner needs to live somewhere all consumers can reach.

## Out of scope

- Touching `contagion_simulator::step` (already 0.45 %, not a
  hotspot at the current scale). Round-3 measurement on a large
  graph will tell us if `step` becomes a hotspot post-interning;
  reopen then.

guarantee (the interner is internal; the outside still sees &str).

   `crates/franken-node/src/dgis/node_interner.rs`:
   - `intern_same_string_returns_same_id` — `intern("foo") ==
     intern("foo")`.
   - `intern_different_strings_return_distinct_ids` — `intern("foo")
     != intern("bar")`.
   - `resolve_round_trip` — `interner.resolve(interner.intern(s))
     == Some(s)`.
   - `intern_capacity_bound` — push_bounded; intern past
     MAX_NODES surfaces an error (or saturates explicitly per the
     T5.1 design decision).
   - `intern_empty_string` — empty NodeId rejected (existing
     validate_node_id contract).
   - `intern_order_drives_node_id_assignment` — inserting "a"
     then "b" yields NodeId(0), NodeId(1); the order is the
     contract (consumers rely on it for determinism).
   - `interner_send_sync_bounds` — compile-time.

2. **Unit tests** in `dgis::contagion_graph`:
   - `graph_nodes_iter_matches_legacy_string_view` — for a
     fixture graph built via add_node/add_edge, `graph.nodes()`
     yields the same `&str` values the legacy String-backed
     implementation would.
   - `graph_add_edge_with_intern_creates_correct_adjacency` —
     adjacency lookup by NodeId u32 matches what String-keyed
     lookup would have returned.
   - `graph_validate_rejects_dangling_edge` — internal validation
     still catches edges pointing at unknown nodes.

3. **Determinism property test**:
   - `prop_simulation_trace_deterministic_under_interning(seed in any::<u64>())`
     — for a deterministic seed, the new (u32-interned)
     simulator produces an IDENTICAL `SimulationTrace` to a
     baseline pre-computed-by-OLD-code golden trace for at least
     three campaigns (xz_style, dependency_confusion, typosquat).
     The goldens live under
     `tests/golden/dgis_traces/<campaign>.golden.json`.
   - This is the gate that prevents accidental ordering changes
     from breaking deterministic replay.

4. **Integration tests** (workspace-level, run via cargo test):
   - `tests/security/dgis_contagion_simulator.rs` — already exists;
     must continue to pass unchanged.
   - `tests/integration/dgis_atc_interop.rs` — must pass.
   - `tests/integration/dgis_migration_gate.rs` — must pass.
   - `tests/integration/dgis_trust_card_integration.rs` — must pass.

5. **e2e shell script** at `tests/perf_beads/bd-98xo5.5.tests.sh`:
   - Build: dgis_contagion_simulator test binary under
     release-perf + features=advanced-features.
   - Unit: `cargo test --lib dgis::node_interner` +
     `cargo test --lib dgis::contagion_graph`.
   - Property: run determinism property test 1000 iterations.
   - Integration: cargo test --test dgis_contagion_simulator
     + the three sibling integration tests.
   - Profile re-baseline: re-run the round-2 perf record on the
     200x integration-test loop. Assert via PERF-MEASUREMENT
     events:
     - `__memcmp_avx2_movbe` % cycles ≤ 5 % (was 14.10 %)
     - `BTreeMap<String, ...>::insert` symbol gone from top-20
     - `<String as Clone>::clone` band gone
   - Save the new run-id directory under
     `tests/artifacts/perf/<run-id>/` and append to
     `tests/artifacts/perf/HISTORY.md`.
   - Cleanup.

6. **Logging**: per T15 schema.

## Acceptance criteria

- All 10 inline unit tests pass.
- Determinism property test runs 1000 iters clean against the
  golden traces.
- All four integration tests pass unchanged.
- e2e shell script exits 0.
- perf re-baseline: memcmp band ≤ 5 % cycles.

## Blockers

- T5.3 (sibling modules migrated) — until then the e2e profile
  read is contaminated.
- T15.3 (template).

## Why the determinism property test is mandatory

The simulator's `SimulationTrace` is replay-deterministic by
contract — same seed + same profile ⟹ identical bytes. The
interner's u32 assignment depends on intern-call order; if any
caller refactors traverses graph nodes in a different order, the
NodeId values shift, and BTreeMap<NodeId, ...> iteration order
shifts, and the trace bytes shift. Determinism is the single
hardest invariant to preserve here; the goldens lock it down.

title: T6 — replay_bundle Vec::len → streaming ByteCounter (score 5.0)
description:
# Task T6 — replay_bundle: replace Vec::len() after to_vec() with streaming ByteCounter

Parent: bd-98xo5 (epic). Score 5.0. Smallest, cleanest, single-
file change in this epic.

## Background

`replay_bundle_gzip_bench` proves that measuring the serialized
event size via a streaming `ByteCounter` (write-and-count, no
materialised Vec) is **1.83-1.86× faster** than the "to_vec → len"
pattern, AT EVERY SIZE.

Round-1 measurements
(`tests/artifacts/perf/20260520T214003Z_franken_node_perf/criterion_raw/replay_bundle_gzip.txt`):

| Events    | vec_len    | streaming_counter | streaming wins by |
|----------:|-----------:|------------------:|-------------------|
|        10 |   4.98 µs  |   2.71 µs         | 1.84×             |
|       100 |  57.60 µs  |  27.80 µs         | 2.07×             |
|     1 000 | 622.20 µs  | 335.00 µs         | 1.86×             |

## Where the pattern lives

Production must have at least one `Vec::len()` call sitting after
a `serde_json::to_vec(...)` call where the only purpose of the
allocation is to measure size. Grep:

```bash
rg -n 'to_vec\(.*\)\?[.\s\n]*\.len\(\)' crates/franken-node/src/tools/
rg -n 'serde_json::to_vec.*\.len' crates/franken-node/src/tools/replay_bundle.rs
```

The bench's `streaming_counter` variant uses an `io::Write` impl
that counts bytes without storing them. Promote that helper to
`crates/franken-node/src/tools/replay_bundle.rs` (or a small
utilities module).

## Recommended fix shape

```rust
pub struct ByteCounter(pub u64);

impl io::Write for ByteCounter {
    fn write(&mut self, buf: &[u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
        self.0 = self.0.saturating_add(buf.len() as u64);
        Ok(buf.len())
    }
    fn flush(&mut self) -> io::Result<()> { Ok(()) }
}

// Use instead of `to_vec(...)?.len()`:
let mut counter = ByteCounter(0);
serde_json::to_writer(&mut counter, &value)?;
let size = counter.0;
```

Saturating_add is the project convention for counters (see
README cryptographic-primitives + AGENTS.md hardening patterns).

## Equivalence proof

There's nothing to preserve byte-wise — the change drops a
`Vec<u8>` allocation. The behavioural output is identical (the
returned `usize` size IS the same).

## Re-baseline target

Round 4 (after this lands), re-run the bench and confirm the
streaming-counter speedup is now visible at the production call
site (not just the bench-local variant). Hard target: any caller
that today materialises a Vec just to call `.len()` on it must be
gone.

## Tradeoff

There is no real tradeoff. The bench documents the win exists
and the fix is mechanical. The only reason this is rank 6 (not
rank 1) is that the absolute impact is small — replay-bundle
generation runs at most a handful of times per incident.

title: T7 — fleet_transport canonicalize_json_value path-alloc cleanup (score 5.0)
description:
# Task T7 — fleet_transport::canonicalize_json_value: defer path String allocation

Parent: bd-98xo5 (epic). Round-2 REFRAMED finding (was originally
flagged in round 1 as "same hotspot as trust_card" but round-2
static read rejected that hypothesis).

## Background

`canonicalize_json_value` is the canonical encoder for fleet
convergence receipts in
`crates/franken-node/src/control_plane/fleet_transport.rs:154-180`.
The full body:

```rust
fn canonicalize_json_value(value: Value, path: &str) -> Result<Value, FleetTransportError> {
    match value {
        Value::Array(items) => items
            .into_iter()
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(index, item)| canonicalize_json_value(item, &format!("{path}[{index}]")))
            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()
            .map(Value::Array),
        Value::Object(map) => {
            let mut entries = map.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();
            entries.sort_by(|left, right| left.0.cmp(&right.0));
            let mut canonical = serde_json::Map::new();
            for (key, item) in entries {
                canonical.insert(
                    key.clone(),
                    canonicalize_json_value(item, &format!("{path}.{key}"))?,
                );
            }
            Ok(Value::Object(canonical))
        }
        Value::Number(number) if number.is_f64() => Err(FleetTransportError::serialization(
            format!("fleet convergence receipt contains non-deterministic float at {path}"),
        )),
        other => Ok(other),
    }
}
```

## What round 2 confirmed (and rejected)

Round-2 static read confirmed:
- ✓ This function does NOT have the trust_card recursive-clone
  problem. `items.into_iter()` and `map.into_iter()` CONSUME the
  input (no clones).
- ✓ BUT — `format!("{path}[{index}]")` and `format!("{path}.{key}")`
  allocate two new Strings per recursive call. The `path` is used
  ONLY in the float-error branch (L175-177), so on the happy path
  those allocations are pure waste.
- ✓ AND — `let mut canonical = serde_json::Map::new()` has no
  capacity hint, so it grows-and-rehashes as keys are inserted.

Each individual issue is small. Combined per-Value visited:
- 2× `format!()` String allocs ≈ ~50-100 bytes each on a typical
  JSON path (e.g. `"$.zone_id"`).
- 1× IndexMap (serde_json::Map) growth without `with_capacity(N)`.

This is ALLOCATION HYGIENE, not the trust_card Θ(W^N × N) cliff.
Demoted to score 5.0 in the round-2 hotspot table.

## Recommended fix shape

Two complementary moves, in priority order:

1. **Defer the `path` string construction to the error site.**
   Replace the `path: &str` argument with a `path_segments:
   &mut Vec<PathSeg>` (stack-like), where `PathSeg` is an enum
   `{ Key(&str), Index(usize) }`. Push/pop around each recursion
   level. On the float-error branch, render the path String once
   from the segments. On the happy path, NEVER format anything.

   Sketch:

   ```rust
   enum PathSeg<'a> { Key(&'a str), Index(usize) }

   fn canonicalize(value: Value, path: &mut Vec<PathSeg>) -> Result<Value, FleetTransportError> {
       match value {
           Value::Object(map) => {
               let mut entries: Vec<_> = map.into_iter().collect();
               entries.sort_by(|l, r| l.0.cmp(&r.0));
               let mut out = serde_json::Map::with_capacity(entries.len()); // (2)
               for (key, item) in entries {
                   path.push(PathSeg::Key(&key));
                   let value = canonicalize(item, path)?;
                   path.pop();
                   out.insert(key, value);
               }
               Ok(Value::Object(out))
           }
           Value::Number(n) if n.is_f64() => Err(FleetTransportError::serialization(
               format!("fleet convergence receipt contains non-deterministic float at {}", render_path(path)))),
           ...
       }
   }
   ```

2. **Pre-allocate the output Map with `with_capacity(entries.len())`.**
   Avoids `hashbrown` rebucketing on each insert.

## Equivalence proof

The CRITICAL invariant: the error message format from L175-177
("fleet convergence receipt contains non-deterministic float at
{path}") must produce IDENTICAL strings after the change. Today
the path string is something like `"$.zone[0].timestamp"`. The
new `render_path` function must produce exactly that.

The existing inline test
`fleet_convergence_receipt_payload_hash_domain_separation` at
`fleet_transport.rs:3383-3445` exercises the canonical encoder; it
must continue to produce the same canonical bytes (the path is
not on its path, but the canonical_payload is).

Add a new inline test that triggers the float-error branch and
asserts the rendered path string matches the OLD format
byte-for-byte across nested arrays + objects.

## Re-baseline note

There's no Criterion bench for this code today. T7 does NOT
include authoring one (that's deferred to the round-3 bench-gap
task list — and is low value since the function isn't a real
hotspot). Round 4 will rely on the existing unit-test correctness
guards.

## Optional: cross-task amortization with T4

The streaming encoder pattern from T4 (trust_card) applies here too,
if the team wants to consolidate. But trust_card's deep-clone
problem is structurally bigger; this function is fine with the
small fixes above. Recommend keeping them separate so reviewers can
focus.

The recommended fix shape (PathSeg stack + render_path helper + with_capacity at object insertion site + Vec::with_capacity on array allocation) is fully implemented at crates/franken-node/src/control_plane/fleet_transport.rs:154-216. Regression test canonicalize_json_value_float_error_path_matches_legacy_format at fleet_transport.rs:3485 pins the operator-facing error string format ($.zones[0].timestamp). Verified rch exec -- cargo check -p frankenengine-node --tests + cargo fmt --check both clean. Only remaining child bd-98xo5.7.2 is explicitly 'Optional amortisation: share streaming encoder with T4 (consider only after T4 ships)' — T4 (bd-98xo5.4 trust_card structural deep-clone removal) is still OPEN, so .7.2 stays parked until T4 lands and the streaming-encoder share-point exists. Closing the parent now reflects that the round-2 hotspot signal (score 5.0 allocation hygiene) has been fully addressed by .7.1; the optional amortisation is downstream of independent T4 work.

# Task T9 — Round-3 measurement: migration tree-sitter benchmark on real corpora

Parent: bd-98xo5 (epic). Closes the round-2 measurement gap for
the `migration` module's tree-sitter parsing path. Static
hypothesis: tree-sitter parsing of large JS/TS files is in the
hot path of `franken-node migrate audit`; nobody has measured it
at production scale.

## Background

`crates/franken-node/Cargo.toml` declares `tree-sitter` +
`tree-sitter-javascript` as dependencies (see AGENTS.md → "Key
Dependencies" table). They drive:
- `migrate audit` (`franken-node migrate audit ./app`) JS/TS AST
  scanning for migration risk findings.
- conformance / lockstep surface migrations.

Tree-sitter is generally fast (incremental, native-code parser),
but on 100k+ line files it can be a noticeable cost. The
end-to-end test `migrate_cli_e2e` validates correctness but
doesn't expose timing.

## Measurement strategy

1. Source one or two realistic JS corpora:
   - A small project: e.g. a typical npm package's main file
     (≈ 1 000 LOC).
   - A large bundle: e.g. a webpack-style concatenated bundle
     (≈ 50 000 - 100 000 LOC). The OSS world has plenty;
     pick something license-clean.
   Cache fixtures under
   `tests/fixtures/migrate_corpora/` so the bench is reproducible.

2. New bench file
   `crates/franken-node/benches/migrate_tree_sitter_bench.rs`:

   ```rust
   fn bench_audit(c: &mut Criterion) {
       let mut group = c.benchmark_group("migrate_tree_sitter");
       for (name, path) in CORPORA {
           let src = std::fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap();
           group.bench_with_input(BenchmarkId::new("audit", name),
               &src, |b, source| b.iter(|| {
                   black_box(run_audit_on_source(black_box(source)))
               }));
       }
   }
   ```

3. perf record the bench under release-perf; identify the
   dominant cost — parser vs visitor vs allocator.

## Acceptance

A baseline Criterion + perf flat report exists for at least two
input sizes. The hotspot ranking decision is:
- If tree-sitter parse time is < 50 % of total: visitor / output
  formatting is the hot spot; file an optimisation bead.
- If tree-sitter parse time is > 50 %: parsing IS the cost
  (irreducible without grammar work); document the production SLO
  expectation.

## Out of scope

- Authoring a custom JS parser (insane scope).
- Changing the tree-sitter grammar (upstream territory).
- Parallelising migrate audit across files (independent feature
  decision, not a profile finding).

title: [REASONING] QuarantineController is Clone and stores HMAC secret as plain String
description:
LENS: Concurrency / data-flow + secret hygiene
FILE: crates/franken-node/src/security/quarantine_controller.rs:167-187 (struct + new), 398-415 (sign_evidence)
CONCERN: QuarantineController derives #[derive(Debug, Clone)]. The signing_key is held as 'signing_key: String', not a SecretString or zeroizing wrapper. Because the type is Clone, every .clone() silently duplicates the HMAC secret on the heap, and Drop does not zero the previous copies. Debug prints (manual or via panic = trace) will include the secret. There is no internal synchronization, so callers wanting concurrent decide_for_posterior either share an Arc<QuarantineController> (read-only OK) or wrap in Arc<Mutex<...>> (test code at line 1644 does this), but each Mutex acquisition path that Clone's the controller produces an independent copy of the secret.
WHY IT MATTERS: Anti-entropy and other security-critical modules in this codebase already use ct_eq, length-prefixed hashing, and other rigor. Storing the HMAC key for the quarantine signer in a plain String + Clone violates the same hygiene level. Even if no current caller leaks via Debug, a future panic message, tracing::debug!, or test print will exfiltrate the key.
SUGGESTED REMEDIATION: (1) Wrap signing_key in zeroize::Zeroizing<String> or a custom SecretBytes type. (2) Implement Debug manually to print '<signing_key=REDACTED>'. (3) Either remove the Clone derive (force callers to wrap in Arc) or document that Clone duplicates the secret and requires the caller to prove this is acceptable. (4) Add a unit test asserting format!('{:?}', controller) does NOT contain the signing_key bytes.
close_reason: Completed

title: Return QueueTimeout for expired remote bulkhead queue entries
description:
Why this exists:
`crates/franken-node/src/remote/remote_bulkhead.rs` defines `BulkheadError::QueueTimeout`, but `poll_queued()` currently calls `evict_expired_queue_entries()` before looking up the caller's queued request. When the request has already timed out, the front-eviction path removes it first and the method degrades into `UnknownRequest` instead of returning the explicit timeout error promised by the API.

What this bug must do:
1. Preserve timed-out queue entries long enough for `poll_queued()` to classify the caller's own request as `QueueTimeout`.
2. Ensure timed-out requests are still removed from the queue and logged as rejected.
3. Add focused regressions proving a timed-out queued request returns `QueueTimeout` rather than `UnknownRequest`.
4. Run focused Rust validation through `rch` only.

Acceptance criteria:
1. `poll_queued()` returns `BulkheadError::QueueTimeout` for an expired queued request id.
2. Timed-out queue entries are removed and rejection telemetry remains intact.
3. Unknown ids still return `UnknownRequest`.
4. Focused `rch`-offloaded checks/tests for `remote::remote_bulkhead` pass or the remote blocker is documented precisely.
notes: Current tree reread found the timeout-classification fix and focused regressions already present in crates/franken-node/src/remote/remote_bulkhead.rs, so no source edit was needed. Fresh exact rch validation used CARGO_TARGET_DIR=.rch-target-bd-99kid-v1 and cargo test -p frankenengine-node queue_timeout_is_enforced -- --exact --nocapture on worker vmi1264463; it progressed through sync and dependency compile, reached frankenengine-engine, then stayed completely silent across repeated follow-up polls until cancelled locally as another remote closeout blocker reproduction.

title: Add validation proof debt ledger for blocked and retryable proofs
description:
Epic: bd-i9m9u. Builds on recorder, broker status, and recovery planner decisions.

Purpose:
Give swarm operators a compact ledger of validation proofs that are blocked, retryable, source-only, stale, or waiting on capacity, so agents can pick useful follow-up work instead of rediscovering the same RCH blocker.

Scope:
- Define a deterministic ledger view derived from validation broker statuses, recorder artifacts, recovery planner decisions, and bead IDs.
- Group entries by blocker class: worker infra, cargo contention, sibling dependency blocker, disk pressure, stale lease, product compile/test failure, source-only fallback, and proof-cache reuse.
- Include bead id, thread id, requester/owner when known, command digest, latest recorder path, receipt path, next action, freshness, and whether the proof blocks another bead.
- Keep output machine-readable and suitable for doctor/readiness or a future dashboard.

Acceptance:
- Ledger cannot mark retryable worker infra as green proof.
- Ledger distinguishes local product failures from remote infrastructure failures.
- Entries are stable-sorted for deterministic diffs and artifact checks.
- Fixture coverage includes multiple agents and duplicate/coalesced proof attempts.

Verification expected:
- Unit tests for grouping/sorting/freshness.
- Fixture replay test showing multiple beads and agents.
- Contract checker if the ledger writes JSON artifacts.

title: [REALITY] AGENTS.md workspace shape omits crates/franken-security-macros member
description:
CLAIM: AGENTS.md 'Workspace Shape' table (line ~245) and 'Repository Reality Check' section list only two workspace members: 'crates/franken-node/' and 'sdk/verifier/'. The Workspace Shape table explicitly says: 'Cargo.toml | Workspace manifest for crates/franken-node and sdk/verifier'.

REALITY: Root Cargo.toml [workspace].members declares THREE crates: 'crates/franken-node', 'crates/franken-security-macros', 'sdk/verifier'. The franken-security-macros crate is a proc-macro crate (proc-macro = true) that crates/franken-node consumes as a path dependency: 'franken-security-macros = { path = "../franken-security-macros" }' (Cargo.toml line 74). It is not optional and not feature-gated.

FILE: AGENTS.md (Workspace Shape section, table near line 245; Repository Reality Check section near line 21); confirmed against Cargo.toml [workspace].members and crates/franken-node/Cargo.toml line 74.

IMPACT: Agents told via AGENTS.md to treat the workspace as a two-crate shape will not realize that procedural macros live in a third crate, may miss it during audits, and may overlook security-macro changes when reviewing PRs. The 'Key Dependencies' table also omits franken-security-macros entirely.

SUGGESTED FIX: Update AGENTS.md to add crates/franken-security-macros to (a) the Workspace Shape table with a one-line purpose ('proc-macro helpers consumed by frankenengine-node'), (b) the Repository Reality Check primary-crate paragraph, and (c) the Key Dependencies table.

title: Verification harness full run includes guarded clippy gate
description:
## Background
`scripts/verify_all_verification_targets.sh` documents step 4 as `cargo deny / fmt / clippy`, and `bd-rjc2m.3` requires clippy as part of the comprehensive verification gate. The live script only runs cargo-deny and cargo fmt, so a full gate run can omit the clippy proof while still producing a report that appears to include it.

## What
Add the missing clippy guarded gate to `scripts/verify_all_verification_targets.sh`, preserving lockfile-drift protection and report-tail evidence. Add a cheap Python contract test that reads the shell script and fails if the full-run gate loses deny, fmt, or clippy markers again.

## Why
The verification gate must be honest about every advertised validation command. Missing clippy weakens the E2E remediation proof and can let lint regressions escape the final acceptance report.

## How
Append a `run_guarded_gate` invocation for `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` with its own log and lockfile-drift JSON report. Keep cargo-heavy execution behind the script's existing `VERIF_GATE_CARGO_PREFIX` / `rch exec --` prefix. Add a unit test in `tests/test_check_tnr_ci_verification_gate.py` that checks the script contains the guarded deny/fmt/clippy commands.

## Risks
Do not run the full verification script locally; that is intentionally expensive. Validate the script contract and selftest path instead.

## Success Criteria
- Script has a guarded clippy gate with separate log and lockfile-drift JSON paths.
- Python tests cover the full-run gate command contract.
- `python3 tests/test_check_tnr_ci_verification_gate.py` passes.
- `scripts/verify_all_verification_targets.sh --selftest` passes.
- `git diff --check` and `ubs` pass on touched files.
