title: [10.18] Define canonical `ExecutionReceipt` schema and deterministic serialization rules.
description:
## Why This Exists

Section 10.18 implements the Verifiable Execution Fabric (VEF) — Enhancement Map 9L — which provides proof-carrying runtime compliance for franken_node. VEF upgrades trust from replay-based auditing to cryptographic demonstration of policy compliance, a category-defining differentiator under Track C (Trust-Native Ecosystem Layer).

This bead defines the canonical ExecutionReceipt schema — the foundational data structure that every high-risk action emits. Receipts are the atomic unit of evidence in the VEF pipeline: they flow into hash-chained streams (bd-3g4k), get windowed for proof generation (bd-28u0), and are validated by verification gates (bd-1o4v). Without a stable, deterministic, hash-stable receipt format, no downstream VEF component can function correctly.

The receipt schema must capture enough context for cryptographic proof binding (action type, capability context, actor/artifact identity, policy snapshot hash) while remaining efficient enough for hot-path emission in the extension host.

## What This Must Do

1. Define the canonical `ExecutionReceipt` schema with all required fields: action type, capability context, actor identity, artifact identity, policy snapshot hash, monotonic timestamp, sequence number, and witness references.
2. Specify deterministic serialization rules that produce hash-stable output — identical receipt content always serializes to identical bytes regardless of field insertion order, platform, or serializer version.
3. Define canonical hashing algorithm and parameters for receipt content addressing.
4. Specify schema versioning strategy (v1 baseline) with forward-compatibility rules for schema evolution.
5. Produce machine-readable schema definition (`spec/vef_execution_receipt_v1.json`) with JSON Schema or equivalent formal validation.
6. Generate golden test vectors covering all field combinations, edge cases (empty witnesses, maximum-length fields, Unicode in identifiers), and hash stability assertions.
7. Document the schema rationale, field semantics, and serialization contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Receipt schema includes action type, capability context, actor/artifact identity, policy snapshot hash, timestamp/sequence, and witness references; serialization is canonical and hash-stable.
- Serialization is deterministic: identical logical receipts produce identical byte sequences across platforms and serializer implementations.
- Hash stability: re-hashing the same receipt content always produces the same digest.
- Schema validation rejects receipts with missing required fields, invalid types, or out-of-range values with classified error codes.
- Golden vectors pass on all target platforms (Linux x86_64, aarch64 at minimum).
- Schema version field is present and enforced in validation.

## Testing & Logging Requirements

- Unit tests for each receipt field: valid values, boundary values, invalid values (missing, wrong type, overflow).
- Hash stability tests: construct N distinct receipts, serialize, hash, repeat 1000x — all hashes match.
- Cross-platform golden vector tests: committed test vectors with expected serialized bytes and expected hashes.
- Round-trip tests: serialize -> deserialize -> re-serialize produces identical bytes.
- Fuzz tests: random valid receipt construction never produces non-deterministic serialization.
- Schema validation tests: malformed receipts (missing fields, extra fields, wrong types) produce stable error codes.
- Structured logging: `VEF-RECEIPT-001` (receipt created), `VEF-RECEIPT-002` (receipt serialized), `VEF-RECEIPT-ERR-*` (validation failures).
- Trace correlation IDs linking receipt creation to the originating action's execution context.

## Expected Artifacts

- `docs/specs/vef_execution_receipt.md` — schema specification, field semantics, serialization rules, versioning strategy.
- `spec/vef_execution_receipt_v1.json` — machine-readable schema definition with validation rules.
- `artifacts/10.18/vef_receipt_schema_vectors.json` — golden test vectors with expected serialization and hash outputs.
- `artifacts/section_10_18/bd-p73r/verification_evidence.json` — machine-readable CI/release gate evidence.
- `artifacts/section_10_18/bd-p73r/verification_summary.md` — human-readable summary linking intent to measured outcomes.

## Dependencies

- bd-16fq (blocks) — VEF policy-constraint language and compiler contract: receipts must reference policy snapshot hashes and action types defined by the constraint language.

Dependents: bd-3g4k (hash-chained receipt stream), bd-2hjg (section gate), bd-32p (plan-level tracker).
acceptance_criteria: - Receipt schema includes action type, capability context, actor/artifact identity, policy snapshot hash, timestamp/sequence, and witness references; serialization is canonical and hash-stable.

title: [REALITY] Make verify corpus validate corpus semantics
description:
Reality-check gap: `franken-node verify corpus` currently proves that a requested path/name exists under known roots, but the policy-level corpus promises require schema validation, minimum case count, API-family coverage, per-band thresholds, stale-evidence checks, and fail-closed CI semantics.

User outcome: before migration or lockstep gates rely on a compatibility corpus, users should know the corpus is large enough, fresh enough, well-formed, representative, and tied to actual execution evidence. Do not simplify this into a file-exists checker or a docs-only gate; preserve direct path support and named corpus discovery while adding semantic validation.

Implementation requirements:
1. Teach verify corpus to parse supported corpus/report manifests, including artifacts/13/compatibility_corpus_results.json and any canonical corpus manifests used by lockstep.
2. Validate schema version, total case count, per-test identifiers, API-family tags, bands, risk bands, status enums, thresholds, required-family coverage, duplicate IDs, stale timestamps/digests, and linkages to execution/lockstep evidence.
3. Emit structured JSON details for every failed invariant so operators can fix the corpus without reading source.
4. Support explicit modes for corpus-manifest validation and compatibility-report validation, while preserving existing CLI ergonomics for direct paths and names.
5. Make downstream scripts/gates call the stronger verifier or share the same validation library to avoid divergent semantics.

Testing/logging requirements:
- Unit tests for valid corpus, missing file, malformed JSON/TOML, duplicate test IDs, undersized corpus, missing required API family, invalid band/risk tag, stale evidence, threshold regression, and direct-path/named-corpus resolution.
- E2E CLI tests for `franken-node verify corpus <path> --json` success and multiple fail-closed cases, asserting exit codes and machine-readable failure details.
- A script-level regression test that mutates a temporary copy of the compatibility report and proves the gate fails on each important invariant.
- Structured logs/events for corpus_validation_started, corpus_manifest_loaded, corpus_invariant_failed, coverage_summary_emitted, stale_evidence_detected, and corpus_validation_completed; include trace_id, corpus_id, manifest_path, case_count, and coverage summary.
- Verification commands must include rch cargo check/clippy/fmt plus focused verify-corpus Rust tests and relevant Python gate tests.
design:
Design notes for implementation:
- Treat this as the shared corpus-validation foundation for the lockstep and compatibility-report beads; avoid a one-off CLI-only parser. Prefer a reusable Rust validation function plus script/gate adapters so CLI, CI, and report generation use the same invariants.
- Preserve existing direct path and name discovery UX, but separate discovery from validation: discovery finds candidates, validation proves semantics.
- Model outcomes explicitly: PASS, FAIL, ERROR, and UNPROVEN/STALE where appropriate. Do not let a partial artifact become PASS.
- Emit machine-readable invariant IDs so E2E scripts can assert exact failure causes without brittle text matching.
- Keep fixture/test corpora clearly marked; they can prove code paths but must not satisfy release/headline thresholds.
- Good implementation split: manifest/report loader, schema and enum validator, coverage/threshold evaluator, staleness/digest checker, CLI renderer, structured logger, test-fixture builder.
- Estimate: medium-large; finish this before lockstep/compatibility evidence work because it defines their input contract.
acceptance_criteria: PASS requires semantic validation, not path existence. The command fails closed on malformed, undersized, stale, duplicate, threshold-regressed, or coverage-incomplete corpora. Existing path/name workflows still work. JSON output contains invariant-level diagnostics and coverage summaries. Comprehensive unit, E2E, script-level mutation tests, and structured logs are included.
notes:
Second plan-space audit note: Preserve existing `verify corpus` CLI ergonomics and downstream JSON consumers while tightening semantics. If output schemas change, add versioned schema fields, golden JSON tests, and migration/compatibility assertions rather than silently breaking scripts. Treat shared corpus validation as a reusable primitive for lockstep and compatibility report generation; do not fork separate validators. User-facing diagnostics must include exact invariant IDs and remediation hints, not only pass/fail.

Third plan-space audit note: Completion must include failing-first unit tests for every invariant plus mock-free E2E CLI/script tests that write temporary corrupt corpora/reports and assert exit codes, invariant IDs, remediation hints, trace IDs, and detailed structured logs. Do not close from happy-path fixtures alone; release/headline mode must reject fixture-only or degraded evidence.

Fourth plan-space audit note: Make the validation contract explicit enough for users and downstream gate authors: document invariant IDs, severity, authoritative vs diagnostic evidence, remediation hints, and schema-version behavior in generated output or companion docs. If implementation discovers another corpus/report format, add it through the shared validator with tests rather than special-casing a caller. Keep the first implementation slice usable for operators even before lockstep/compat report beads land.

title: Epic: NUMA-aware workspace artifact cache and build-pressure governor
description:
Idea-wizard Phase 2/3 result: the best non-duplicative improvement for massive agent swarms is a workspace-wide artifact cache and pressure governor that understands generated build output, target-dir hotsets, RCH/local cargo contention, disk pressure, memory headroom, and 64+ core/256GB+ hosts.

Why this is distinct: existing idea-wizard beads cover validation proof coalescing, flight records, RCH recovery, and scheduler SLOs. This epic covers the substrate beneath those flows: a safe, observable, NUMA-aware way to share generated artifacts, avoid duplicate target-dir blowups, choose local vs remote execution, and clean stale outputs without deleting source, logs, Beads, Mail, or user/session history.

Success criteria:
- Generated artifacts are inventoried with provenance, ownership, TTL, size, and safety class.
- Build/run admission can decide run-local, offload-through-rch, queue, wait, or refuse-local-fallback from deterministic inputs.
- Cleanup is opt-in, pin-aware, audit-logged, and never deletes source or user data.
- Doctor/readiness output gives agents a stable JSON view of disk, memory, cargo/rustc, RCH, target-dir, and cache pressure.
- Tests include deterministic fixture replay, golden JSON output, and at least one mock-free E2E using real temp target trees and real artifact metadata.

Phase 6 polish notes:
- Do not collapse this into existing validation-broker proof scheduling; it must be workspace-wide and reusable by validation, docs gates, fuzzing, and benchmark lanes.
- Every implementation bead must include bounded-growth checks, explicit caps, and detailed structured logs.
- Cargo-heavy validation must use rch exec; source-only and fixture tests should remain runnable without cargo.

title: Implement generated artifact inventory with pins and safety classes
description:
Purpose: provide a structured inventory for generated build artifacts so agents can reason about cleanup, reuse, provenance, and ownership without ad hoc du/find parsing.

Scope:
- Add a workspace-artifact inventory model in the ops/tooling layer, reusing existing serialization/error patterns.

- All string/list growth is capped.

title: Add workspace build admission and cleanup decision policy
description:
Purpose: turn inventory and pressure signals into deterministic decisions that agents can use before starting expensive work or cleanup.

Scope:
- Implement policy decisions: allow-local, require-rch, queue, wait, refuse-local-fallback, and propose-cleanup-candidates.
- Distinguish validation/proof jobs, fuzzing, benchmark, docs gates, and one-off source-only checks by cost class.
- Include priority inheritance from bead priority and user urgency, but cap queue growth and retry windows.
- Cleanup candidates must be suggestions with audit evidence unless a caller explicitly operates in approved cleanup mode.
- Produce stable diagnostics for why a decision was made and what would change it.

Acceptance:
- Deterministic policy fixtures cover healthy, saturated, disk-warning, memory-warning, RCH-unavailable, corrupt-mail, and pinned-artifact cases.
- Protected classes are never cleanup candidates.
- High-priority source-only work is never blocked by stale build-output cleanup suggestions.
- Policy output includes machine-readable reason codes and human-readable summary.

Verification:
- Unit tests over fixture decisions.
- Golden JSON fixtures for at least six scenarios.
- rch exec for any cargo-heavy validation; otherwise exact blocker recorded.

title: Validation shard planner ignores active cargo pressure
description:
Idea-wizard source-only follow-up from the workspace pressure/resource-governor lane.

Why this exists:
The validation shard planner carries `active_builds` in `ValidationShardRchQueueState`, but `is_saturated()` only checks `workers_available == 0` or `queued_builds > workers_available`. That means a plan can mark RCH cargo shards ready while the local workspace already has many active cargo/rustc processes. This conflicts with the repo operational rule to back off above the cargo/rustc contention threshold and with `ops::rch_adapter::DEFAULT_MAX_ACTIVE_CARGO_PROCESSES` / `RchCommandPolicy::max_active_cargo_processes`, which classify over-threshold launches as `RCH-CONTENTION-DEFERRED`.

Evidence:
- `crates/franken-node/src/ops/validation_planner.rs:768` includes `active_builds` in `ValidationShardRchQueueState`.
- `crates/franken-node/src/ops/validation_planner.rs:811` ignores `active_builds` in `is_saturated()`.
- `crates/franken-node/src/ops/validation_planner.rs:1074` uses that predicate to decide whether RCH cargo shards are Ready or Waiting.
- `crates/franken-node/src/ops/rch_adapter.rs:23` sets `DEFAULT_MAX_ACTIVE_CARGO_PROCESSES` to 2, and `crates/franken-node/src/ops/rch_adapter.rs:746` classifies deferred commands when active cargo/rustc count exceeds the policy threshold.

Required fix:
Make validation shard planning fail closed under over-threshold active cargo/rustc pressure. The planner should mark RCH cargo shards Waiting with a stable reason and blocked_by detail when `active_builds` exceeds the shared active-cargo threshold, even if workers are otherwise available and the RCH queue is short. Keep behavior deterministic and fixture-testable; do not launch cargo in tests.

Acceptance:
- `ValidationShardRchQueueState::is_saturated()` or an equivalent planner gate accounts for active cargo/rustc pressure.
- A focused validation planner test proves a queue with available workers and low queued builds still waits when `active_builds` exceeds the active-cargo threshold.
- Waiting output includes `active_builds` in `blocked_by` so operators know why proof launch was deferred.
- Source-only checks pass (`rustfmt --edition 2024 --check` on touched Rust files, `UBS_SKIP_RUST_BUILD=1 ubs` on touched files, `git diff --check`).
- RCH cargo proof is run through `rch exec` only when cargo/rustc pressure is at or below the repo threshold; otherwise record the exact deferred command as blocker evidence.

Why This Improves User Outcomes:
- "[12] Risk control: topological choke-point false positives" is required to reduce operator error, increase deterministic safety guarantees, and improve time-to-diagnosis for failures in real-world workflows.

acceptance_criteria:
RISK: Over-hardening false positives — security hardening rules are too aggressive, blocking legitimate operations and creating alert fatigue.
IMPACT: Developers disable hardening, legitimate extensions are rejected, operational overhead from investigating false positives.
COUNTERMEASURES:
  (a) Counterfactual simulation: before deploying a new hardening rule, simulate it against historical traffic to measure false-positive rate.
  (b) Expected-loss calibration: each hardening rule has an expected-loss threshold; rules whose false-positive cost exceeds blocked-threat cost are rejected or tuned.
  (c) Staged rollout: new hardening rules deploy in audit-only mode first, then warn mode, then enforce mode.
VERIFICATION:
  1. Counterfactual simulation framework exists and can replay >= 1000 historical operations against a proposed rule.
  2. False-positive rate for any enforced rule is <= 1% (measured on historical data).
  3. Expected-loss calibration: every enforced rule has documented false-positive cost vs blocked-threat cost, with net positive expected value.
  4. Staged rollout: every new rule goes through audit -> warn -> enforce stages with minimum 24h per stage.
TEST SCENARIOS:
  - Scenario A: Propose a rule that would block 5% of legitimate operations; verify counterfactual simulation catches this and rejects enforcement.
  - Scenario B: Deploy a rule in audit mode; verify it logs violations without blocking.
  - Scenario C: Promote a rule from warn to enforce; verify only rules with FP rate <= 1% are promotable.
  - Scenario D: Verify expected-loss calculation: a rule blocking $100/day of legitimate ops to prevent $10/day of threats is flagged as net-negative.

title: Gate bayesian_risk_quarantine behind policy-engine
description:
## Background
A broad RCH cargo-check validation attempt for the current tree reached Cargo execution and failed before useful downstream diagnostics because the bayesian_risk_quarantine integration target imports frankenengine_node::policy::* while the frankenengine-node crate only exports policy behind cfg(feature = "policy-engine"). Several neighboring policy tests in crates/franken-node/Cargo.toml already declare required-features = ["policy-engine"], but bayesian_risk_quarantine does not.

## Goal
Make the Cargo test target feature metadata match its imports so cargo check --all-targets does not schedule this target in a default-feature build that cannot provide the policy module.

## Implementation approach
Edit the existing [[test]] entry for bayesian_risk_quarantine in crates/franken-node/Cargo.toml and add required-features = ["policy-engine"]. Avoid broad manifest reordering or unrelated test-table cleanup.

## Risks and considerations
This should not disable policy coverage; it should make the coverage explicit under the feature that exposes the module. Verify with a focused RCH cargo check for the target under --features policy-engine, then rerun broad cargo check --all-targets through RCH to see whether the original blocker is gone or a new unrelated blocker appears.

## Success criteria

title: [10.4] Implement ecosystem telemetry for trust and adoption metrics.
description:
## Why This Exists

The extension ecosystem generates trust and adoption signals that must be measured, tracked, and acted upon. Ecosystem telemetry provides the quantitative feedback loop that drives reputation scoring, certification decisions, policy tuning, and program success measurement (Section 13 targets). Without telemetry, the ecosystem operates blind: trust claims cannot be validated, adoption cannot be measured, and emerging threats cannot be detected early.

This bead implements the telemetry pipeline specifically for trust and adoption metrics in the extension ecosystem. It complements the per-extension trust card (bd-2yh) by providing aggregate, ecosystem-level views: how many extensions are at each certification level? What is the average time-to-quarantine? How quickly are revocations propagating? What is the adoption curve for new trust features?

## What This Must Do

1. Define the ecosystem telemetry schema: trust metrics (certification level distribution, revocation propagation latency, quarantine-to-resolution time, provenance coverage rate, reputation distribution) and adoption metrics (extensions published per period, extensions using each provenance level, operator trust-card query volume, policy override frequency).
2. Implement telemetry collection pipeline: privacy-respecting aggregation from node-level events to ecosystem-level metrics. Must respect operator privacy preferences and comply with the privacy envelope from 10.19.
3. Implement telemetry storage with time-series retention policy (granular recent data, aggregated historical data).
4. Implement telemetry query API for dashboards, operator copilot, and policy engines.
5. Implement anomaly detection on telemetry streams: sudden drops in provenance coverage, spikes in quarantine events, or reputation distribution shifts may indicate ecosystem-level attacks.
6. Implement telemetry export for program success criteria measurement (Section 13): compatibility corpus pass rate, migration velocity, compromise reduction metrics.
7. Define telemetry data governance: what is collected, what is aggregated, what is retained, and what is published.
8. Implement telemetry dashboards or dashboard-ready data endpoints for ecosystem health monitoring.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Telemetry schema covers all defined trust and adoption metric families.
- Telemetry collection is opt-in with clear data governance documentation.
- Privacy-preserving aggregation is verified: no individual extension or operator data leaks through aggregate metrics.
- Anomaly detection triggers on at least 5 defined ecosystem-level threat patterns.
- Telemetry query API supports time-range queries, aggregation levels, and metric filtering.
- Telemetry export produces machine-readable artifacts compatible with Section 13 success criteria measurement.
- Telemetry pipeline has bounded resource consumption (CPU, memory, storage) with configurable limits.

## Testing & Logging Requirements

- Unit tests: telemetry aggregation correctness, privacy filter validation, anomaly detection threshold logic, time-series retention policy.
- Integration tests: event ingestion -> aggregation -> query pipeline, anomaly detection trigger -> alert emission.
- E2E tests: simulated ecosystem activity -> telemetry collection -> dashboard data -> anomaly detection.
- Adversarial tests: telemetry poisoning (injecting false metrics), privacy leakage through aggregate queries (differential privacy attacks), resource exhaustion through telemetry flooding.
- Structured logs: TELEMETRY_INGESTED, TELEMETRY_AGGREGATED, TELEMETRY_QUERY_SERVED, TELEMETRY_ANOMALY_DETECTED (with anomaly type and severity), TELEMETRY_EXPORT_GENERATED, TELEMETRY_PRIVACY_FILTER_APPLIED. All with trace IDs.

## Expected Artifacts

- `docs/specs/section_10_4/bd-phf_contract.md` — ecosystem telemetry spec
- `src/supply_chain/ecosystem_telemetry.rs` — Rust types for telemetry pipeline
- `scripts/check_ecosystem_telemetry.py` — verification script with `--json` and `self_test()`
- `tests/test_check_ecosystem_telemetry.py` — unit tests for verification script
- `artifacts/section_10_4/bd-phf/verification_evidence.json` — CI/release gate evidence
- `artifacts/section_10_4/bd-phf/verification_summary.md` — outcome summary

## Dependencies

- No section-internal blockers (this is a cross-cutting telemetry layer).
- Blocks: bd-261k (section gate), bd-1xg (plan tracker)
acceptance_criteria:
1. Telemetry schema captures ecosystem-level metrics: extension install/uninstall rates, trust-level distribution across installed extensions, quarantine frequency, revocation event rates, certification level distribution, and publisher reputation tier distribution.
2. Adoption funnel metrics: discovery -> install -> activate -> retain, with per-extension and aggregate views.
3. Trust health metrics: percentage of extensions at each certification level, mean time from quarantine to resolution, revocation propagation latency percentiles, and stale-attestation rates.
4. Telemetry data is privacy-preserving: no personally identifiable information is collected. Extension-level metrics are aggregated to publisher level or above before export. Local-only mode is the default; opt-in for remote telemetry.
5. Telemetry export formats: machine-readable JSON for automated consumption, and human-readable summary via CLI `franken-node ecosystem stats`.
6. Metric namespace follows the stable namespace convention from 10.13 (bd-1ugy): all ecosystem metrics use the `fnode.ecosystem.*` prefix with versioned schema.
7. Telemetry retention policy: local telemetry retained for configurable period (default 90 days); older data is summarized into aggregate snapshots before pruning.
8. Dashboard-ready: telemetry output includes all fields needed to populate a trust-health dashboard without additional transformation.
9. All telemetry operations emit structured log events: TELEMETRY_COLLECTED, TELEMETRY_EXPORTED, TELEMETRY_PRUNED with metric counts and trace IDs.

title: SaaS security audit: unauthenticated trust card API mutations allow unauthorized state changes
description:
**SAAS SECURITY AUDIT: UNAUTHENTICATED TRUST CARD API VULNERABILITIES**

**Critical Finding:** Trust card API handlers lack authentication and authorization controls, allowing unauthorized state mutations.

**1. trust_card_routes.rs:94** - `create_trust_card()` unauthenticated mutation  
**Exploit:** `POST /api/trust-cards` with arbitrary trust card data → creates unauthorized trust cards  
**Impact:** Attacker can inject malicious trust cards into the registry  
**Fix:** Add `identity: &AuthIdentity, trace: &TraceContext` params + `enforce_handler_contract()` call

**2. trust_card_routes.rs:124** - `update_trust_card()` unauthenticated mutation  
**Exploit:** `PUT /api/trust-cards/{id}` with arbitrary mutation → modifies existing trust cards  
**Impact:** Attacker can corrupt/disable legitimate trust cards  
**Fix:** Add `identity: &AuthIdentity, trace: &TraceContext` params + `enforce_handler_contract()` call

**3. trust_card_routes.rs:154** - `get_trust_card()` unauthenticated read  
**Exploit:** `GET /api/trust-cards/{id}` → leaks trust card details  
**Impact:** Information disclosure of trust card configurations  
**Fix:** Add authentication params + authorization check

**4. trust_card_routes.rs:183** - `list_trust_cards()` unauthenticated enumeration  
**Exploit:** `GET /api/trust-cards` → enumerates all trust cards  
**Impact:** Complete registry disclosure + reconnaissance  
**Fix:** Add authentication params + authorization check

**Pattern:** All trust card handlers miss the standard auth pattern used elsewhere:
```rust
// Missing pattern:
pub fn handler(identity: &AuthIdentity, trace: &TraceContext, ...) -> Result<...> {
    enforce_handler_contract(identity, trace, "METHOD", "/path")?;
    // handler logic
}
```

**Severity:** Critical - unauthenticated state mutations violate fundamental SaaS security principles.

title: [REVIEW] verifier sdk: mismatched trust anchors bypass structural-only guardrail
description:
Module: sdk/verifier/src/lib.rs

Finding:
`VerifierSdk::verify_trust_state()` now returns a signed `VerificationResult` with `VerificationVerdict::Fail` when the caller supplies a mismatched `anchor_integrity_hash`, instead of preserving the structural-only `UnauthenticatedStructuralBundle` guardrail. The same method still fails closed for a matching anchor.

Why this is a real bug:
- Structural replay bundles are supposed to remain unauthenticated; `verify_migration_artifact()` and `execute_workflow()` both reject them with `UnauthenticatedStructuralBundle`.
- `verify_trust_state()` can now be coerced into producing an appendable/session-recordable facade result simply by passing any wrong anchor hash.
- That lets callers convert an otherwise blocked structural bundle into a signed result artifact by lying about the expected anchor, which undermines the guardrail the API advertises.

Repro:
1. Build a same-verifier structural replay bundle.
2. Call `verify_trust_state(&state, &"0".repeat(64))`.
3. Observe it returns `Ok(VerificationResult { verdict: Fail, ... })` with a failed `trust_anchor_matches_integrity_hash` assertion instead of `Err(UnauthenticatedStructuralBundle { .. })`.
4. The returned result can then flow into other facade APIs that accept in-process `VerificationResult`.

Evidence:
- `sdk/verifier/src/lib.rs` returns `build_result(...)` on mismatch around the `trust_anchor_matches_integrity_hash` assertion path.
- `sdk/verifier/tests/conformance_harness.rs:1569` still encodes the fail-closed structural-only contract for `verify_trust_state`.

Suggested fix:
Keep the mismatch signal, but do not return a reusable facade result for structural bundles. Either return `UnauthenticatedStructuralBundle` in all structural-only cases, or split out a non-reusable diagnostic type that cannot be mistaken for an authenticated facade result.

title: Add fenced work-stealing for stale validation proof producers
description:
## Scope
Add a fenced work-stealing protocol for stale validation proof producers. This builds on proof coalescer lease state and flight recorder stale-progress evidence.

## Required behavior
- A waiter may steal only when lease freshness, heartbeat age, recorder stale-progress evidence, and timeout budget all satisfy the contract.
- Stealing must create a new fence token and preserve the previous producer, lease id, stale reason, and recorder artifact path.
- Completed stale output from the old producer must not be trusted unless it matches the fresh fence and proof work key.
- The protocol must distinguish abandoned producer, slow-but-live producer, corrupted lease, and worker-infra timeout.
- Agent Mail/bead closeout text should be able to cite the stealing decision without reading terminal history.

## Acceptance
- Tests cover active lease wait, stale lease steal, old producer finishes late, corrupted lease fail-closed, and proof-cache handoff after steal.
- No stale output can overwrite or satisfy the new fenced proof.
- Operator output names old producer, new producer, bead id, lease path, fence token digest, and required action.

## Verification expected
- Focused proof coalescer/recovery tests through `rch exec -- cargo test -p frankenengine-node <target>` if Rust code changes.
- Fixture checker for any checked-in lease/recorder artifacts.

title: [AUDIT-LOGIC] concurrent migration protection gap - multiple migration pipelines can interfere without coordination
description:
**Logic Gap**: Migration pipeline lacks explicit concurrency controls to prevent multiple migration processes from interfering with each other.

**Flow Breakdown**:
1. **Pipeline Creation**: new() creates PipelineState with cohort_id and idempotency_key but no locking mechanism (line 616 in migration_pipeline.rs)
2. **Stage Progression**: advance() operates on PipelineState without checking for concurrent operations
3. **Rollback Operations**: rollback() can be called without coordination with other active migrations
4. **Receipt Issuance**: No protection against multiple pipelines issuing conflicting receipts

**Gap**: No mutex, file locking, or coordination mechanism prevents multiple migration pipelines from:
- Operating on overlapping extension sets
- Creating conflicting rollback states  
- Racing during verification/execution phases
- Interfering with shared system resources

**Attack Scenario**:
1. Migration A starts for extension set {X, Y}
2. Migration B starts for extension set {Y, Z} (overlapping extension Y)
3. Migration A reaches execution, modifies extension Y state
4. Migration B verification runs with stale pre-Migration-A evidence for Y
5. Both migrations proceed with conflicting assumptions about extension Y
6. System state becomes inconsistent across extension boundaries

**Impact**: Race conditions between concurrent migrations can lead to inconsistent system state, verification bypasses, and conflicting rollback states.
close_reason: ff2f8d90 concurrent migration protection implemented via ACTIVE_MIGRATIONS global registry (migration_pipeline.rs:38-73 check_and_register_migration + lines 664,796,827 registration/cleanup). Fail-closed semantics: only one migration at a time. Tests: test_concurrent_migration_protection_blocks_second_pipeline verifies blocking, test_migration_rollback_releases_concurrency_lock verifies cleanup on rollback.

title: [10.14] Map remote/control tasks to lane-aware scheduler classes with priority policies.
description:
## Why This Exists

The 9J enhancement maps require that all control-plane and remote-effect workloads run under explicit scheduling discipline to prevent priority inversion, lane starvation, and uncontrolled resource consumption. Without lane-aware scheduling, a flood of low-priority remote tasks can starve critical epoch transitions or marker writes, violating runtime invariant #7 (epoch barriers must complete within bounded time). This bead establishes the foundational scheduler classification that all downstream lane-policy consumers (10.15 lane mapping, 10.11 product integration) depend on. It directly supports invariant #9 (deterministic verification gates) by making task classification auditable and telemetry-backed.

## What This Must Do

1. Define a `SchedulerLane` enum covering at minimum: `ControlCritical`, `RemoteEffect`, `Maintenance`, `Background`, each with configurable priority weight and concurrency cap.
2. Implement a `LaneMappingPolicy` that maps incoming task types (identified by `TaskClass` discriminant) to scheduler lanes based on declarative policy configuration.
3. Enforce lane starvation detection: if any lane has zero completions within a configurable time window while tasks are queued, emit a `LANE_STARVED` alert event with lane ID, queue depth, and elapsed time.
4. Enforce misclassification detection: reject tasks whose `TaskClass` does not match any policy rule and emit `LANE_MISCLASS` event with task metadata.
5. Expose lane telemetry counters: `lane_active_count`, `lane_queued_count`, `lane_completed_total`, `lane_starvation_events`, per-lane latency histograms.
6. Produce a spec document defining the lane model, priority semantics, starvation thresholds, and configuration schema.
7. Produce a conformance test that validates lane assignment correctness, starvation detection firing, and misclassification rejection under controlled load.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Task classes are mapped to lanes by policy; lane starvation and misclassification checks are enforced; lane telemetry is exposed.
- Given 4+ task classes, each maps to exactly one lane per policy; no task class maps to zero lanes.
- Starvation detection fires within 2x the configured starvation window when a lane is blocked.
- Misclassification rejection returns a typed error with the unrecognized `TaskClass` value.
- Telemetry counters increment correctly under concurrent load (verified via test harness).
- Policy changes take effect without restart (hot-reload path exists and is tested).

## Testing & Logging Requirements

- Unit tests: lane assignment for each task class; starvation timer triggers on blocked lane; misclassification rejection for unknown task class; policy reload applies new mapping.
- Integration tests: concurrent multi-lane load with starvation injection; lane fairness under skewed workloads; telemetry accuracy under >1000 tasks.
- Conformance tests: `tests/conformance/lane_mapping_enforcement.rs` -- normative test covering all policy rules and edge cases.
- Structured logs: `LANE_ASSIGN` (task_id, task_class, lane_id), `LANE_STARVED` (lane_id, queue_depth, elapsed_ms), `LANE_MISCLASS` (task_class, rejection_reason), `LANE_METRICS` (periodic telemetry snapshot). All events carry trace correlation IDs.

## Expected Artifacts

- `docs/specs/lane_mapping_policy.md` -- specification of lane model, priority semantics, configuration schema
- `tests/conformance/lane_mapping_enforcement.rs` -- normative conformance tests
- `artifacts/10.14/lane_mapping_metrics.csv` -- telemetry snapshot from conformance run

- `artifacts/section_10_14/bd-qlc6/verification_summary.md` -- human-readable verification summary

## Dependencies

- Upstream: bd-v4l0 (global remote bulkhead with `remote_max_in_flight`) -- provides the concurrency envelope this bead subdivides into lanes.
- Downstream: bd-3epz (section-wide verification gate), bd-cuut (10.15 lane mapping for control-plane workloads), bd-lus (10.11 product integration of scheduler lanes), bd-5rh (section gate).

title: [bd-qlc6] Detect queued-lane starvation before first completion
description:
Why this exists:
`crates/franken-node/src/runtime/lane_scheduler.rs` only reports starvation when `last_completion_ms` is `Some(...)`. That means a lane that immediately saturates, queues additional work, and then stays blocked past the starvation window is treated as non-starved forever until the first completion happens. `tests/conformance/control_lane_policy.rs::starvation_detected_when_lane_idle_too_long` expects the opposite behavior: queued Background work should be reported as starved after the window elapses even if the lane has never completed a task yet.

What this bug must do:
- make starvation detection use a stable baseline for lanes with queued work but no completion history yet
- keep the implementation fail-closed and deterministic
- update inline/unit/conformance coverage so the never-completed queued case is treated as starved after the configured window instead of silently ignored

Acceptance criteria:
1. `LaneScheduler::check_starvation` reports starvation for a queued lane after the configured window even if the lane has never completed a task.
2. The scheduler records accurate starvation telemetry and audit evidence for that case.
3. Inline tests in `runtime/lane_scheduler.rs` and the existing conformance expectation in `tests/conformance/control_lane_policy.rs` agree on the same behavior.
4. Validation uses `rch` for cargo-heavy checks only.
notes:

- added `first_queued_at_ms` to track when queued work began waiting

- inline tests now cover pre-window no-starvation, queued-before-first-completion starvation, and audit evidence

description:
**Parent design**: `docs/specs/crypto_trait_abstraction.md` (bd-18dd1, closed 2026-04-27), Phase 3 ("Security Hardening").

**Scope.** After bd-dwx4l, bd-acvur, bd-lbnkf land (the three consumer migrations), audit every crypto call site for:
1. Constant-time comparison invariant — every signature/hash equality check goes through `security::constant_time::ct_eq{,_bytes}`.
2. Domain-separator coverage — every signature preimage starts with a stable, schema-versioned domain string.
3. Length-prefixed canonical inputs — every variable-length field is `u64::to_le_bytes` length-prefixed before the bytes.
4. Saturating arithmetic — every counter/sequence/timestamp in the crypto paths.

**New fuzz harnesses to land.**
- `fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_crypto_scheme_roundtrip.rs` — arbitrary keypair + arbitrary domain + arbitrary message must satisfy `verify(sign(x)) == true`.
- `fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_crypto_scheme_cross_domain.rs` — different domains must produce different signatures.
- `fuzz/fuzz_targets/fuzz_crypto_signer_chain.rs` — chained signers must not leak prior signatures' state.

**Performance benchmark.** Add `crypto_scheme_bench` under `[[bench]]` in `crates/franken-node/Cargo.toml` comparing trait-mediated signing/verifying against direct `ed25519_dalek` calls. The spec asserts zero-cost abstraction; the bench is the proof.

**Depends on.** bd-dwx4l (adds the `sign_raw`/`verify_raw` API), bd-acvur (remote_cap migration), bd-lbnkf (replay_bundle migration). The audit is only meaningful once consumer migrations are complete.

**Done when.**
- All four invariant audits pass with `cargo test`.
- All three fuzz targets run successfully for at least 60s without finding a crash.
- The `crypto_scheme_bench` Criterion report shows wrapper-trait overhead is within 5% of direct `ed25519_dalek` calls.
- The bead-spec's Phase 3 section in `docs/specs/crypto_trait_abstraction.md` is updated with the audit + bench artifact paths.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
BLOCKER discovered (CrimsonCrane 2026-07-11, after closing bd-bg2hy) — supersedes the producer-design assumption in my earlier scoping notes.

The earlier notes assumed `ltv attest` can straightforwardly build a `LongTermVerificationEvidence` and `ltv verify-as-of` can call `VerifierSdk::verify_as_of_ltv`. Reading the code end-to-end, that path is BLOCKED by two facts:

1. `frankenengine-verifier-sdk` is a DEV-DEPENDENCY ONLY of franken-node (crates/franken-node/Cargo.toml:181, under [dev-dependencies]). The product BINARY (main.rs) does not link it, so it cannot call `verify_as_of_ltv` (sdk/verifier/src/lib.rs:1021) at runtime today.

2. EVERY construction helper for the SDK evidence is PRIVATE (`fn`, reachable only from the SDK's own #[cfg(test)]): long_term_artifact_marker_hash (:3050), long_term_marker_leaf_hash (:3105), long_term_merkle_root_from_leaf_hashes (:3137), compute_long_term_reattestation_hash (:3060), compute_long_term_witness_content_hash (:3072), long_term_threshold_signing_message (:3168). There is NO public builder and NO product-side producer of `LongTermVerificationEvidence`. The only assembler is the test-only `reference_long_term_verification_evidence` (:3983).

Consequence: the product-side `control_plane::mmr_proofs` types the harness ltv_leg uses (MmrCheckpoint / MmrRootReattestationChain / MmrRootWitnessReceipt) are a DIFFERENT type family from the SDK's `LongTerm*` DTOs. The harness leg NEVER calls verify_as_of_ltv — it exercises product-side reattestation + witness anteriority in-process. So `verify_as_of_ltv` is currently exercised ONLY by SDK-internal tests with the private reference builder.

Also: the bead text says "emits FN-LTV-001/002", but those exact codes do not exist. The SDK defines FN_LTV_VERIFY_AS_OF_COMPLETED / FN_LTV_WITNESS_ANTERIORITY_PROVEN / FN_LTV_BACKDATING_REJECTED / FN_LTV_HYBRID_SURVIVED_ALGO_DEATH (sdk/verifier/src/lib.rs:139-145) as string constants, not FN-LTV-NNN. New product-side FN-LTV-* codes would need registration in docs/observability/tnr_event_metrics_registry.{json,md} (check_tnr_observability_contract.py is the authority; scan roots = crates/franken-node/src + scripts).

TWO clean resolutions (pick one — this is the design decision that must be settled first):

Option A (RECOMMENDED — keeps LTV crypto in one place, gate-safe): promote the SDK's reference builder to a PUBLIC constructor, e.g. `pub fn build_long_term_evidence_from_parts(artifact, suite_records, inclusion_proof, reattestation_chain, witness_receipt) -> LongTermVerificationEvidence` (or a higher-level `build_from_bundle`), and make `frankenengine-verifier-sdk` a REGULAR dependency of franken-node. `ltv attest` derives MMR leaves from the verified bundle's receipt-chain hashes + integrity hash, re-attests, cosigns with real threshold keys, and calls the public builder; `ltv verify-as-of` calls verify_as_of_ltv. Verifier-independence is preserved (that property is "the verifier need not depend on the PRODUCT", not "the product must not depend on the SDK" — the product already produces artifacts the SDK verifies).

Option B (avoids a product->SDK runtime dep): keep the CLI purely on the PRODUCT-side mmr_proofs + evidence_ledger types (the harness ltv_leg IS the template), define product-side FN-LTV-001/002, and DO NOT touch the SDK LTV path. This gives an operator CLI leg for reattestation/witness/anteriority but does NOT exercise verify_as_of_ltv — the SDK LTV path stays SDK-test-only. Weaker (no offline SDK re-derivation of the LTV claim from the CLI), but zero architectural change and zero duplication.

Recommendation: Option A. It is the only one that gives the master pipeline a CLI leg that ends in an offline SDK verify_as_of_ltv (the whole point of the bead), and it keeps all LTV hashing in the SDK (no duplicate-implementation-gate violation). Cost: one small public SDK API addition + moving frankenengine-verifier-sdk from [dev-dependencies] to [dependencies] (feature-gate it under verifier-tools if binary size matters). Then: new `ltv attest`/`ltv verify-as-of` clap subcommands, cli_subcommand_goldens re-bless (new top-level subcommand changes --help; incident_help snapshot pattern), and replace the harness in-process ltv_leg with a CLI leg.

Cross-refs: sdk/verifier/src/lib.rs (LongTerm* types :414-542, verify_as_of_ltv :1021, private builders :3050-3200, reference builder :3983), control_plane/mmr_proofs.rs (product mmr_root_reattestation + witness fns), observability/evidence_ledger.rs:1696 (append_mmr_root_witness_receipt), crates/franken-node/tests/tnr_full_pipeline_e2e.rs ltv_leg (:544).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: DESIGN DECISION ADOPTED (CrimsonCrane 2026-07-11): Option A, per the recommendation in the 18:36 blocker note. The orchestrating user reviewed the blocker handoff and directed continued execution of the remaining beads in optimal logical order without overriding the recommendation; bd-rgkd2 is the sole blocker of P1 epic bd-f5b04.8, so proceeding with Option A: (1) promote the SDK's private LTV evidence construction helpers to a public builder API in frankenengine-verifier-sdk (keeps all LTV crypto in one place — no duplicate-implementation-gate violation); (2) move frankenengine-verifier-sdk from [dev-dependencies] to [dependencies] of frankenengine-node (unconditional, NOT feature-gated: the tnr master pipeline drives the default-features binary, so the ltv CLI leg must exist in default builds; the SDK is small and has no heavy transitive deps); (3) add 'ltv attest' / 'ltv verify-as-of' subcommands; (4) register product-side FN-LTV-001/002 in the TNR observability registry; (5) re-bless cli_subcommand_goldens; (6) replace the tnr harness in-process ltv_leg with a CLI leg. Verifier independence is preserved: the SDK still depends on nothing product-side.

title: EPIC: Verification-scaffolding integrity remediation (conformance+SDK+fuzz API-drift, ~68 targets) + recurrence-prevention gate
description:
STRATEGY (gauntlet Round-0). franken_node implementation is strong, but its VERIFICATION SCAFFOLDING silently drifted from rapid API evolution across all three layers: 23/264 conformance [[test]] targets, 45/146 fuzz targets, and the verifier-SDK lib-tests do not compile (~68 targets). Same systemic API-drift (crate rename franken_node->frankenengine_node; renamed fields/methods/variants; fallible-constructor changes). Because cargo aborts the whole build on any non-compiling target, those contracts have been UNVERIFIED and the suite cannot run. NOT a security defect; a provable-assurance / coverage-integrity blocker.

This epic is decomposed into children (see dependency tree). Ordering:
1. FOUNDATION (.A): in-repo API-drift remediation guide + shared remediation test-harness + structured JSONL logging schema — every remediation bead logs through it.
2. RECURRENCE-PREVENTION (.G1, P0): a CI compile-census gate so a non-compiling test/fuzz target can NEVER again silently drop coverage. THE key improvement for users.
3. REMEDIATION: conformance clusters (.C1-.C4), fuzz clusters (.FZ1-.FZ5), SDK (.SDK1) — apply the dictionary, fix per-target drift, and CRITICALLY preserve every harness assertion (MUST/SHOULD checks) — do NOT delete or weaken tests to force a compile (cf. title: [.LOCKDRIFT] Make validation fail fast when cargo metadata or gates mutate Cargo.lock
description:
Context: A cargo-deny/cargo metadata validation pass left `Cargo.lock` dirty on 2026-06-06 before a fully successful repo-wide RCH check could be proven. Lockfile mutation during validation is a trust problem: it can hide dependency resolution changes inside a gate that operators expect to be read-only.

Scope:
- Identify validation scripts/gates that run cargo metadata, cargo-deny, or cargo commands capable of refreshing `Cargo.lock`.
- Ensure validation paths either use `--locked` where cargo supports it or explicitly snapshot and report lockfile drift as a fail-closed condition.
- Add structured output that names the command, files changed, and exact next action instead of silently leaving the workspace dirty.
- Do not revert or overwrite the current `Cargo.lock` without explicit user approval; this bead is about making future validation behavior deterministic.

Acceptance:
- Tests or script-level checks prove a synthetic lockfile drift is detected and reported with a non-zero result.
- Happy-path tests prove validation succeeds without changing `Cargo.lock`.
- Human and JSON output include the command and changed path list.
- UBS passes on changed files.
- Final validation uses `rch exec -- cargo fmt --check`, `rch exec -- cargo check --all-targets`, `rch exec -- cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, or records the first hard RCH blocker if worker infra is unavailable.

title: Verification harness records aborting cargo test logs as RED evidence
description:
## Background
The comprehensive verification harness turns full cargo/fuzz/SDK runs into remediation-log-v1 JSONL. Today `parse_cargo_test_output` only emits records when a target reaches a `test result:` line. If `cargo test` aborts during compile/link/setup before any target result, the JSONL can be empty and the operator loses concrete RED evidence for the failed command.

## What
Teach `scripts/parse_cargo_test_results.py` to emit a deterministic RED `RemediationRecord` when cargo output contains an aborting compile/build/setup failure and no per-target test records were parsed. Cover at least `could not compile`, `error: test failed`, and linker/build-script style cargo abort text without falsely marking successful no-test output green.

## Why
The E2E verification gate is supposed to be an honesty mechanism. Empty or under-specified evidence makes failures harder to triage and weakens the final remediation report.

## How
Keep the parser pure. Add a small helper that derives one synthetic target name from the layer, records `compiles=false`, `ran=false`, `errors_after=1`, `tests_run=0`, `tests_passed=0`, and a concise note containing the first useful cargo error line. Add unit tests for compile abort, test binary abort, and benign empty/no-result output.

## Risks
Do not duplicate RED records when normal per-target records already exist. Do not treat a cargo log that simply has no tests as a compile failure unless it contains explicit abort markers.

## Success Criteria
- Parser unit tests cover green targets, failed target results, ignored tests, fuzz failures, cargo compile aborts, cargo test binary aborts, and benign no-result output.
- `scripts/verify_all_verification_targets.sh --selftest` passes.
- `ubs` and `git diff --check` pass on touched files.

Implemented the verification-harness abort evidence fallback.

- `scripts/test_parse_cargo_test_results.py` now covers compile aborts, test-binary aborts, benign no-result output, and the no-duplicate case when normal target records already exist.

title: [VALAUTO] Epic: Validation autopilot for no-ready agent swarms
description:
## Background
The current live tracker state has no br-ready work and no in-progress beads to revive, while bv still surfaces blocked epics and RCH/cross-repo lanes. Recent no-ready tooling can classify this state, but operators and agents still need a higher-level autopilot that turns the evidence into the next safe, concrete action without communication purgatory or false claims.

## Goal
Create a validation-autopilot package that consumes br ready/list, bv robot outputs, blocked-bead freshness evidence, RCH evidence-normalizer records, Agent Mail handoff context, and repo runbook policy, then emits a deterministic next-action plan: claim a ready bead, refresh a stale blocker, create a narrow follow-up bead, retry RCH under a bounded policy, or produce an operator handoff.

## Non-Goals
Do not bypass blocked bead state, do not auto-close beads, do not run bare bv, do not run local cargo/build/test outside rch, and do not invent compatibility shims for product code.

## Success Criteria
The child graph contains a ready contract/design bead, implementation beads with explicit dependencies, fixture-backed unit and e2e coverage, operator documentation, and closeout evidence requirements. The final implementation should reduce repeated no-ready stalls by producing auditable, low-conflict next actions.

comments.text: DISCOVERED 2026-06-24 (CrimsonCrane) while completing bd-201vt (.c callback form). title: dispatch_run exits the PROCESS (127) on RequestedRuntimeUnavailable — kills test harnesses and embedders; test_native_engine_error_handling_propagation aborts the whole native_engine_compat suite on machines without a resolvable franken-engine binary
description: Found 2026-07-10 by CrimsonCrane while fixing bd-4f4f0. engine_dispatcher.rs dispatch_run: 'Err(DispatchResolutionError::RequestedRuntimeUnavailable(error)) => { eprintln!; std::process::exit(127); }' — a LIBRARY function terminating the process is a CLI-ism buried in the ops layer. Concrete damage: crates/franken-node/tests/native_engine_compat.rs test_native_engine_error_handling_propagation constructs EngineDispatcher::new(None, PreferredRuntime::FrankenEngine) and calls dispatch_run; on any machine where no candidate franken-engine binary resolves (e.g. rch workers, clean checkouts without a built sibling engine target), resolution returns RequestedRuntimeUnavailable and the TEST HARNESS PROCESS exits 127 mid-suite — every test after it silently never runs ('test exited abnormally'). Reproduced: cargo test --test native_engine_compat error_handling => exit 127 with empty/truncated output, both at HEAD and pre-qr5i2. FIX SHAPE: dispatch_run should return a typed error (ActionableError) and main.rs should map it to exit 127 at the CLI boundary (contract preserved — bd-4f4f0's rewritten test_native_engine_missing_binary_error_handling already asserts the CLI-level 127 via subprocess, so it keeps guarding the operator contract through the refactor); then make the propagation test hermetic (explicit temp engine placeholder like the other native tests) so it stops depending on host PATH/candidate state.
close_reason: Fixed via 4828be4b4: EngineDispatcher::dispatch_run no longer terminates the process on RequestedRuntimeUnavailable — the arm at crates/franken-node/src/ops/engine_dispatcher.rs:1275 now returns the typed error (DispatchResolutionError made pub) and the CLI boundary in main.rs run arm downcasts it, printing the identical actionable message and exiting 127 there (operator contract still pinned by test_native_engine_missing_binary_error_handling via real subprocess). New regression test test_requested_runtime_unavailable_returns_typed_error_in_process pins the in-process Err + downcast seam — the exact call that previously killed the whole harness. test_native_engine_error_handling_propagation and test_native_engine_execution_with_telemetry made hermetic via explicit fixture engine placeholders (host PATH/candidate state can no longer mask or abort them). Un-hidden latent failure also fixed: test_engine_timeout_handling_with_fixture_binary gated cfg(not(engine)) per the bd-4f4f0 sibling convention (subprocess timeout path only exists without the engine feature; suite death had masked it). bd-fmhij FIXME updated honestly (exit-seam fixed; still gated pending bd-yom8c env-injection seam). Validation: cargo test -p frankenengine-node --test native_engine_compat => 14/14 green where the suite previously exited 127 with truncated output; clippy -D warnings clean; no-engine lane compiles; fmt clean.

title: [12] Risk control: compatibility illusion
description:
Master Plan Source: PLAN_TO_CREATE_FRANKEN_NODE.md
Section: 12 — Risk Register
Risk: Compatibility Illusion (Risk #1 of 12)

Why This Exists:
The compatibility illusion risk is that franken_node appears compatible in testing but diverges in subtle, hard-to-detect ways under real-world conditions. This is the #1 risk because it directly undermines the core value proposition.

Task Objective:
Implement countermeasures for the compatibility illusion risk: lockstep oracle + divergence receipts. Ensure the risk is continuously monitored and the countermeasures are active.

Detailed Acceptance Criteria:
1. Lockstep oracle (from 10.0 Initiative #4) actively running on all compatibility bands with continuous divergence detection.
2. Divergence receipts (from 10.0 Initiative #1) automatically generated for any detected behavioral difference.
3. Compatibility corpus targets >= 95% pass rate (Success Criteria from Section 13).
4. Monitoring dashboard shows real-time compatibility health per API family (from 10.2 regression dashboard).
5. Alert system triggers when compatibility drops below threshold or new divergences appear.
6. Risk mitigation documented with explicit evidence artifacts proving countermeasure effectiveness.

Key Dependencies:
- Depends on 10.2 (Compatibility Core) for lockstep runners and band definitions.
- Depends on 10.0 (compatibility envelope, lockstep oracle) for countermeasure implementation.
- Feeds into 13 (Success Criteria) for >= 95% compatibility corpus pass target.

Expected Artifacts:
- Risk mitigation report with evidence of countermeasure effectiveness.
- Monitoring configuration for compatibility health.
- artifacts/section_12/bd-s4cu/verification_evidence.json

Testing and Logging Requirements:
- Unit tests: risk threshold detection, alert triggering logic.
- Integration tests: lockstep oracle -> divergence detection -> receipt generation -> alert pipeline.
- E2E tests: simulated compatibility degradation triggering alert and risk escalation.
- Structured logs: RISK_COMPATIBILITY_CHECKED, DIVERGENCE_DETECTED, RISK_THRESHOLD_BREACHED, COUNTERMEASURE_ACTIVE with risk level and trace IDs.
acceptance_criteria:
RISK: Compatibility illusion — passing compatibility tests while actual runtime behavior diverges, creating false confidence.
IMPACT: Production failures in migrated workloads that passed all pre-migration checks; erosion of trust in compatibility claims.
COUNTERMEASURES:
  (a) Lockstep oracle: run franken_node and reference Node.js side-by-side on identical inputs, compare outputs byte-for-byte.
  (b) Divergence receipts: every oracle comparison produces a signed receipt recording inputs, outputs, and match/mismatch verdict.
  (c) Receipt persistence: all divergence receipts are stored in artifacts/ with retention policy.
VERIFICATION:
  1. Lockstep oracle exists and runs on >= 500 representative API call sequences from the compatibility corpus.
  2. Divergence receipts are generated for every comparison (both match and mismatch).
  3. Any mismatch receipt triggers a blocking CI failure — no silent divergences.
  4. Receipt format is machine-parseable (JSON) with fields: input_hash, expected_output_hash, actual_output_hash, verdict, timestamp.
TEST SCENARIOS:
  - Scenario A: Inject a subtle behavioral divergence (e.g., different error message format); verify oracle detects it and blocks merge.
  - Scenario B: Run 100 matching comparisons; verify all produce match receipts and CI passes.
  - Scenario C: Tamper with a receipt; verify integrity check catches the tampering.

title: [10.7] Adopt canonical trust protocol vectors from `10.13` + `10.14` and enforce release/publication gates on those vectors.
description:
## [10.7] Adopt Canonical Trust Protocol Vectors and Enforce Release Gates

### Why This Exists

Sections 9E.10 and 9I.20 require "CDDL-like schema + golden vectors for cross-impl parity." The 10.13 and 10.14 tracks have produced golden test vectors — `fnode_trust_vectors_v1.json`, interop fixtures, idempotency vectors, epoch key vectors, seed derivation vectors, and MMR proof vectors — that define the canonical behavior of franken_node's trust protocol. These vectors must be promoted from development-time test assets to mandatory release gates. No release may ship if any canonical vector fails. This ensures cross-implementation parity and prevents protocol drift between releases.

### What It Must Do

**Vector adoption**: Collect all golden vectors from 10.13 (`vectors/fnode_trust_vectors_v1.json`, `fixtures/interop/`) and 10.14 (idempotency vectors, epoch key vectors, seed derivation vectors, MMR proof vectors) into a canonical vector registry. The registry is a manifest file (`vectors/canonical_manifest.toml`) that lists every vector suite, its source, its schema version, and its required-pass status.

**Release gate enforcement**: A CI gate runs all canonical vector suites before any release. The gate loads the manifest, executes each suite, and blocks the release if any required suite fails. The gate produces structured JSON output listing each suite's name, vector count, pass count, fail count, and overall status.

**Vector change control**: Modifications to any canonical vector file require an explicit changelog entry in `vectors/CHANGELOG.md` documenting what changed, why, and which implementations are affected. A pre-commit hook or CI check enforces that vector file changes are accompanied by changelog entries.

**Schema validation**: Each vector file must conform to its declared schema (JSON Schema or CDDL-derived). The gate validates schema conformance before executing vectors, so malformed vectors are caught early with clear error messages rather than producing confusing runtime failures.

**Cross-implementation parity check**: Where multiple implementations exist (Node shim, Bun shim, native franken_node), the gate runs vectors against all available implementations and reports any divergence. Divergence on a required vector is a release blocker.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. A canonical vector manifest (`vectors/canonical_manifest.toml`) lists all vector suites with source path, schema version, and required-pass status.
2. CI release gate executes all suites listed in the manifest and blocks release on any required-suite failure.
3. Gate output is structured JSON: suite name, vector count, pass/fail counts, overall status, execution time.
4. Modifications to canonical vector files require a corresponding entry in `vectors/CHANGELOG.md`; CI enforces this.
5. Schema validation runs before vector execution; malformed vectors produce clear error messages identifying the schema violation.
6. Cross-implementation parity is checked where multiple implementations are available; divergence on required vectors blocks release.
7. Verification script `scripts/check_canonical_vectors.py` with `--json` flag validates the full vector pipeline.
8. Unit tests in `tests/test_check_canonical_vectors.py` cover manifest parsing, schema validation, changelog enforcement, parity checking, and gate pass/fail logic.

### Key Dependencies

- Golden vectors from 10.13 (fnode_trust_vectors_v1.json, interop fixtures).
- Vectors from 10.14 (idempotency, epoch key, seed derivation, MMR proof).
- Lockstep harness from 10.2 (for cross-implementation execution).
- JSON Schema or CDDL schema definitions for each vector format.

### Testing & Logging Requirements

- Gate pass test: run with all vectors passing, assert gate passes and structured output is correct.
- Gate fail test: inject a failing vector, assert gate blocks with clear identification of the failure.
- Changelog enforcement test: modify a vector file without changelog, assert CI rejects.
- Schema validation test: inject a malformed vector, assert schema error is reported before execution.
- Structured JSON logs for each suite execution: suite name, vectors tested, pass/fail, duration.

### Expected Artifacts

- `vectors/canonical_manifest.toml` — vector registry.
- `vectors/CHANGELOG.md` — vector change log.
- `scripts/check_canonical_vectors.py` — verification script.
- `tests/test_check_canonical_vectors.py` — unit tests.
- `artifacts/section_10_7/bd-s6y/verification_evidence.json` — gate results.
- `artifacts/section_10_7/bd-s6y/verification_summary.md` — human-readable summary.

title: [10.14] Define immutable correctness envelope that policy controllers are forbidden to modify.
description:
## Why This Exists
franken_node's policy engine allows external controllers to tune runtime behavior — adjusting budgets, thresholds, and scheduling parameters. But certain invariants are correctness-critical and must NEVER be modified by any controller: things like the monotonic hardening direction, the evidence emission requirement, the deterministic seed derivation algorithm, and the integrity proof verification logic. The correctness envelope defines the boundary between "tunable policy" and "immutable correctness" — a formal enumeration of invariants that no policy controller is permitted to modify. This is directly inspired by FrankenSQLite's immutable page-header invariants (9J enhancement map) and enforces Section 8.5 Invariant #1 (correctness guarantees are never policy-overridable) by making the boundary explicit, documented, and code-enforced.

## What This Must Do
1. Define the `CorrectnessEnvelope` struct in `crates/franken-node/src/policy/correctness_envelope.rs` containing:
   - `invariants: Vec<Invariant>` — the set of non-tunable invariants.
   - Each `Invariant` has: `id: InvariantId`, `name: String`, `description: String`, `owner_track: SectionId` (which 10.N section owns this invariant), `enforcement: EnforcementMode` (Compile, Runtime, Conformance).
2. Enumerate the initial invariant set (minimum 10 invariants covering the Section 8.5 hard runtime invariants):
   - Monotonic hardening direction (cannot be reversed without governance artifact).
   - Evidence emission is mandatory for policy-driven actions.
   - Deterministic seed derivation algorithm is fixed per version.
   - Integrity proof verification cannot be bypassed.
   - Ring buffer overflow policy is FIFO (not policy-tunable).
   - Epoch boundaries are monotonically increasing.
   - Witness reference integrity hashes are SHA-256 (algorithm not overridable).
   - Guardrail precedence over Bayesian recommendations.
   - Object class profiles are versioned and append-only.
   - Remote capability tokens are required for network operations.
3. Implement `fn is_within_envelope(proposal: &PolicyProposal) -> Result<(), EnvelopeViolation>` that checks whether a proposed policy change touches any immutable invariant.
4. Write governance specification at `docs/specs/correctness_envelope.md` mapping each invariant to its owner track, enforcement mode, and rationale.
5. Write security tests at `tests/security/controller_envelope_enforcement.rs` verifying that controller API calls targeting immutable invariants are rejected.
6. Produce manifest at `artifacts/10.14/correctness_envelope_manifest.json` listing all invariants with their enforcement status.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Envelope enumerates non-tunable invariants; controller API rejects writes outside allowed policy set; governance doc maps invariant ownership.
- At least 10 immutable invariants are defined, covering all Section 8.5 hard runtime invariants.
- `is_within_envelope` correctly rejects proposals that would modify any immutable invariant.
- `is_within_envelope` correctly allows proposals that modify tunable policy parameters.
- Governance document maps every invariant to its owner track.
- Manifest artifact is machine-readable and lists all invariants with enforcement mode.
- Adding a new invariant requires updating both code and governance doc (enforced by CI).

## Testing & Logging Requirements
- Unit tests: Each invariant is present in the envelope; `is_within_envelope` rejects known-bad proposals for each invariant; `is_within_envelope` allows known-good proposals; `EnvelopeViolation` error contains the violated invariant ID.
- Integration tests: Controller API integration — submit a policy update targeting an immutable invariant via the full API stack and verify rejection; submit a valid policy update and verify acceptance.
- Conformance tests: Envelope manifest matches governance doc (automated cross-check); all Section 8.5 invariants are covered; no invariant has enforcement mode `None`.
- Adversarial tests: Attempt to modify the envelope itself via controller API; submit a proposal that modifies a tunable parameter but includes a side-effect on an immutable one; attempt to remove an invariant.
- Structured logs: `EVD-ENVELOPE-001` on envelope check pass; `EVD-ENVELOPE-002` on envelope violation (includes `invariant_id` and proposal summary); `EVD-ENVELOPE-003` on envelope loaded at startup. All logs include `epoch_id`.

## Expected Artifacts
- `crates/franken-node/src/policy/correctness_envelope.rs` — implementation
- `docs/specs/correctness_envelope.md` — governance specification
- `tests/security/controller_envelope_enforcement.rs` — security tests
- `artifacts/10.14/correctness_envelope_manifest.json` — invariant manifest
- `artifacts/section_10_14/bd-sddz/verification_evidence.json` — machine-readable pass/fail evidence
- `artifacts/section_10_14/bd-sddz/verification_summary.md` — human-readable summary

## Dependencies
- Upstream: bd-nupr (EvidenceEntry schema — evidence emission invariant references the entry type)
- Downstream: bd-bq4p (controller boundary checks enforce the envelope), bd-3a3q (guardrail monitors reference the envelope), bd-2ona (replay validator uses envelope to identify immutable constraints), bd-3epz (section gate), bd-5rh (10.14 plan gate)
acceptance_criteria:
1. The correctness envelope enumerates these concrete immutable invariants: (a) monotonic hardening — hardening level can only increase without governance rollback, (b) append-only evidence ledger — evidence entries cannot be modified or deleted, (c) monotonic control epoch — epoch value cannot decrease, (d) hash-chain integrity — marker stream hash chain cannot be broken, (e) deterministic replay — same inputs always produce same outputs, (f) fail-closed trust verification — missing trust data blocks rather than permits.
2. Each invariant is identified by a stable ID (e.g., ENVELOPE_MONOTONIC_HARDENING) and documented with: description, rationale, violation detection method, and consequence of violation.
3. The envelope is stored as a signed manifest file (correctness_envelope_v1.json) that is verified on system startup. Tampering with the envelope halts the system.
4. Policy controller API rejects any write operation that would violate an envelope invariant. Rejection produces structured error ENVELOPE_VIOLATION with the invariant ID and attempted mutation.
5. Governance doc maps invariant ownership: each invariant has a designated owner role responsible for its maintenance and any governance waiver requests.
6. Envelope versioning: adding new invariants creates a new envelope version (monotonic). Removing invariants requires a governance waiver with M-of-N approval.
7. All envelope operations emit structured log events: ENVELOPE_VERIFIED, ENVELOPE_VIOLATION_BLOCKED, ENVELOPE_WAIVER_REQUESTED, ENVELOPE_WAIVER_GRANTED with invariant ID and trace IDs.

title: [HIGH] Telemetry slowloris partial-line cap is only enforced on successful read_until
description: crates/franken-node/src/ops/telemetry_bridge.rs:1031-1052 — handle_connection checks event_bytes.len() > MAX_EVENT_BYTES only in the Ok(_) arm of BufRead::read_until. read_until may append bytes and then return TimedOut before a newline; the TimedOut arm immediately continues without checking or clearing event_bytes. A client that sends small fragments separated by read timeouts can grow event_bytes past MAX_EVENT_BYTES without an Ok(_) boundary. Repro: UnixStream sends MAX_EVENT_BYTES+1 bytes one fragment per CONNECTION_READ_TIMEOUT+epsilon, no newline; memory grows and no ADMISSION_SHED is recorded until a later successful read. Fix direction: after TimedOut/WouldBlock, check event_bytes.len() and shed/clear when over cap while preserving legitimate partial_write_survives_read_timeout behavior below the cap.

title: Child-process containment gate: authenticate private worker entry and guarantee non-escapable process-tree teardown before guest spawn
description: bd-wwjxn introduces a private one-shot native-session worker and relies on process-group kill because the current HostIo/JS surface cannot spawn descendants. design: Linux launch contract: supervisor uses an unnamed Unix socketpair as the request/liveness channel. Direct mode authenticates the positive SO_PEERCRED pid against the exact current franken-node executable. Parent parses --info-fd child-pid, immediately opens a pidfd for namespace PID1, and on timeout SIGKILLs via pidfd, waits for outer bwrap (which proves namespace empty), then drains/closes IPC.
