title: [CRITICAL] TOCTOU race condition in bd-q5iee validation proof work stealing
description:
Critical Time-of-Check-Time-of-Use race condition in validation_proof_coalescer.rs steal_stale_lease function.

**Bug Location:** crates/franken-node/src/ops/validation_proof_coalescer.rs:999-1144 

**The Problem:** 
1. Line 1009: read_lease() reads lease from disk 
2. Line 1022: assess_work_steal() checks staleness
3. Lines 1120+: Lease modified and written back via write_bytes_replace()

**Race Window:** Between read and write, another agent can:
- Complete the work and update the lease  
- Steal the same lease (duplicate ownership)
- Change fencing tokens
- Update lease expiry

**Risk:** Work stealing can steal already-completed work or create multiple owners for same validation work, breaking proof integrity.

**Evidence:** No file locking mechanisms found (grep for fs2/lock/mutex shows no results). write_bytes_replace() uses temp files but no advisory locks.

**Severity:** CRITICAL - corrupts validation proof integrity in multi-agent environments.

**Fix Required:** Add advisory file locking around entire read-assess-write sequence, similar to hardening patterns used elsewhere in codebase.

**Repro:** Start two agents attempting to steal same stale lease simultaneously.

title: Native dispatch quiescence can outlive timeout indefinitely on stuck synchronous HostIo
description: Fresh review follow-up from bd-45ck9. The no-detached-effects trust boundary correctly cancels admission, crosses the effect mutex, and joins the engine worker before returning. However, an already-admitted synchronous HostIoProvider::perform holds that mutex for its full call, so cancel_and_wait_for_effects has no bound if the provider never returns. SandboxedHostIo network setup currently includes blocking DNS resolution before connect_timeout. Design a genuinely cancellable or comprehensively bounded effect path that preserves the invariant that no guest or host effect survives the returned timeout; do not fix this by detaching the effect worker or returning before quiescence. Add a regression with a deliberately stuck admitted effect and an explicit overall deadline.
close_reason: Implemented in b60696b29: replaced unbounded in-process native dispatch with a versioned nonce-bound SHA256-framed one-shot worker process owning source load, parse/lower/execute, synchronous HostIo, telemetry, and effect-ledger construction. Parent enforces one absolute deadline, process-group kill and direct-child reap, bounded pipe drain, parent-death watchdog, and strict response plus ledger validation before returning. Real product E2E passed 1/1 in 10.72s through admitted loopback HTTP, proving bounded timeout, exact worker identity gone before return, no delayed callback, and subsequent-run health. Scoped RCH lib plus bin check passed; exact rustfmt and diff checks passed; independent lifecycle and adversarial reviews found no blocking defect. Repository-wide hidden-inline tests remain separately blocked by documented unrelated cfg errors.

comments.author: OliveCanyon
comments.text: 2026-07-22 read-only architecture audit (no source/status change): exact hang is CancellationGatedHostIo holding the per-run mutex across synchronous inner.perform while cancel_and_wait_for_effects blocks on that mutex before worker join. Engine CancellationToken only interrupts interpreter checkpoints. Blocking ToSocketAddrs DNS in SsrfGatedHostIo/SandboxedHostIo and filesystem syscalls are real uncooperative cases. No safe in-process Rust thread design can both force-stop and join an arbitrary stuck provider; timed mutex/helper thread would recreate the detached-effect violation bd-45ck9 fixed. Narrow honest design is a persistent per-run process-isolated HostIo broker: cancel admissions, kill+reap broker process group, cross effect barrier after IPC closes, join engine worker, then return EngineTimeout. Acceptance must prove bounded timeout, child reaped, no delayed marker/effect, later requests denied, crash/round-trip transcript preservation, and a real franken-node run path. Cooperative deadline APIs are defense-in-depth only. Agent Mail note 20284 sent to NobleLake.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: 2026-07-22 independent closeout review widens the hard-liveness scope beyond admitted HostIo: the supervised worker also performs blocking entrypoint fs::read_to_string and other setup before orchestrator execution, and parse/lowering may run before the next cancellation checkpoint. Timeout then unconditionally joins, so FIFO/special-file reads or a stuck setup/parse path can hang indefinitely even with no HostIo. The durable solution/acceptance must cover the entire native dispatch session, not only the HostIo broker; process-isolating the whole native session is the comprehensive variant. Also add a deterministic mid-execution product-path regression rather than relying only on the current 1ms infinite-loop test, which may cancel before execution begins; engine bd-61y6z separately proves both interpreter lanes observe cancellation during execution.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: 2026-07-22 implementation design selected after two independent read-only reviews: replace the parent Rust-thread deadline with a one-shot native-session worker process. The worker owns source loading, normalization, parse/lower/execute, synchronous HostIo, effect-ledger construction, and telemetry cleanup. Parent uses a versioned nonce-bound bounded stdin/stdout frame, isolates the worker in its own Unix process group, enforces one absolute deadline, sends immediate group SIGKILL on expiry, kills/reaps the direct child, drains bounded pipes, then returns EngineTimeout. Success is accepted only after typed frame validation and clean child exit. Product-path regressions must prove deterministic mid-execution/admitted-effect entry, bounded return, no delayed marker, and subsequent run health. Current HostEffectLedger v1 cannot honestly encode an effect interrupted after admission; that evidence-contract gap is split into a separate follow-up rather than fabricating allowed/denied receipts.

4. Co-metric baselines are established: each security/trust metric has a defined acceptable range.

6. Co-metrics are measured under at least 2 hardening profiles (balanced, strict).
7. Evidence: security_trust_cometrics.json with per-profile metric values and trade-off summary.

title: [mock-code-finder] Replace placeholder git_ref in security conformance fixtures
description:
Mock-code-finder source scan found a real placeholder in tests/security_conformance.rs:180-182. `get_git_ref()` is part of the SecurityFixture metadata, but it returns the literal string `current` with comments saying "In real implementation, get actual git commit hash" and "For now, use placeholder".

Why this matters:
- Golden security conformance fixtures and compliance reports cannot identify the source revision that produced them.
- This weakens deterministic replay and cross-version security evidence.
- `br search "get_git_ref current placeholder security conformance" --json` returned no existing open tracking bead.

Required fix:
- Replace the placeholder with a deterministic real git revision source for fixture/report generation, or make the fixture generator require an explicit revision input and fail closed if unavailable.
- Preserve reproducibility for checked-in golden fixtures; do not silently stamp non-deterministic data into committed goldens.
- Add a regression assertion that generated security conformance metadata never uses `current`, `placeholder`, or another sentinel for `git_ref`.

title: Resource-exhaustion DoS: unbounded JSON parsing + collection accumulation
description:
**RESOURCE-EXHAUSTION DoS VULNERABILITIES**

**1. main.rs:8385** - Fleet action log parsing DoS  
`serde_json::from_str(&line)` parsing PersistedFleetActionRecord without JSON depth/recursion limits  
**Attack:** Attacker places deeply nested JSON in fleet action log → stack overflow on parsing  
**Fix:** Use `serde_json::Deserializer::from_str().depth_limit(64).deserialize()` pattern

**2. main.rs:22296** - Evidence entry parsing DoS  
`serde_json::from_str(&line)` parsing EvidenceEntry without JSON depth/recursion limits  
**Attack:** Attacker places deeply nested JSON in transparency log → stack overflow on parsing  
**Fix:** Use `serde_json::Deserializer::from_str().depth_limit(64).deserialize()` pattern

**3. main.rs:22298** - Evidence collection memory exhaustion  
`entries.push(entry)` accumulating unbounded entries in Vec without size limits  
**Attack:** Attacker provides massive transparency log → OOM via unbounded Vec growth  
**Fix:** Add `push_bounded(&mut entries, entry, MAX_EVIDENCE_ENTRIES_PER_OPERATION)` limit

**Pattern:** All use raw `serde_json::from_str()` without depth limits + unbounded collection growth. JSON parser bombs can exhaust stack via deep nesting or heap via large collections.

Idea-wizard Phase 5 output.

The project has many evidence-producing surfaces, but operators need a single way to ask whether the node is currently producing trustworthy evidence: signed decisions, non-sentinel hashes, replay bundle integrity, trust-card roots, verifier capsules, and telemetry export health. title: [REALITY] Make verify migration require successful migration artifacts
description:
Reality-check gap: emit_verify_migration can currently report PASS when no state record exists but a lane source file is present. That proves the verifier code path exists, not that a migration/audit/validation actually succeeded.

User outcome: teams using `franken-node verify migration` before rollout should get a trustworthy migration verdict with actionable evidence, not a false green based on source presence. Preserve useful lane-source discovery as diagnostics, but do not let it satisfy a success claim by itself.

Implementation requirements:
1. Define the authoritative migration evidence inputs: audit report, rewrite manifest, rollback artifact, validation/lockstep record, state record, and status fields.
2. Require PASS to include a matching state/evidence record for the requested migration ID or lane, successful status, matching project/root scope, compatible schema version, and post_conditions_met=true where applicable.
3. Return UNPROVEN/WARN or FAIL for source-present/no-state cases, with JSON details explaining what evidence is missing and where the verifier looked.
4. Preserve existing helpful diagnostics for known lanes and source paths, but make them non-authoritative unless tied to real evidence.
5. Ensure migration evidence can be consumed by docs/gates without special-casing source-present passes.

Testing/logging requirements:
- Unit tests for successful state record, missing state record, source-present/no-state, malformed record, schema mismatch, project-scope mismatch, failed post conditions, stale validation timestamp, missing rollback artifact, and successful lockstep-linked validation.
- E2E CLI tests for `franken-node verify migration <id> --json` covering PASS, FAIL, and UNPROVEN/WARN outputs with exact exit-code expectations.
- Script/gate tests that mutate a temporary migration evidence bundle and prove the verifier fails closed on each critical missing field.
- Structured logs/events for migration_verify_started, evidence_record_loaded, lane_source_resolved, evidence_missing, post_condition_failed, migration_verify_completed; include trace_id, migration_id, project_root, record_path, lane_source, status, and missing_fields.
- Verification commands must include rch cargo check/clippy/fmt, focused verify-migration tests, and any relevant migration CLI E2E tests.
design:
Design notes for implementation:
- Preserve lane-source lookup as a diagnostic aid, but move it below evidence verification in the authority hierarchy. Source existence can explain what verifier lane exists; it cannot prove a migration happened.
- Define a small migration-evidence status model before changing outputs: PASS for validated success, FAIL for validated failure or invalid evidence, UNPROVEN for source/no-state or insufficient evidence, ERROR for IO/schema/runtime errors.
- Keep JSON stable where possible by adding detail fields rather than removing fields downstream tools may consume. If exit semantics change, document and test them explicitly.
- Evidence should bind migration id, project root, audit/rewrite/validate artifacts, rollback artifact, lockstep result where available, schema version, and timestamps.
- Make tests create temp migration evidence bundles rather than relying on ambient repo state. That gives reliable E2E coverage and avoids false positives from existing artifacts.
- Estimate: medium; high operator-safety value because it removes a false green rollout risk.
acceptance_criteria: PASS is only possible with successful migration evidence, not source presence. Source-present/no-state becomes explicit UNPROVEN/WARN or FAIL. JSON output reports searched locations and missing evidence. Unit, E2E, mutation/script, and structured logging coverage proves success and fail-closed behavior without removing lane diagnostics.
notes:
Second plan-space audit note: Preserve existing useful `verify migration` diagnostics and downstream JSON fields where possible; add authority/status fields rather than removing information. Add golden output tests for PASS, FAIL, UNPROVEN, and ERROR so automation can safely adapt. Do not weaken audit/rewrite/validate/rollback/lockstep evidence requirements to keep old source-present passes green. User-facing output should explain whether a result is rollout-authoritative or only diagnostic.

Third plan-space audit note: Completion must add authority-hierarchy unit tests and E2E temp evidence bundles for PASS, FAIL, UNPROVEN, and ERROR. The mutation script should remove state, corrupt schema, mismatch project/root scope, stale timestamp, and remove rollback or lockstep linkage to verify fail-closed behavior. Logs must show searched paths, selected authoritative record, missing fields, and why source-only evidence is diagnostic rather than success.

Fourth plan-space audit note: Make the migration UX safer for rollout operators: include explicit exit-code semantics for PASS/FAIL/UNPROVEN/ERROR, remediation hints for each missing evidence class, and a compatibility note for automation that previously treated source-present as success. Do not remove lane discovery; demote it to diagnostic context and prove gates consume only authoritative evidence.
close_reason: completed

title: [10.14] Implement fork/divergence detection via marker-id prefix comparison and binary search.
description:
## Why This Exists

Fork and divergence detection is the mechanism that identifies when two instances of the marker stream (e.g., a primary and a replica, or two nodes after a network partition) have diverged from a common history. This is essential for the 9J runtime because divergent marker streams mean divergent control-plane histories -- different nodes may have committed different epoch transitions, policy changes, or trust decisions. Without precise divergence detection, the system cannot perform safe reconciliation or alert operators to split-brain conditions. This bead uses the marker stream's hash-chain property (bd-126h) to perform efficient O(log N) divergence detection via binary search, directly supporting runtime invariant #9 (verification gates must detect inconsistencies deterministically). The 10.10 rollback/fork detection system (bd-2ms) depends on this capability.

## What This Must Do

1. Implement `find_divergence_point(local: &MarkerStream, remote: &MarkerStream) -> DivergenceResult` that returns the greatest common prefix (last sequence number where both streams agree) and the exact divergence point (first sequence number where they differ).
2. Use marker-id (hash) prefix comparison: start at the latest common sequence, compare hashes, and binary search backward/forward to find the exact divergence point. Total comparisons must be O(log N) where N is the stream length.
3. `DivergenceResult` must include: `common_prefix_seq: u64`, `divergence_seq: u64`, `local_hash_at_divergence: Hash`, `remote_hash_at_divergence: Hash`, and `evidence: DivergenceEvidence` containing the comparison trace.
4. Handle degenerate cases: identical streams (no divergence), completely divergent streams (diverge at sequence 0), one stream empty, streams of different lengths.
5. Ensure determinism: given the same two streams, `find_divergence_point` always returns the same result regardless of call order or concurrent operations.
6. Produce a spec document defining the divergence detection algorithm, complexity proof, and evidence format.
7. Produce integration tests with multiple divergence scenarios including single-marker divergence, bulk divergence, and divergence at stream boundaries.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Divergence finder returns greatest common prefix deterministically; fork detection scales logarithmically; mismatch evidence includes exact divergence point.
- For two streams that agree on markers 0..999 and diverge at 1000, `common_prefix_seq == 999` and `divergence_seq == 1000`.
- For two identical streams of length N, result indicates no divergence.
- For two streams diverging at marker 0, `common_prefix_seq` indicates no common prefix.
- Binary search performs at most `ceil(log2(N))` hash comparisons for a stream of length N.
- Evidence includes the local and remote hashes at the exact divergence point.
- Result is identical regardless of argument order (`find_divergence_point(a, b) == find_divergence_point(b, a)` modulo local/remote label swap).

## Testing & Logging Requirements

- Unit tests: identical streams; single-point divergence at various positions; complete divergence; different-length streams; empty stream vs non-empty; determinism check (call twice, same result).
- Integration tests: divergence detection on streams of 10K, 100K, 1M markers; divergence detection with concurrent appends; comparison count verification (must be <= log2(N)).
- Conformance tests: `tests/integration/marker_divergence_detection.rs` -- normative divergence detection scenarios.
- Structured logs: `DIVERGENCE_DETECTED` (common_prefix_seq, divergence_seq, local_hash_prefix, remote_hash_prefix, comparison_count, trace_id), `DIVERGENCE_NONE` (stream_length, trace_id), `DIVERGENCE_SEARCH_STEP` (step_seq, match_result, trace_id -- debug level).

## Expected Artifacts

- `tests/integration/marker_divergence_detection.rs` -- normative integration tests
- `docs/specs/divergence_detection.md` -- algorithm specification and complexity proof
- `artifacts/10.14/divergence_detection_examples.json` -- divergence examples from test runs
- `artifacts/section_10_14/bd-xwk5/verification_evidence.json` -- machine-readable CI/release gate evidence
- `artifacts/section_10_14/bd-xwk5/verification_summary.md` -- human-readable verification summary

## Dependencies

- Upstream: bd-126h (append-only marker stream -- provides hash-chained markers for comparison).
- Downstream: bd-2ms (10.10 rollback/fork detection in control-plane state), bd-3epz (section gate), bd-5rh (section gate).
acceptance_criteria: Divergence finder returns greatest common prefix deterministically; fork detection scales logarithmically; mismatch evidence includes exact divergence point.

title: [REVIEW] Frankensqlite audit-window truncation hides historical tampering
description: FrankensqliteAdapter::write() silently truncates the in-memory audit replay window once MAX_AUDIT_LOG_ENTRIES is exceeded. Repro: write MAX_AUDIT_LOG_ENTRIES+1 unique AuditLog keys, tamper an evicted historical store entry, then call replay(); the tampered oldest entry is never checked because replay only walks the truncated window, and gate_pass() can still report PASS. Impact: fail-open forensic coverage for Tier1 audit data.

title: [conformance] canonical serializer harness does not exercise CanonicalSerializer
description:
Test: canonical_serializer_conformance (registered in crates/franken-node/Cargo.toml:457-459)

Finding:
crates/franken-node/tests/canonical_serializer_conformance.rs claims BD-JJM/INV-CAN conformance, but it never calls the real CanonicalSerializer implementation. The only product import is TrustObjectType at lines 10-11.

False assertions:
- Determinism at lines 150-158 only checks fixture canonical_bytes are non-empty and valid JSON. It does not serialize payload_json through CanonicalSerializer.
- Round-trip at lines 176-187 parses fixture bytes with serde_json and reserializes with serde_json::to_vec; the test comment says the real implementation would use CanonicalSerializer.
- Negative cases at lines 269-299 only check that invalid fixture names exist (float_payload and non_canonical_bytes). They never submit those payloads/bytes to the real serializer or assert a SerializerError.

Why this is HIGH:
This conformance target can report PASS while the real serializer accepts floats, emits non-canonical bytes, or diverges from the fixture corpus. It is registered as a shipping test target, so it creates false release confidence for bd-jjm/INV-CAN coverage.

Proper assertion:
For every positive fixture, instantiate CanonicalSerializer::with_all_schemas(), call serialize_value(object_type, &fixture.payload_json, trace_id), compare exact bytes to fixture.canonical_bytes, then call deserialize/round_trip_canonical against the same bytes. For preimages, compare through the real public preimage builder or add one if missing. For negative fixtures, feed float_payload/non_canonical_bytes into the real API and assert the exact SerializerError/rejection code. Load/validate the docs/specs bd-jjm contract or an extracted matrix instead of leaving spec coverage implicit.

title: PERF: tools replay_bundle processes events with heavy per-event allocations
[10.12] Implement operator intelligence recommendation engine with rollback proofs.
description:
Master Plan Source: PLAN_TO_CREATE_FRANKEN_NODE.md — Section 10.12 (Frontier Programs), cross-ref Section 9H.4 (Operator Intelligence Program), 9F.6 (Autonomous incident commander)

## Why This Exists
Operators of high-trust extension ecosystems face a combinatorial explosion of configuration, migration, and security decisions where wrong choices have compounding downstream costs. The Operator Intelligence Program (9H.4) addresses this by shipping expected-loss-aware control recommendations with deterministic action replays — meaning every recommendation the system makes comes with a quantified risk estimate, a concrete action plan, and a cryptographic rollback proof that guarantees the action can be undone to a known-good state. This bead implements the recommendation engine core, the expected-loss scoring model, and the rollback proof infrastructure. It directly advances the category-defining floor targets of "100% deterministic replay artifact availability" (every recommendation produces a replay artifact) and ">= 3x migration throughput and confidence quality" (operator intelligence reduces decision latency and error rates during migration campaigns).

## What This Must Do
1. Implement a `RecommendationEngine` module (`crates/franken-node/src/connector/operator_intelligence.rs`) that accepts an operator context (current system state snapshot, pending operations queue, active alerts) and produces a ranked list of `Recommendation` structs, each containing: action description, expected-loss score (quantified downside in a normalized risk unit), confidence interval, prerequisite checks, and estimated execution time.
2. Implement an expected-loss scoring model that computes risk estimates from: (a) historical outcome data (migration success/failure rates from 10.3), (b) current compatibility state (from 10.2 compatibility core), (c) trust posture (from 10.4/10.13 trust fabric — revocation state, certificate validity), and (d) operational telemetry (error rates, latency percentiles, resource utilization). The model must be deterministic: identical inputs produce identical scores.
3. Implement a `RollbackProof` structure that captures: (a) pre-action state snapshot (content-addressed), (b) the action specification (deterministic command sequence), (c) post-action expected state, and (d) a rollback command sequence that restores pre-action state. The proof must be independently verifiable — an external party can check that the rollback sequence, applied to the post-action state, produces the pre-action state hash.
4. Implement deterministic action replay: every recommendation that is executed produces a replay artifact containing the full input context, the recommendation chosen, the action sequence executed, the observed outcome, and the rollback proof. Replay artifacts must be machine-parseable and re-executable.
5. Implement a recommendation audit trail that logs every recommendation generated (whether accepted or rejected by the operator), with timestamps, context fingerprints, and outcome tracking for accepted recommendations.
6. Provide a CLI subcommand (`franken-node recommend`) that invokes the engine for the current system state and presents recommendations in priority order with expected-loss scores and rollback proof summaries.
7. Implement degraded-mode behavior: when input data sources are unavailable (e.g., historical data missing), the engine must still produce recommendations but with wider confidence intervals and explicit data-quality warnings, never silently degrading accuracy.

## Context from Enhancement Maps
- 9H.4: "Ship expected-loss-aware control recommendations with deterministic action replays." This bead is the direct implementation of that program's core engine.
- 9F.6: "Autonomous incident commander" — the recommendation engine is the decision-making core that an autonomous incident commander would invoke; this bead establishes the deterministic, auditable recommendation infrastructure that future autonomous operation builds on.
- Category-defining targets (Section 3.2): "100% deterministic replay artifact availability" — every executed recommendation produces a complete replay artifact with rollback proof. ">= 3x migration throughput and confidence quality" — operator intelligence reduces decision errors and accelerates migration campaigns by quantifying expected loss before each action.

## Dependencies
- Upstream: bd-3c2 (verifier-economy SDK — provides independent validation workflows that can verify rollback proofs), Section 10.2 (compatibility core — compatibility state is an input to expected-loss scoring), Section 10.3 (migration system — historical migration outcome data feeds the scoring model), Section 10.4/10.13 (trust/security — trust posture and revocation state are scoring inputs).
- Downstream: bd-2aj (ecosystem network-effect APIs — recommendation outcomes and rollback proofs are published as compliance evidence), bd-n1w (frontier demo gates — operator intelligence must register a demo gate), bd-1d6x (section-wide verification gate), bd-go4 (section 10.12 plan rollup).

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The `RecommendationEngine` accepts a well-defined operator context and produces a ranked list of recommendations, each with action description, expected-loss score, confidence interval, prerequisites, and estimated execution time.
2. Expected-loss scores are deterministic: given identical operator context inputs, the engine produces byte-identical recommendation rankings and scores across 100 consecutive runs.
3. Every executed recommendation produces a `RollbackProof` containing pre-action state hash, action specification, post-action expected state, and rollback command sequence.
4. Rollback proofs are independently verifiable: a test harness can apply the rollback sequence to the post-action state and confirm the resulting state hash matches the pre-action state hash.
5. Replay artifacts contain the full input-to-output trace and can be re-executed to reproduce the same outcome (deterministic replay).
6. The recommendation audit trail records all generated recommendations (accepted and rejected) with context fingerprints and timestamps.
7. Degraded-mode operation produces recommendations with explicit data-quality warnings and widened confidence intervals when input sources are unavailable, without crashing or producing silent errors.
8. The `franken-node recommend` CLI subcommand produces human-readable output with expected-loss scores and rollback proof summaries for the current system state.

## Testing & Logging Requirements
- Unit tests: Test expected-loss score computation with fixed inputs for determinism; test recommendation ranking stability; test rollback proof generation and verification round-trip; test degraded-mode behavior with missing input sources; test confidence interval widening logic.
- Integration tests: End-to-end recommendation generation from real system state snapshots; test action execution -> rollback proof generation -> rollback execution -> state verification cycle; test audit trail completeness (all recommendations logged).
- E2E tests: Operator workflow — trigger a migration recommendation, review expected-loss scores, execute the recommended action, verify rollback proof is generated, execute rollback, confirm system returns to pre-action state.

title: BUG: verifier SDK accepts tampered session nonces
description: Fresh-eyes audit of sdk/verifier/src/lib.rs found that VerificationSession carries a mutable session_nonce used by session_step_signature(), but validate_session_provenance() never checks that nonce against the originally derived value or any immutable origin field. A caller can create a valid session, mutate session_nonce in memory, and then have record_session_step() and seal_session() continue to accept the session and recompute step signatures against the forged nonce. That breaks session provenance binding because the append/seal path no longer guarantees the session is the one originally minted by create_session(). Fix direction: bind session_nonce to immutable session provenance (for example store origin_session_nonce and compare it, or recompute and verify the derived nonce from session_id + verifier_identity + created_at) and add regressions proving tampered nonces are rejected during both record_session_step() and seal_session().

title: Implement atomic in-flight validation proof lease store
description:
## Scope
Implement the file-backed in-flight validation proof lease store that lets agents create, join, complete, and fence proof work without duplicate writers.

## Required Behavior
- Atomic create-new lease writes keyed by canonical proof-work key.
- Fencing tokens prevent stale owners from completing or overwriting newer leases.
- Stale lease detection is time-bounded and fail-closed when metadata is malformed.
- Completed leases carry receipt path, cache key, producer agent, bead id, trace id, and RCH command metadata.
- Store operations sync parent directories and never overwrite active proof artifacts.
- Corrupted metadata yields structured repair decisions, not panics or silent reuse.

## Expected Surfaces
- A focused module under `crates/franken-node/src/ops/` following existing validation broker/proof-cache patterns.
- Inline unit tests for create/join/complete/stale/fence/corruption behavior.
- Integration coverage in `crates/franken-node/tests/` using real temp directories and real lease files.

## Acceptance
- Equivalent keys converge to one running lease with join decisions for waiters.
- Divergent keys produce independent leases.
- Stale and corrupted leases fail closed with stable reason codes.
- No code path uses unsafe code or lossy string parsing for structured lease data.

description:
Master Plan Source: PLAN_TO_CREATE_FRANKEN_NODE.md
Section: 10.0 — Top 10 Initiative Tracking (Initiative #3)
Cross-references: 9A.3, 9B.3, 9C.3, 9D.3

Why This Exists:
Trust cards are the #3 strategic initiative. They surface provenance, behavioral telemetry, revocation status, and policy constraints in a single explainable trust model consumable by both humans and automation. Trust cards are the primary interface through which operators and tools understand the trustworthiness of extensions and publishers.

Task Objective:
Implement the trust card system for extensions and publishers — a structured, queryable trust profile that aggregates provenance data, behavioral evidence, revocation status, policy constraints, and reputation signals into an explainable, API-accessible trust assessment.

Detailed Acceptance Criteria:
1. Trust card schema captures: provenance attestations, behavioral telemetry summary, revocation status, policy constraint set, certification level, publisher reputation score, and risk tier.
2. CLI surface: franken-node trust card {extension_id} displays full trust card in human-readable format.
3. API surface: programmatic trust-card query returns structured JSON suitable for automation.
4. Trust deltas decomposed into posterior components with counterfactual action impacts exposed (9C.3).
5. Authenticated data structures and transparency-style append-only proofs for trust evidence lineage (9B.3).
6. Trust-card materialization optimized with incremental updates and bounded recomputation (9D.3).
7. Trust card integrates with extension certification levels (10.4), policy controls (10.5), and fleet quarantine (10.8).
8. Publisher trust cards aggregate across all published extensions with explainable reputation transitions.

Key Dependencies:
- Depends on 10.4 (Extension Ecosystem) for manifest schema and provenance attestation.
- Consumed by 10.5 (Security) for policy-visible trust decisions.
- Consumed by 10.17 (Radical Expansion) for Bayesian adversary graph integration.
- Consumed by 10.21 (BPET) for behavioral phenotype evidence.

Expected Artifacts:
- src/security/trust_card.rs — trust card schema, builder, query API.
- src/security/trust_card_publisher.rs — publisher-level aggregation.
- CLI integration in cli.rs for trust card/list/revoke commands.
- docs/specs/section_10_0/bd-y4g_contract.md
- artifacts/section_10_0/bd-y4g/verification_evidence.json

Testing and Logging Requirements:
- Unit tests: trust card construction, field validation, incremental update correctness, posterior decomposition.
- Integration tests: trust card generation from mock extension manifests + behavioral data + revocation feeds.
- E2E tests: franken-node trust card {extension_id} CLI workflow producing correct output.
- Adversarial tests: malformed provenance data, stale revocation, conflicting signals.
- Structured logs: TRUST_CARD_MATERIALIZED, TRUST_CARD_QUERIED, TRUST_DELTA_COMPUTED, REPUTATION_UPDATED with trace IDs.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Trust card schema includes: publisher identity, provenance chain (build source -> artifact), behavioral telemetry summary, revocation status, policy constraint set, trust score, last-audit timestamp.
2. Provenance chain is cryptographically verifiable: each link signed, tamper-evident, traceable to source commit.
3. Behavioral telemetry captures: permission usage (fs/net/child_process), resource consumption bounds, anomaly flags; updated on each publish cycle.
4. Revocation status propagates within <= 60 seconds to all connected fleet nodes (real-time revocation channel).
5. Policy constraints expressed as declarative rules (e.g., "no net access", "fs read-only /app/**"); enforced at runtime with deny-by-default semantics.
6. Trust model is explainable: CLI command (`franken-node trust explain <extension>`) outputs human-readable rationale for current trust score decomposition.
7. Compromise reduction target: trust card system contributes to >= 10x compromise reduction (Section 3) by blocking extensions that fail provenance or behavioral checks.
8. Trust cards queryable via API and CLI in JSON format; support filtering by publisher, score range, revocation status.
9. Integration with secure extension distribution network (bd-2ac): trust card is mandatory for registry publish; missing card blocks distribution.
10. Verification evidence includes: sample trust cards for test extensions, revocation propagation latency measurement, policy constraint enforcement test results.

title: Epic: Swarm handoff plane for stale agents, reservations, and cross-repo blockers
description: Idea-wizard Phase 2/3 result: with ready implementation beads exhausted and proof lanes blocked, the highest non-duplicative improvement is a swarm handoff plane that makes stale work, dead agents, active reservations, RCH liveness, and cross-repo blockers visible and safe to act on. Existing beads cover proof scheduling, RCH recovery, artifact pressure, and stale proof producers. This epic covers the coordination layer above them: deciding whether a bead claim is alive, blocked, abandoned, waiting on a reserved sibling file, or safe to reopen without trampling another agent. User impact: large agent swarms stop losing time rediscovering stale claims or waiting in communication purgatory. Operators get deterministic evidence for who owns what, what is actually live, which reservations block progress, and the safe next action. Non-goals: no destructive cleanup, no automatic file deletion, no silent reservation override, and no proxying worker-infra failures as product success. Epic acceptance: a read-only evidence model ingests Beads state, Agent Mail identity/reservation metadata, RCH queue liveness, recent git activity, and optional cross-repo blocker links; a fail-closed policy classifies active, blocked, stale, abandoned, contested, and ready-to-reopen states; doctor/readiness/closeout can emit concise JSON and human summaries; fixture replay covers dead-agent, active-holder, stale-reservation, cross-repo blocker, and RCH-live cases; every reopen or handoff recommendation includes audit evidence and requires an explicit br operation by an agent.

Live bv/br state on 2026-05-07 had no ready implementation beads, no in-progress beads to rescue, and highest-impact blockers in validation/RCH/resource-governor lanes. title: TEST: 5a7473ff time-math wraparound test only covers happy path, not boundary conditions
description:
Commit 5a7473ff fixed critical time math wraparound vulnerabilities in latest_file_age_secs() and current_unix_secs(), but no regression tests were added to verify the boundary conditions work correctly.

Missing test coverage for exact pre-bound cases that would have triggered wraparound:

1. **latest_file_age_secs() future timestamp bypass**:
   - Test: Create file with future timestamp (SystemTime > now)  
   - Expected: Should return large age (u32::MAX secs), not Duration::ZERO
   - Regression: Verify old code would have returned 0 (fresh), new code returns very stale

2. **current_unix_secs() pre-EPOCH wraparound**:
   - Test: Mock SystemTime before UNIX_EPOCH (clock rewind scenario)
   - Expected: Should return u64::MAX (far future), not 0
   - Regression: Verify old code would have returned 0, new code fails-closed

3. **i64::MAX boundary conditions**:
   - Test: Edge cases near maximum time values
   - Expected: Saturating behavior, not panic or wraparound

4. **Clock skew attack simulation**:
   - Test: File timestamps significantly in future (days/years ahead)
   - Expected: Staleness detection should not be bypassed

Current tests only verify normal flow but don't exercise the specific security vulnerabilities that were fixed.

title: [10.0] Implement fleet quarantine UX + control plane.
description:
Master Plan Source: PLAN_TO_CREATE_FRANKEN_NODE.md
Section: 10.0 — Top 10 Initiative Tracking (Initiative #6)
Cross-references: 9A.6, 9B.6, 9C.6, 9D.6

Why This Exists:
Fleet quarantine UX + control plane is the #6 strategic initiative. It turns engine-level containment primitives into operator-grade workflows with global scope, blast-radius views, convergence indicators, and rollback controls. Without this, quarantine operations remain low-level and error-prone.

Task Objective:
Build the fleet quarantine user experience and control plane that enables operators to manage quarantine/revocation operations across distributed deployments with clear visibility into scope, impact, convergence state, and rollback options.

Detailed Acceptance Criteria:
1. Fleet control API for quarantine/revocation operations with zone/tenant scoping.
2. Blast-radius visualization showing affected extensions, publishers, and dependent workloads.
3. Convergence indicators: real-time progress tracking of quarantine propagation across fleet.
4. Rollback controls: deterministic rollback to pre-quarantine state with verification.
5. Anti-entropy reconciliation and bounded degraded-mode semantics under network partition (9B.6).
6. Probabilistic SLO proofs for containment latency and convergence quality (9C.6).
7. Propagation path latency and conflict reconciliation fast paths optimized (9D.6).
8. CLI surface: franken-node fleet status/release/reconcile commands.
9. Convergence timeout configurable per profile (strict=60s, balanced=120s, legacy-risky=300s per config.rs).

Key Dependencies:
- Depends on engine-level containment primitives from franken_engine.
- Consumed by 10.8 (Operational Readiness) for fleet control API.
- Consumed by 10.5 (Security) for policy-driven quarantine decisions.
- Integrates with 10.20 (DGIS) for topology-aware containment.

Expected Artifacts:
- src/fleet/ module with control_plane.rs, convergence.rs, blast_radius.rs, rollback.rs.
- CLI integration for fleet commands in cli.rs.
- docs/specs/section_10_0/bd-yqz_contract.md
- artifacts/section_10_0/bd-yqz/verification_evidence.json

Testing and Logging Requirements:
- Unit tests: convergence calculation, blast radius computation, rollback state verification, anti-entropy reconciliation.
- Integration tests: quarantine propagation across simulated multi-zone fleet.
- E2E tests: franken-node fleet status/release/reconcile CLI workflows.
- Fault injection tests: network partition during quarantine propagation, convergence under degraded mode.
- Structured logs: QUARANTINE_INITIATED, PROPAGATION_PROGRESS, CONVERGENCE_REACHED, ROLLBACK_EXECUTED, DEGRADED_MODE_ENTERED with trace IDs and zone metadata.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Global scope: quarantine operations apply fleet-wide; single quarantine action propagates to all enrolled nodes within <= 120 seconds.
2. Blast-radius views: CLI and API expose affected node count, affected workload count, estimated user impact percentage, and dependency graph of quarantined components.
3. Convergence indicators: real-time dashboard data (JSON API) showing: quarantine propagation progress (% nodes confirmed), rollback progress, and time-to-convergence estimate.
4. Rollback controls: deterministic single-command rollback (`franken-node quarantine rollback <id>`) that restores pre-quarantine state; rollback verified by post-rollback health check.
5. Quarantine policies are declarative: trigger conditions (severity threshold, anomaly score, revocation event), scope (extension/version/publisher), and auto-escalation rules.
6. Audit trail: every quarantine action (create/extend/rollback/expire) logged with timestamp, actor, justification, blast-radius snapshot; append-only and tamper-evident.
7. Integration with trust cards (bd-y4g): revocation events automatically trigger quarantine evaluation; trust score drop below threshold triggers quarantine proposal.
8. Compromise reduction contribution: quarantine system contributes to >= 10x compromise reduction target (Section 3) by containing blast radius within <= 60 seconds of detection.
9. UX: quarantine status visible in `franken-node status` output; color-coded severity; actionable next-step suggestions.
10. Verification evidence includes: propagation latency measurement, rollback success test, blast-radius calculation accuracy test, convergence indicator correctness test.

title: [AUDIT-LOGIC] verification relies on stale evidence without freshness validation - analysis evidence can become outdated before verification
description:
**Logic Gap**: Verification stage relies on evidence collected during analysis without any freshness validation, creating potential for decisions based on stale data.

**Flow Breakdown**:
1. **Analysis Stage**: Populates compatibility_report.findings and extension_specs.evidence fields (validation_samples, lockstep_samples, validation_failures, etc.)
2. **Pipeline Progression**: ANALYSIS → PLAN_GENERATION → PLAN_REVIEW → EXECUTION → VERIFICATION (multiple stages between evidence collection and usage)
3. **Verification Usage**: run_verification() directly uses spec.evidence fields without timestamp or freshness checks (lines 1651-1658 in migration_pipeline.rs)

**Gap**: No evidence age validation. Evidence collected during analysis (potentially minutes/hours earlier) is used in verification without checking if it's still representative of current system state.

**Attack Scenario**:
1. Analysis stage collects evidence showing extension as compatible
2. Extension's actual behavior degrades during pipeline progression
3. Security patches or configuration changes invalidate analysis findings
4. Verification proceeds with stale evidence showing false positive compatibility
5. Migration executes based on outdated safety assessment

**Impact**: Stale evidence can lead to false positive verification results, allowing unsafe migrations to proceed when current system state would fail verification criteria.
close_reason: ff2f8d90 evidence freshness validation implemented to reject stale data (migration_pipeline.rs:345,1683-1726 validate_evidence_freshness + line 1763 integration). Added collected_at timestamp to ExtensionEvidence with 1-hour freshness threshold. Fail-closed semantics: stale evidence = verification failure. Tests: test_verification_rejects_stale_evidence verifies rejection, test_verification_accepts_fresh_evidence verifies acceptance within threshold.

title: Epic: Proof-lane readiness and credential drift capsules
description:
Idea-wizard result after the bd-agpdg proof-lane blocker: franken_node needs a first-class, deterministic readiness capsule for validation proof lanes before agents launch expensive cargo/RCH work.

Problem:
Current validation beads can stall behind terminal-only facts: RCH_WORKER overrides may not be honored by the installed daemon, same-toolchain workers can be missing runtime capabilities, and the only suitable worker can fail authentication while generic RCH status still looks degraded rather than hard-blocked. Agents then improvise: retry on mismatched workers, fall open locally, or leave bead comments that are hard to consume programmatically.

Goal:
Add a product-side proof-lane readiness contract that records worker override effectiveness, same-toolchain availability, credential/auth failure, capability freshness, worker pressure, local fallback refusal, and the exact action an agent/operator should take. This must complement, not replace, existing validation broker, flight recorder, resource governor, and RCH recovery planner work.

Success criteria:
- Readiness capsules are deterministic JSON artifacts with stable schema, reason codes, event codes, freshness, command digest, target worker, selected worker, local toolchain, worker toolchain, and auth/capability status.
- Capsules distinguish override_not_honored, same_toolchain_missing, worker_auth_failed, worker_capability_unknown, worker_pressure_blocked, and local_fallback_refused.
- Existing proof/recovery/doctor surfaces can cite capsule paths instead of terminal history.
- Unit and fixture tests cover the current ts2 auth/capability blocker, old override mismatch behavior, healthy same-toolchain worker, missing toolchain, degraded worker, and stale capsule expiry.
- Cargo-heavy validation must use rch exec; source-only and fixture checks must remain runnable without live RCH.

title: Implement deterministic proof-lane readiness classifier
description:
Purpose:
Implement the pure, fixture-driven classifier that turns RCH dry-run/status/capability snapshots into a proof-lane readiness decision. This is the code slice that should let agents know whether a cargo proof can be launched, must be queued, must use a different worker, or must fail closed with a source-only blocker.

Scope:
- Add a data-model API in the validation ops layer, reusing existing serde/error/constant-time patterns where appropriate.
- Accept deterministic inputs: command digest, requested/preferred worker list, selected worker, local toolchain, worker capability map, worker health/pressure state, SSH/auth status, local fallback policy, and observation freshness.
- Return a stable capsule/decision with reason_code, event_code, operator summary, required_action, retryability, fail_closed flag, and freshness expiry.
- Do not shell out or contact live RCH from unit tests; live probes must remain narrow adapters.
- Enforce bounded growth for worker lists, strings, diagnostic snippets, and capsule references.

Acceptance:
- Unit tests cover healthy same-toolchain lane, override not honored, selected worker toolchain mismatch, worker auth failed, capability unknown, stale capability snapshot, local fallback refused, and pressure blocked.
- The classifier never marks product compile/test failure as worker infra and never marks worker infra as a green proof.
- Missing optional inputs are explicit unknowns or fail-closed decisions, not silent success.

- UBS on touched Rust files.

title: Gate no-ready recovery with fixture-backed e2e evidence
description:
## What
Add the final fixture-backed e2e/golden gate for the actionable-work recovery package. It should run the claimability checker, blocker freshness audit, RCH evidence normalizer, and runbook fixture over a synthetic no-ready graph and produce one detailed PASS/FAIL summary.

## Why
This project treats docs/specs/artifacts as product contracts. The recovery package should not be accepted because it sounds reasonable; it should prove that an agent can distinguish blocked graph states from claimable work and produce an auditable next action.

## How
After the implementation beads land, add an integration-style test or Python unittest that uses checked-in fixtures only. It should log each layer: br-ready input, BV recommendation input, per-bead claimability classification, blocker freshness verdict, RCH evidence classification, and final no-ready decision.

## Risks
Do not make this gate depend on live Agent Mail, live BV, live RCH, or local Cargo state. The test should be deterministic and fast. Heavy Rust validation for any touched Rust surface must still go through `rch exec -- ...`.

## Success Criteria
- One command produces a stable JSON summary and human-readable log.
- The no-ready fixture recommends `create-new-bead` or `refresh-blocker` rather than `claim` for blocked items.
- A fixture with a truly ready item recommends `claim`.
- Golden output catches regressions in classification labels and exact first-blocker preservation.

Path (2): security/remote_cap.rs HybridRevocationChecker no longer shares ReplayTokenSet's FIFO eviction — revocations are a BTreeMap keyed by token id carrying the capability's own expires_at_epoch_secs, retired only once now >= expires_at (safe because authorize_network returns RemoteCapError::Expired from that instant regardless), never evicted while live, and REFUSED at capacity via the new RevocationOutcome enum with a REMOTECAP_REVOKE_REFUSED audit event rather than silently un-revoking an enforced entry; an earliest_expiry watermark keeps the retire sweep O(1) on the authorize hot path. comments.text:
2026-07-24 CrimsonCrane, verified by reading. THREE independent paths let a revoked credential become valid again. Path (1) is FIXED in this session; (2) and (3) remain.

(1) FIXED — security/zk_attestation.rs:609. verify_proof used the stored ledger record for contains_key ONLY, then read status/expires_at_ms/generated_at_ms off the CALLER-SUPPLIED &ZkAttestation. revoke_attestation mutates the ledger record, never the caller's struct, so a holder of a pre-revocation copy verified forever; same for sweep_expired. The comment at :605-608 named exactly this threat and implemented only the existence half. Fixed by binding the ledger record and checking lifecycle against it (is_valid() already did this correctly).

(2) OPEN — security/remote_cap.rs:371-381. CapabilityGate.revoked_tokens is a HybridRevocationChecker pinned to CheckMode::Fallback; its insertion_order/btree_backup pair FIFO-evicts at MAX_REPLAY_ENTRIES=4096. Revoke capability C (still inside TTL; issue() has no max-TTL clamp), then perform 4096 further revocations: C is drained from btree_backup and authorize_network(Some(&C)) returns Ok. Same hazard the repo already reasoned about for deny rules — network_guard.rs:204-206 explicitly refuses to evict them. Live blast radius is limited today because main.rs:16005 builds a fresh gate per CLI invocation. Fix: never evict on expiry-bearing revocation entries; drop only once expires_at_epoch_secs has passed.

(3) OPEN — security/cuckoo_filter.rs:190,205. On eviction-chain exhaustion every visited bucket is full, so each mem::swap writes the carried fingerprint into an occupied slot and takes out a live one; when the 500-iteration loop gives up, that carried fingerprint is DROPPED. num_items is never decremented, so nothing signals the loss. CheckMode::Hybrid short-circuits on !cuckoo.contains(token_id) without consulting btree_backup, so a revoked token reports not-revoked — violating the type's own :39 contract 'No false negatives (critical for security)'. Compounded by random_slot() at :212-220: addr_of!(self.buckets) is the Vec HEADER address (fixed for the filter's life) and num_items is not mutated inside the loop, so the victim slot is constant for the whole chain and reduces to num_items % 4 (BUCKET_SIZE=4, 0x9e3779b9 mod 4 == 1, addr 8-byte aligned) — defeating the randomization that lets a cuckoo walk escape cycles. Fix: record the (bucket,slot) path and roll the swaps back on failure; vary the slot per iteration.

Section 13 is the program's "done" definition. Without verified success criteria, the program has no objective completion standard. This gate ensures that each criterion has a measurement mechanism, each quantitative target has a pass/fail threshold, and the overall program can produce a defensible success report.

description:

Avoid simulated generate_expected_decision() logic in the verifier path.

title: [PERF] Threshold signature verification should preparse signer keys and reuse the message buffer
description: Standalone Criterion harness against the live threshold_sig implementation measured verify_threshold at 456.91-459.68 us for 8-of-8 and 1.8751-1.8923 ms for 32-of-32; a preparsed-keys model dropped to 407.59-411.83 us (-10.7%) and 1.6541-1.6665 ms (-11.8%). title: [REVIEW] Threshold signature collection scans unbounded partials
description:
FILE: crates/franken-node/src/supply_chain/artifact_signing.rs:725
PATTERN: unbounded signature-verification loop / test claims bounded iteration without enforcing a cap
WHY IT'S A BUG: collect_threshold_signatures() iterates every supplied partial until it finds the required number of valid signatures. For a known key with many invalid signatures, seen_keys is not marked until a valid signature succeeds, so each invalid partial can trigger Ed25519 verification. The hardening test named bounded_iteration only proves 1000 invalid entries still succeed when valid signatures are at the end; it does not enforce a maximum or fail closed.
SUGGESTED FIX: Add a MAX_PARTIAL_SIGNATURES or per-key attempt cap, reject oversized partial slices before verification, and mark/limit repeated attempts per key so one key cannot force unbounded signature checks. Update the hardening test to assert rejection or capped verification count.
EVIDENCE: git blame shows 46d7ce002 lines 725-739 looping over all partials, b8aa82212 lines 729-733 verifying before inserting into seen_keys, and 2a3d13cf6 lines 2135-2169 naming a bounded-iteration test while placing valid signatures after 1000 invalid entries.
close_reason: Bounded threshold partial input and repeated per-key verification attempts
